issues.title: One alignable entry switches all keys to symbolic names; path keys are silently skipped
issues.description: AlignGeometry() chooses the lookup mode once for all keys from gGeoManager->GetNAlignable() > 0. If the geometry has any alignable entry, every key is treated as a symbolic name, and AlignGeometryBySymlink() skips keys without an entry and logs nothing (lines 70-80). Path keys, the form that README.dox documents, are then not applied and the user is not told. AlignGeometry() also uses gGeoManager without a null check.
issues.fix: Choose the mode per key (symbolic name when GetAlignableEntry() finds one, otherwise full path) and log every key that cannot be resolved.

issues.title: AlignGeometryByFullPath() ignores the result of cd() and crashes on an invalid path
issues.description: AlignGeometryByFullPath() does not check the return value of gGeoManager->cd(volume_path). For a path that does not exist, ROOT only logs an error and the code reads the matrix of the last valid node. MakePhysicalNode() then returns nullptr because CheckPath() fails. pn->Align() at line 56 dereferences the null pointer, so one wrong key crashes the run.
issues.fix: Check the results of cd() and MakePhysicalNode(), log an error that names the key, and skip that key.

issues.title: Symbolic-name alignment passes a global matrix to Align(), which expects a local one
issues.description: AlignGeometryBySymlink() starts from TGeoPhysicalNode::GetMatrix(), which is the global matrix of the node. It multiplies it by the alignment matrix and passes the result to TGeoPhysicalNode::Align(). Align() installs that matrix as the new matrix relative to the mother volume (ROOT computes new global = mother global * newmat). So every aligned volume whose mother is not at the origin with identity rotation moves to a wrong place, even with an identity alignment matrix. AlignGeometryByFullPath() starts from the local TGeoNode matrix, so the two modes give different geometries for the same input.
issues.fix: Start from the local matrix of the last node (node->GetNode()->GetMatrix()), as AlignGeometryByFullPath() does.
issues.evidence: In ROOT, TGeoPhysicalNode::GetMatrix() returns the global matrix: SetBranchAsState fills fMatrices with copies of the navigator's global matrices. Align() calls SetMatrix(newmat) on the node and then sets global = mother global * newmat. FairAlignmentHandler.cxx:77-87 passes global * delta as the new local matrix, while AlignGeometryByFullPath() starts from the local TGeoNode matrix (lines 44-51). So a node whose mother is not at the identity moves, even with an identity delta. This mode is picked automatically when the geometry has any alignable entry (line 16). No shipped example reaches it, because the Tutorial 4 simulation reads tutorial4.root, which has no entries.

issues.title: AddAlignmentMatrices() always logs 'adding inverting matrices...'
issues.description: AddAlignmentMatrices() logs 'adding inverting matrices...' before the loop, also when invertMatrices is false. So the log says the matrices are inverted when they are not.
issues.fix: Log 'adding alignment matrices', and say 'inverted' only when invertMatrices is true.

issues.title: FairFileHeader input-file list is never filled; AddInputFile()/GetFileInfo() are unused
issues.description: No code in FairRoot calls AddInputFile() or GetFileInfo(). So fFileList, documented as the list of input files used to produce the file, is empty in every written file header. SetFileHeader() of FairFileSource (FairFileSource.h:91) and of FairMixedSource (FairMixedSource.h:108) stores a pointer that nothing reads.
issues.fix: Call AddInputFile() when the sources open their input files, or deprecate AddInputFile(), GetFileInfo() and the SetFileHeader() setters of the sources.

issues.title: FairLink::operator< is not a strict weak ordering when file or entry is -1
issues.description: operator<() skips the file and entry comparison when either side is -1. So a link with entry -1 is equivalent to the links with the same type and index from entry 5 and from entry 6, but those two are not equivalent to each other. This breaks the strict weak ordering that std::set<FairLink> in FairMultiLinkedData needs, as soon as one object holds links with the same type and index from several files or entries next to a -1 link (event mixing, time-based data). A standalone copy of operator<() and InsertLink() shows that the set then depends on insertion order: one merged link (weight 3) if the -1 link comes first, two links if it comes last. operator==() is also asymmetric, because the wildcard applies only to its right-hand side.
issues.fix: Compare file and entry as plain values in operator<(), and do wildcard matching only in explicit lookups such as LinkPosInList().

issues.title: FairMCEventHeader::fT comment says [s], but the constructor and GetT() say [ns]
issues.description: The comment of member fT says 'Event time [s]'. The constructor documentation (L38), GetT() (L58), the file header (L11, 'change the event time to ns') and the log of FairFileSource::GetEventTime() all use ns. No FairRoot code calls SetTime(), so users who fill the time depend on this documentation. L37 also has the typo 'oordinates'.
issues.fix: Change the fT comment to 'Event time [ns]' and fix 'oordinates' at L37.

Double32_t fZ;                 ///  Primary vertex z [cm]
Double32_t fT;                 ///  Event time [s]
Double32_t fB;                 ///  Impact parameter [fm] (if relevant)

issues.title: FairMesh::print() prints NXbin as the NY value and never prints NZbin
issues.description: print() writes 'NY' followed by NXbin, so the printed NY value is wrong when NYbin differs from NXbin. It does not print NZbin at all.
issues.fix: Print NYbin after 'NY' and add NZbin to the output.

issues.title: FairMultiLinkedData_Interface::operator=() keeps stale links and forces history on
issues.description: operator=() copies the links only when rhs has a link object. When rhs has none (links off, or no link added yet), *this keeps its old links. It also sets the history flag to kTRUE instead of copying it from rhs, as the copy constructor does (L49). So assignment and copy construction give different objects; FairHit, FairTimeStamp and FairMCPoint use this operator through their implicit assignment.
issues.fix: Reset the link object of *this when rhs has none, and copy the history flag of rhs instead of setting kTRUE.

issues.title: AddInterfaceData() dereferences a null link pointer when FairLinks are off
issues.description: AddInterfaceData() ends with SetInsertHistory(GetPointerToLinks()->GetInsertHistory()). FairLinks are off by default (FairRootManager::fUseFairLinks is kFALSE until FairRun::SetUseFairLinks(kTRUE) is called). In that mode GetPointerToLinks() is null, so this line crashes, while all the other link setters do nothing. When links are on, the line reads back the kFALSE that L178 just set, so history insertion stays off for every later AddLink() on the object (see the comment 'todo add previous history value').
issues.fix: Save the old history flag before L178 when GetPointerToLinks() is not null, and restore it at the end only in that case.
issues.evidence: Links are off by default (FairRootManager.cxx:90). With links off, CreateFairMultiLinkedData() returns nullptr and never creates fLink (FairMultiLinkedData_Interface.cxx:64-75), so line 188 dereferences a null pointer. Every other setter checks for null first. The history claim is also right: line 178 sets the flag to false, and line 188 reads that false back. The only in-tree caller (FairTestDetectorTimeRecoTask.cxx:92) runs from run_reco_timebased.C, which turns links on (line 47), so no shipped macro crashes, but any task that calls this public method in the default setup does.

issues.title: Unreachable null checks on FairRootManager::Instance() in the FairLinks code
issues.description: FairRootManager::Instance() returns the address of a thread_local static (FairRootManager.cxx:66-72), so it is never null. The check 'if (ioman == 0)' in AddLink() and its '-W- no IOManager present!' message never run, and InsertHistory() would dereference a null manager anyway. FairMultiLinkedData_Interface::CreateFairMultiLinkedData() (FairMultiLinkedData_Interface.cxx:66) has the same dead check.
issues.fix: Remove both null checks.

issues.title: InsertHistory() calls InheritsFrom() on a null object for links with index < 0
issues.description: For a link with index < 0, InsertHistory() calls InheritsFrom() on the result of FairRootManager::GetObject() without a null check. GetObject() returns nullptr when the branch is not available, or when the type is unknown (GetBranchName() then returns 'Branch not found'). AddLink() skips the persistence check for such links and always calls InsertHistory() while history is on, so such a link crashes the job. The TClonesArray path (L233) has the check.
issues.fix: Return early when myObject is nullptr, as the TClonesArray path does.

issues.title: FairMultiLinkedData::DeleteLink() does nothing because its body is commented out
issues.description: The body of DeleteLink(Int_t, Int_t) is commented out, so both DeleteLink() overloads do nothing, although the header says that they delete a link (FairMultiLinkedData.h:108-112). FairMCMatch::GetMCInfoForward() (FairMCMatch.cxx:145) calls it to remove the start link. FindStagesPointingToLinks() adds that link when no later stage points to the start object (FairMCMatch.cxx:200-201), so these forward results keep the start object as its own match.
issues.fix: Find the link with std::find(fLinks.begin(), fLinks.end(), FairLink(type, index)) and erase it when the iterator is not end().

issues.title: GetLinksWithType() and GetSortedMCTracks() filter through FairLinkManager and need a run
issues.description: GetLinksWithType(), which GetSortedMCTracks() uses, fills its result with InsertLink(). InsertLink() drops every link whose type the current FairLinkManager ignores, so these getters can return fewer links than the object holds. In include mode (AddIncludeType()), GetSortedMCTracks() is empty unless the MCTrack branch is included, and in the default mode every memory-only branch of the current run is ignored (FairRootManager::RegisterImpl() adds it). Without a FairRun, FairLinkManager::Instance() is null and InsertLink() dereferences it (L187), so these getters crash in a plain ROOT macro.
issues.fix: Insert the matching links into result.fLinks directly instead of through InsertLink(), and make InsertLink() handle a null FairLinkManager::Instance().

issues.title: FairPrintFairLinks casts branch objects to TClonesArray and the link interface unchecked
issues.description: InitBranchList() casts the object of every branch that passes its name filter to TClonesArray* with a C-style cast. Exec() (L101) then casts each element to FairMultiLinkedData_Interface* without a check. The branches MCMatch (a FairMCMatch, which is a TNamed) and MCLink (a TClonesArray of FairMCEntry, which derives from FairMultiLinkedData, not from the interface) pass the filter. Exec() then calls methods on objects of the wrong type, which is undefined behavior and usually a crash.
issues.fix: Use dynamic_cast<TClonesArray*> in InitBranchList(), and skip the elements that do not inherit from FairMultiLinkedData_Interface in Exec().

issues.title: FairPrintFairLinks logs a message with an '-E-' prefix at warning level
issues.description: InitBranchList() logs '-E- FairPrintFairLinks <name> is not a valid branch name!' with LOG(warning). The old '-E-' (error) prefix contradicts the warning level that the logger prints.
issues.fix: Drop the '-E-' prefix from the message.

issues.title: Private Register(), Reset() and ProduceHits() are declared but never defined
issues.description: FairPrintFairLinks declares the private functions Register(), Reset() and ProduceHits() but never defines them. FairMCMatchCreatorTask.h:67-71, FairMCMatchLoaderTask.h:59-63 and FairMCMatchSelectorTask.h:78-82 have the same three declarations. FairMCObject.h:88 declares PosInList(std::pair<int, int>) without a definition.
issues.fix: Remove these declarations.

issues.title: FairRadMapPoint::fVolMass comment says 'radiation length'; it holds the volume mass
issues.description: The comment of fVolMass says 'radiation length'. FairRadMapManager::AddPoint() fills it with fActMass, the volume mass that TGeoVolume::WeightA() gives in kg (FairRadMapManager.cxx:109-114 and 204).
issues.fix: Change the comment to 'mass of the volume [kg]'.

excerpt.code:
Float_t fZmat;       // Z of material
Float_t fDensity;    // density of material
Double_t fVolMass;   // radiation length

Double_t fStep, fDose, fDoseSL;

issues.title: FairRecoEventHeader::SetIdentifier() doc comment says 'Set the run ID for this run'
issues.description: The doc comment of SetIdentifier() is a copy of the SetRunId() comment (L42) and says 'Set the run ID for this run'. The function sets fIdentifier.
issues.fix: Change the comment to 'Set the identifier'.

issues.title: FairRunInfo::CreateAndFillHistograms() crashes when no event called StoreInfo()
issues.description: CreateAndFillHistograms() calls front() and back() on a sorted copy of fTimeDiff (L110-111) without a size check, so an empty vector makes it crash. fTimeDiff stays empty when no event called StoreInfo(). That happens with Geant4 MT, because FairMCApplication::FinishEvent() skips StoreInfo() when IsMT() (FairMCApplication.cxx:687), and in any run that processes no event. The master's FairMCApplication::FinishRun() (FairMCApplication.cxx:364-365) and FairRunAna still call WriteInfo() before the output is written, so SetGenerateRunInfo(kTRUE) crashes such runs. In the same case, EventtimeVsEvent is booked with 0 bins (L103-104). Correction: The 0-bin EventtimeVsEvent (L103-104) does no harm: ROOT's TH1 constructor turns nbins <= 0 into 1 bin and prints a warning. The crash is only at L110-111. Workers do not call WriteInfo(), because their FairRunSim keeps the default fGenerateRunInfo=kFALSE (FairRun.cxx:51), so the crash is on the master.
issues.fix: Return early from WriteInfo() when fTimeDiff is empty, and either collect the per-event data in MT mode or skip WriteInfo() there.
issues.evidence: CreateAndFillHistograms() copies fTimeDiff and reads front() and back() without a size check (FairRunInfo.cxx:106-111). Only StoreInfo() fills fTimeDiff. In Geant4 MT the master never calls StoreInfo() (FairMCApplication.cxx:687), but RunMC() still calls FinishRun() after ProcessRun() (L302-304), and FinishRun() calls WriteInfo() (L364-365) before Write() (L368-369). FairRunAna also calls WriteInfo() before LastFill()/Write() when its loop processes no event (FairRunAna.cxx:298-344, 382-417), and a standalone copy of L106-111 with an empty vector crashes with SIGSEGV at -O0 and -O2.

issues.title: FairField(name, title) ignores the title
issues.description: The constructor FairField(const char* name, const char* title) leaves the title parameter unnamed and calls only TVirtualMagField(name). So GetTitle() stays empty, also with the default title 'FAIR Magnetic Field'.
issues.fix: Call SetTitle(title) in the constructor body.

issues.title: FairField::IsConst()/IsMap() test fType 1/2, but the field classes use 0 = constant
issues.description: IsConst() tests fType == 1 and IsMap() tests fType == 2, as the comment at FairField.h:110 says. But GetType() is documented as 0 = constant, 1 = map, 2 = map sym2, 3 = map sym3 (FairField.h:61), and FairConstField, FairConstPar, the templates' MyConstField and the field creators all use 0 for a constant field. So IsConst() returns kFALSE for FairConstField, and under the documented convention it returns kTRUE for a type-1 map. Nothing in the repository calls these functions.
issues.fix: Make IsConst() test fType == 0 and IsMap() test fType >= 1, and fix the comment at FairField.h:110.

issues.title: FairField.h class comment calls GetBx/GetBy/GetBz pure virtual and offers GetBxyz()
issues.description: The class comment says that a concrete field implements 'the pure virtual methods GetBx, GetBy and GetBz and/or GetBxyz'. None of them is pure virtual: GetBx(), GetBy() and GetBz() log a warning and return 0, and GetBxyz() only logs a warning. Field() and GetFieldValue() call only GetBx(), GetBy() and GetBz(), and no code calls GetBxyz(), so a field that implements only GetBxyz() gives a zero field and a warning on every call.
issues.fix: Say that a field must override GetBx(), GetBy() and GetBz() (or GetFieldValue()), and drop 'pure virtual' and 'GetBxyz' from the comment.

excerpt.code:
**
** Abstract base class for magnetic fields in FAIR
** Concrete field should implement the pure virtual methods
** GetBx, GetBy and GetBz and/or  GetBxyz
**
** Note: Field values should be returned in kG (thanks to Geant3)

issues.title: FairBaseContFact title says 'Factory for parameter containers in libSts'
issues.description: The factory title was copied from another library and names libSts. The factory belongs to the Base library, and FairRuntimeDb::ls() prints this title.
issues.fix: Change the title to 'Factory for parameter containers in libBase'.

issues.title: FairDetector::Initialize() prints 'Define sensitive volume' with std::cout in MT mode
issues.description: In MT mode, Initialize() writes 'Define sensitive volume ' to std::cout for each active detector, on the master and on each worker. The line bypasses FairLogger, so log levels and sinks do not apply. DefineSensitiveVolumes() already logs at info level (L73).
issues.fix: Remove the line, or use LOG(debug) with the detector name.

issues.title: FairDetector::ProcessHits() comment says 'each step'; it runs only in sensitive volumes
issues.description: The comment says that ProcessHits() is called for each step. FairMCApplication::Stepping() calls it only when the current volume is in fVolMap, and fVolMap holds only the sensitive volumes (FairMCApplication.cxx:513-557 and 882-918).
issues.fix: Say that ProcessHits() is called for each step inside a sensitive volume of the detector.

issues.title: FairDetector::Reset() comment says it is called after each event, but nothing calls it
issues.description: Reset() is pure virtual, and its comment says it 'has to be called after each event to reset the containers'. No code in the repository calls FairDetector::Reset(); FairMCApplication::FinishEvent() calls EndOfEvent() instead. A detector that clears its collections only in Reset() keeps the points of all earlier events.
issues.fix: Document that the framework calls EndOfEvent(), not Reset(), or call Reset() from FairMCApplication::FinishEvent().

issues.title: FairDetector::CopyClones() and SaveGeoParams() have no caller
issues.description: No code in the repository calls the virtual hook CopyClones() (L75), so overriding it has no effect. SaveGeoParams() (L105, FairDetector.cxx:123-138) has no caller in the repository either.
issues.fix: Deprecate CopyClones() and SaveGeoParams().

issues.title: FairDoubleHit is not built and not in the dictionary, but stays in the source tree
issues.description: No CMake source list contains FairDoubleHit.cxx (fairroot/base/CMakeLists.txt), so the class is not compiled and its header is not installed. Its LinkDef entry is commented out (fairroot/base/LinkDef.h:18), but Doxygen still documents the class.
issues.fix: Delete FairDoubleHit.h, FairDoubleHit.cxx and the commented-out LinkDef line.

issues.title: FairGenericStack copy constructor leaves the fast-sim indices uninitialized
issues.description: The copy constructor does not initialize fFSMovedIndex, fFSFirstSecondary and fFSNofSecondaries. The other constructors set them to -2, -2 and 0. A CloneStack() built on it, like MyProjStack::CloneStack() in the templates, gives each Geant4 MT worker garbage values, so FairFastSimModel::DoIt() can skip Stepping() (it tests for -2) and read particles at a garbage index. The copy also keeps the master's fDetList but sets fDetIter to null, so a FairStack-like UpdateTrackIndex() calls fDetIter->Reset() on null if the clone is made after SetDetArrayList(). FairStack::CloneStack() uses the default constructor and is not affected.
issues.fix: Initialize the three fast-sim members to -2, -2 and 0 in the copy constructor, and set fDetList to nullptr there.

issues.title: FairGenericStack leaks the old fDetIter in SetDetArrayList() and operator=()
issues.description: SetDetArrayList() replaces fDetIter with a new iterator and does not delete the old one. operator=() sets fDetIter to 0 in the same way. Each repeated call leaks one TIterator, because the destructor deletes only the last one.
issues.fix: Delete the old fDetIter before replacing it, or hold it in a std::unique_ptr.

issues.title: FairGenericStack.h calls the sized constructor a 'Destructor' and has typo 'filltering'
issues.description: The comment 'Destructor with estimated array size' (L38) documents the constructor FairGenericStack(Int_t) (L39). The comment of SetDetArrayList() (L105) has the typo 'filltering'.
issues.fix: Change L38 to 'Constructor with estimated array size' and 'filltering' to 'filtering'.

issues.title: Deprecation warnings in FairGenericVMCConfig say 'DEPRACATED'
issues.description: The warnings in Setup() (L28) and SetupPostInit() (L179) contain the typo 'DEPRACATED'. Every simulation that uses the default FairGenericVMCConfig prints the first one.
issues.fix: Change 'DEPRACATED' to 'DEPRECATED' in both warnings.

issues.title: Deprecation warning points to the YAML config, but no example uses it
issues.description: Setup() and SetupPostInit() call the macro configuration deprecated and send users to examples/common/gconfig/ for the YAML implementation (FairVMCConfig). But FairRunSim::SetMCConfig() still creates FairGenericVMCConfig by default, run_tutorial1.C sets it explicitly (L80-83), and FairVMCConfig appears only in commented-out lines that use the old raw-pointer SetSimulationConfig() (FairMQSimDevice.cxx:60, runMM.C:52, runMC.C:60). So every run prints the warning, and no example shows how to switch.
issues.fix: Port at least one example to SetSimulationConfig(std::make_unique<FairVMCConfig>()) and fix the commented lines, or drop the warning while the macro path is the default.

issues.title: Setup() reads GEANT4VMC_MACRO_DIR, but the generated scripts export Geant4VMC_MACRO_DIR
issues.description: cmake/scripts/config.sh.in:13, config.csh.in:13, set_env.sh.in:10, root_macro.sh.in:18 and run_binary.sh.in:5 export Geant4VMC_MACRO_DIR, and environment variable names are case-sensitive. So Lib_config stays empty, and the fallback at L71-75 looks for g4libs.C in the working directory instead of the Geant4 VMC macro folder. Normal runs still work because g4Config.C creates TGeant4 directly, but the fallback works only if the user exports the upper-case name by hand.
issues.fix: Read Geant4VMC_MACRO_DIR, optionally with the upper-case name as a second choice.

issues.title: FairGenericVMCConfig::Setup() silently accepts an unknown or empty engine name
issues.description: The TGeant4/TGeant3/TFluka if/else chain has no else branch, so a typo or a missing SetName() (empty name) leaves LibMacro and ConfigMacro empty. Setup() still calls LoadMacro() with an empty name and ProcessLine("Config()") (L165-166), then runs SetCuts() (L168-169), and the example SetCuts.C uses the null TVirtualMC (SetCuts.C:28-30). The user sees ROOT errors and a crash, but no message names the bad engine name; FairYamlVMCConfig::Setup() has a LOG(fatal) for this case.
issues.fix: Add an else branch that logs the unknown engine name with LOG(fatal) and returns.

issues.title: SetupPostInit() log prints the macro name with a doubled '.C.C' extension
issues.description: The message at L206 appends ".C" to fPostInitName, which already holds the full file name (default 'g4ConfigPostInit.C', L21 and FairGenericVMCConfig.h:27). When the macro is found in CONFIG_DIR, the log says '(g4ConfigPostInit.C.C)'. FairYamlVMCConfig::SetupPostInit() prints the same message without the extra suffix.
issues.fix: Remove the extra ".C" from the message.

issues.title: FairIon::SetParams() sets the mass to 0 by default, unlike the constructor
issues.description: The constructor documents and applies 'if mass is not given, use A times the proton mass' (FairIon.h:40, FairIon.cxx:38-42). SetParams() has the same parameters and the same default m = 0, but it stores fMass = 0. An ion set up with SetParams() reports GetMass() == 0, and FairMCApplication::AddIons() passes 0 to DefineIon(). FairRoot itself never calls SetParams().
issues.fix: Apply the constructor's A-times-proton-mass rule in SetParams() when m == 0.

issues.title: FairIon declares a static fgNIon that is never defined or used
issues.description: FairIon.h declares static Int_t fgNIon ('Number of ions instantiated'), but FairIon.cxx neither defines nor uses it. The counter that the generators use is FairIonGenerator::fgNIon.
issues.fix: Delete the declaration.

excerpt.code:
private:
  static Int_t fgNIon;   //! /// Number of ions instantiated. One per generator.
  Int_t fZ;              /// Atomic number
  Int_t fA;              /// Atomic mass

issues.title: Global 'std::mutex mtx' in FairMCApplication.cxx has external linkage
issues.description: The mutex is a non-static, namespace-scope variable with a very generic name. FairRoot builds with default symbol visibility, so the FairRoot::Base library exports the symbol 'mtx'. Another global 'mtx' in a user library or executable can clash with it at link time or interpose it at run time.
issues.fix: Make it static or move it into an anonymous namespace.

issues.title: InitMC() dereferences a null fMC after LOG(fatal) 'No MC engine defined'
issues.description: LOG(fatal) stops the program only after FairLogger::GetLogger() installs its fatal handler (fairroot/tools/FairLogger.cxx:37), and no code in fairroot/ calls it; FairLogger itself only prints the line. When the config macro creates no engine, for example with a wrong engine name or an unset VMCWORKDIR, InitMC() logs the fatal line and then calls fMC->GetStack() on a null pointer. The user gets a segmentation fault instead of a clean stop.
issues.fix: Return or throw right after the LOG(fatal), and do the same after 'No Stack defined.' at L261.

issues.title: FairMCApplication log messages say 'FairMCMCApplication' and 'safetly'
issues.description: The debug messages at L313, L380 and L638 name the class 'FairMCMCApplication'. The warning at L621, 'StopRun() exiting not safetly oopps !!!@@@!!!', has a typo and does not tell the user what happened. The comments at L506 ('nay') and L509 ('alredy') have typos too.
issues.fix: Write 'FairMCApplication' in the messages and replace the L621 text with a clear one, such as 'Generator returned no event, stopping the run'.

issues.title: FinishRun() calls GetTotPrimary() through a null generator on Geant4 MT workers
issues.description: On a worker, fRun is the FairRunSim made in CloneForWorker(), which has no generator, so GetPrimaryGenerator() returns nullptr. FinishRunOnWorker() calls FinishRun(), which calls gen->GetTotPrimary() through this null pointer (undefined behavior). It works today only because GetTotPrimary() reads the static fTotPrim, which all worker generators also update in GenerateEvent() (FairPrimaryGenerator.cxx:269) without synchronization, a data race.
issues.fix: Use fEvGen with a null check, read the count only inside the fRadGridMan branch, and make fTotPrim atomic or per instance.

issues.title: FinishRun() never writes the output tree when the radiation grid manager is on
issues.description: FinishRun() calls fRootManager->Write() only under if (!fRadGridMan && fRootManager). With SetRadGridRegister(kTRUE) and AddMesh(), as in run_tutorial1_mesh.C, no other code writes the tree: FairRunSim::Run() only closes the sink, and FairRootFileSink::Close() only calls TFile::Close(), which does not write objects that are in memory. The main output file of such a run has no event tree (unless a TTree AutoSave happened). The mesh test only checks for 'Macro finished successfully', so CI does not see this.
issues.fix: Call fRootManager->Write() whenever fRootManager is set, independent of fRadGridMan.
issues.evidence: FinishRun() calls fRootManager->Write() only when fRadGridMan is null (FairMCApplication.cxx:368-370). SetRadGridRegister(kTRUE) always creates fRadGridMan (FairRunSim.cxx:227-229, FairMCApplication.cxx:1256-1262). After that, FairRunSim::Run() only closes the sink (FairRunSim.cxx:322-329), and FairRootFileSink::Close() only calls TFile::Close() (FairRootFileSink.cxx:203-208). The only WriteTObject(fOutTree) is in FairRootFileSink::Write() (L311-333), TFile::Close() deletes the in-memory TTree without writing it, and the default AutoSave threshold is 300 MB, so a normal grid run has no event tree. The mesh test only checks the final message (Tutorial1/macros/CMakeLists.txt:18-23).

issues.title: CloneForWorker() does not pass the FairLinks flag to the worker's FairRootManager
issues.description: SetUseFairLinks() stores the flag in the FairRootManager instance, which is thread_local (FairRootManager.cxx:70; FairRun.cxx:81 takes it). CloneForWorker() runs on the Geant4 worker thread and copies the engine name, sink, header, run ID and trajectory flag, but not this flag. On workers, CreateFairMultiLinkedData() then sees GetUseFairLinks() == false, so FairStack::UpdateTrackIndex() adds no MCTrack links to the MC points, although the macro turned links on.
issues.fix: Copy the flag in CloneForWorker(), for example workerRun->SetUseFairLinks(fRootManager->GetUseFairLinks()).

issues.title: A Geant4 MT run without a sink crashes in CloneForWorker()
issues.description: FairRootManager and FairRunSim::Run() treat the sink as optional and check it for null. CloneForWorker() calls fRun->GetSink()->CloneSink() without a check, so a multithreaded run without SetSink() dereferences a null pointer on each worker thread. FinishEvent() has the same unchecked call at L640 (fRun->GetSink()->GetSinkType()), which runs only in MT mode.
issues.fix: Check GetSink() for null in CloneForWorker() and FinishEvent(), or stop with a clear LOG(fatal) in Init() when MT mode has no sink.

issues.title: CloneForWorker() slices a user-derived FairMCEventHeader to the base class
issues.description: CloneForWorker() copies the header with new FairMCEventHeader(*(fRun->GetMCEventHeader())). When the run uses a subclass set with SetMCEventHeader() (like FairMCSplitEventHeader in examples/MQ/pixelSimSplit), each Geant4 MT worker gets a plain FairMCEventHeader. The worker output loses the extra fields and any Register() override of the subclass.
issues.fix: Copy the header polymorphically, for example with a virtual clone method or TObject::Clone().

issues.title: Stepping() dereferences fModVolMap.end() for a volume that no module created
issues.description: With the radiation length or radiation map manager on, Stepping() looks up the current volume ID in fModVolMap and uses modvoliter->second without checking for end(). ConstructGeometry() (L764-773) fills the map only with the volumes that GetListOfVolumes() gains while a module builds its geometry. A step in any other volume, for example one added by CloseGeometry() or a runtime shape, reads an invalid iterator and passes a meaningless module ID to AddPoint().
issues.fix: Check modvoliter against end() and skip the point, or use a fallback module ID, when the volume is unknown.

issues.title: StopRun() calls exit(0) inside the MC event loop when a generator runs out of events
issues.description: GeneratePrimaries() (L990-991) calls StopRun() when GenerateEvent() fails, for example when FairAsciiGenerator or FairUrqmdGenerator reaches the end of its input file before nEvents. StopRun() runs FinishEvent() for an event that was never transported, so the sink fills one extra entry, and it writes the tree twice (in FinishRun() and again at L618-620). Then it calls exit(0) inside the engine's event loop (in Geant4 MT mode, from a worker thread). The macro code after Run() never runs (for example CreateGeometryFile() in run_tutorial1_urqmd.C), stack objects are not destroyed, and the exit status still reports success. Correction: FairAsciiGenerator first takes the LOG(fatal) branch at end of file (FairAsciiGenerator.cxx:60-62), because '>> ntracks' fails at EOF. It reaches StopRun() only when no fatal handler is set. With FairLogger::GetLogger() it throws instead. File generators cannot be cloned for MT (FairGenerator.cxx:40-42), so the exit(0) from a worker thread needs a user generator that supports cloning.
issues.fix: Stop through StopMCRun() (fMC->StopRun()) instead of exit(0), skip FinishEvent() for the failed event, and let RunMC() call FinishRun() once.
issues.evidence: GeneratePrimaries() calls StopRun() when GenerateEvent() fails (FairMCApplication.cxx:988-992). StopRun() then runs FinishEvent(), which fills the tree for the event that was not transported (L661-662), runs FinishRun(), which writes the tree (L368-369), writes it again (L618-620) and calls exit(0) (L622). TGeant3::ProcessEvent and TG4PrimaryGeneratorAction call GeneratePrimaries() after BeginEvent(), inside the event loop, so RunMC(), FairRunSim::Run() and all macro code after Run() are skipped. FairUrqmdGenerator returns kFALSE at end of file (FairUrqmdGenerator.cxx:113-118), and the shipped urqmd.ftn14 has 5 events, so run_tutorial1_urqmd.C with nEvents > 5 never reaches CreateGeometryFile() (L101-102) but still exits with status 0.

issues.title: Geant4 MT workers stay in kPreInit, so InitGeometry() logs FATAL on every worker
issues.description: The worker copy constructor (L132-204) does not set fState, so every clone from CloneForWorker() keeps the default kPreInit (FairMCApplication.h:329). Geant4 VMC calls InitGeometry() on each worker thread (TG4SDConstruction::Construct()), and InitGeometry() then logs 'InitGeometry possible in kInit state only' with LOG(fatal). Without a fatal handler, each worker only prints this false FATAL line. If the macro called FairLogger::GetLogger() or gLogger, each worker throws fair::FatalException during its initialization and the process aborts.
issues.fix: Set fState to kInit in the worker copy constructor, or skip the state check when fParent is set.
issues.evidence: The worker copy constructor (FairMCApplication.cxx:132-204) does not set fState, so each clone starts in kPreInit (FairMCApplication.h:329). Only ConstructGeometry() sets kInit (L823), and Geant4 VMC calls it on the master only. On each worker, G4MTRunManagerKernel::StartThread calls Build() first (CloneForWorker and InitOnWorker), then wrm->Initialize(), which runs ConstructSDandField() and TG4SDConstruction::Construct(). That function calls InitGeometry() on the thread-local application on every thread, so the check at L837-838 logs FATAL on each worker. fairlogger has no default fatal callback, but the FairLogger constructor installs one that throws fair::FatalException (FairLogger.cxx:37, 179-201), so run_rutherford.C, which calls FairLogger::GetLogger() (L56) and defaults to TGeant4 with isMT=true (L20), aborts in Init(). Its CTest runs with isMT=false (rutherford/macros/CMakeLists.txt:16).

issues.title: Geant4 MT: GeoTracks is registered after the worker tree exists, so trajectories are lost
issues.description: On a Geant4 MT worker, InitOnWorker() calls InitFinalizer() and WriteFolder() (L473, L939), and the TTree constructor makes branches only for the objects already in the output folder. Geant4 VMC calls InitGeometry() on the worker later: TG4ActionInitialization::Build() runs before the worker run manager's Initialize(). So the FairTrajFilter and its persistent GeoTracks branch (L857-862) are registered too late and never reach the worker files, even though CloneForWorker() copies SetStoreTraj(). The workers still build TGeoTracks for every event and drop them in FinishEvent(), and their filters keep the default cuts, because FairTrajFilter::Instance() in the macro returns the master's thread-local filter.
issues.fix: Create and register the worker's FairTrajFilter in InitOnWorker() before InitFinalizer(), and copy the cuts from the master's filter.

issues.title: UndoGeometryModifications() comments misdescribe the restored matrix and the misalignment
issues.description: L1299 calls node->GetOriginalMatrix() the 'real global matrix, what survey sees'. ROOT stores the original local matrix of the last node there, and Align() expects a local matrix, so the code is right and the comment is wrong. L1276-1277 say the misalignment comes from 'MisalignGeometry methods of the several FairModuls', but FairModule has no such method; FairMCApplication::MisalignGeometry() calls FairRun::AlignGeometry() (FairAlignmentHandler).
issues.fix: Reword both comments: the loop restores the original local matrices, and the misalignment comes from FairAlignmentHandler.

issues.title: Comment on fMcVersion gives the wrong engine numbers
issues.description: The comment says '1= Geant3, 2 = Geant4'. InitMC() sets 0 for TGeant3 and TGeant3TGeo, 1 for TGeant4, 2 for TFluka and 3 for any other engine (FairMCApplication.cxx:270-278), and Stepping() uses 2 for the Fluka workaround (L499).
issues.fix: Change the comment to '-1 = not set, 0 = Geant3, 1 = Geant4, 2 = Fluka, 3 = other'.

issues.title: SetGeometryFileName() ignores its geoVer argument, so GetGeometryFileVer() never changes
issues.description: FairModule.h:62 declares SetGeometryFileName(TString fname, TString geoVer = "0"), but the definition leaves the second parameter unnamed and unused. No other code sets fgeoVer, so GetGeometryFileVer() always returns 'Not defined'.
issues.fix: Store the argument in fgeoVer, or remove the parameter and GetGeometryFileVer().

issues.title: SetGeometryFileName() fatal message says 'absolut path'
issues.description: For a missing absolute geometry file, SetGeometryFileName() logs 'geometry file <name> not found in absolut path!' (L180). 'absolut' is a misspelling of 'absolute'.
issues.fix: Change the text to 'not found at absolute path'.

issues.title: SetGeometryFileName() clears fgeoName for a missing absolute path, then overwrites it
issues.description: For an absolute path that does not exist, the function logs LOG(fatal) and sets fgeoName = "" (L181). L183 then sets fgeoName = fname and logs 'using geometry file', so the assignment at L181 has no effect. Without a fatal handler, the run continues with the missing file name.
issues.fix: Return right after the error, or put L183-185 in an else branch.

issues.title: ProcessNodes() stores the node's own MC id as the mother id
issues.description: Inside if (motherNode), ProcessNodes() calls addedVol->setMotherId(node->getMCid()), while the next line uses motherNode->getCopyNo(). The MC ids are also set only later, in FairDetector::Initialize(), so the stored value is a default. FairVolume::getMotherId() has no callers, so nothing reads the wrong value today.
issues.fix: Use motherNode->getMCid() once the MC ids are known, or remove the unused mother-id field.

issues.title: ConstructGDMLGeometry() error says 'magnet' for every module when ROOT lacks GDML
issues.description: Without ROOT_HAS_GDML, ConstructGDMLGeometry() logs 'Could not construct magnet geometry from gdml file.' for any module that calls it, then LOG(fatal). The text names a magnet even for a detector and does not name the module. In the GDML build, FairModule.h:86 and FairModule.cxx:439 mark posrot as __attribute__((unused)), although L451 uses it.
issues.fix: Log the module name and the file name instead of 'magnet', and drop the unused attribute where posrot is used.

issues.title: FairModule::BeginWorkerRun(), FinishWorkerRun() and ModifyGeometry() are never called
issues.description: The header documents BeginWorkerRun() and FinishWorkerRun() as hooks 'used in MT mode only', but no FairRoot code calls them: FairMCApplication does not override BeginRunOnWorker(), and FinishRunOnWorker() does not call them. The deprecated virtual ModifyGeometry() has no caller either. A user override of any of these methods silently never runs, and the deprecation warning inside ModifyGeometry() never appears.
issues.fix: Call the worker hooks from FairMCApplication::BeginRunOnWorker() and FinishRunOnWorker(), and remove ModifyGeometry() or call it once so its warning shows.

issues.title: ConstructASCIIGeometry() with the default empty container name registers no volumes
issues.description: ConstructASCIIGeometry<T,U>(TString containerName = "") builds the volumes, but it calls ProcessNodes() only inside if ("" != containerName). With the default argument, no FairVolume and no sensitive volume are registered, so an active detector never gets ProcessHits() calls. The function logs nothing in this case.
issues.fix: Always call ProcessNodes() and fill the parameter container only when a name is given, or make the name a required argument.

issues.title: ConstructASCIIGeometry() dereferences a null container when the name is unknown
issues.description: rtdb->getContainer(containerName) returns nullptr when no container factory knows the name (FairRuntimeDb.cxx:214-217). ConstructASCIIGeometry() then calls par->GetGeoSensitiveNodes() without a check. A typo in the container name, or a missing container factory, crashes the run right after the 'Container ... not created!' error.
issues.fix: Check par for null and stop with a LOG(fatal) that names the container and the module.

issues.title: FairParticle 7-argument constructor uses an old, non-standard PDG code for nuclei
issues.description: The 7-argument constructor sets fpdg = 10000000 + 10000*z + 10*a. The 8-argument constructor (L59) and FairMCApplication::GetIonPdg() (FairMCApplication.cxx:1270) use the standard 1000000000 + 10000*z + 10*a. So the same nucleus gets two different codes, and a particle made with this constructor does not match the TDatabasePDG nuclei (for example 1000020040 for the alpha) or the codes that generators produce.
issues.fix: Use 1000000000 + 10000*z + 10*a, or delegate to the 8-argument constructor with s = 0.

excerpt.code:
Double_t decaytime)
: TObject()
, fpdg(10000000 + 10000 * z + 10 * a)
, fParticle(0)
, fMother(0)

issues.title: Clone of FairPrimaryGenerator reads past fTargetZ after SetMultTarget()
issues.description: The copy constructor allocates fTargetZ with one element and copies only fTargetZ[0] (L144), but it copies fNrTargets (L126). ClonePrimaryGenerator() uses it to make the generator of each Geant4 MT worker (FairMCApplication::CloneForWorker()). After SetMultTarget() with more than one target, MakeVertex() on a worker reads fTargetZ[Target] past the end of the array (L475-476). The workers get vertex z values from unrelated heap memory or crash. Correction: The main effect is a wrong vertex z for about (n-1)/n of the events. A crash is unlikely with only a few targets, because the read stays near the 8-byte block. The protected operator= (L200, L218) has the same one-element allocation and also leaks the old array, so the fix should cover it too.
issues.fix: Allocate rhs.fNrTargets elements and copy all target positions in the copy constructor, for example by storing the targets in a std::vector<Double_t>.
issues.evidence: The copy constructor allocates one element (FairPrimaryGenerator.cxx:125) and copies only fTargetZ[0] (L144), but it copies fNrTargets (L126). The worker FairMCApplication copy constructor clones the generator (FairMCApplication.cxx:196-197, called from CloneForWorker at L448). In Geant4 MT the workers generate all events (GeneratePrimaries, L990), so MakeVertex() reads fTargetZ[Target] with Target up to fNrTargets-1 (L475-476). An AddressSanitizer test of the same pattern reports a heap-buffer-overflow read.

    , fPhi(rhs.fPhi)
    , fTargetZ(new Double_t[1])
    , fNrTargets(rhs.fNrTargets)
    , fTargetDz(rhs.fTargetDz)
    , fVertex(rhs.fVertex)
    , fNTracks(rhs.fNTracks)
    , fSmearVertexZ(rhs.fSmearVertexZ)
    , fSmearGausVertexZ(rhs.fSmearGausVertexZ)
    , fSmearVertexXY(rhs.fSmearVertexXY)
    , fSmearGausVertexXY(rhs.fSmearGausVertexXY)
    , fBeamAngle(rhs.fBeamAngle)
    , fEventPlane(rhs.fEventPlane)
    , fStack(nullptr)
    , fGenList(new TObjArray())
    , fListIter(fGenList->MakeIterator())
    , fEvent(nullptr)
    , fdoTracking(rhs.fdoTracking)
    , fMCIndexOffset(rhs.fMCIndexOffset)
    , fEventNr(rhs.fEventNr)
{
    fTargetZ[0] = rhs.fTargetZ[0];
    fGenList->SetName("fGenList");

issues.title: FairPrimaryGenerator::Init() ignores the result of each generator's Init()
issues.description: Init() calls gen->Init() for every generator, drops the result and always returns kTRUE; FairMCApplication::InitFinalizer() (FairMCApplication.cxx:926-942) also ignores the result of fEvGen->Init(). A generator that fails to initialize still runs in every event. FairBaseMCGenerator::Init() returns kFALSE without a message when the multiplicity is <= 0, which is the default of FairYPtGenerator and of the FairBoxGenerator default constructor; such a generator skips its own checks and silently adds no particles.
issues.fix: Return kFALSE (or log a fatal error) when a generator's Init() fails, and check the result in FairMCApplication::InitFinalizer().

issues.title: FairPrimaryGenerator::operator= leaks memory and keeps a 1-element fTargetZ
issues.description: operator= allocates a new fTargetZ (L200) and a new fGenList and fListIter (L212-213) without deleting the old ones, so the old array, the old list and its generators leak. Like the copy constructor, it copies fNrTargets but only fTargetZ[0], and it leaves the generator list empty. The operator is protected and nothing in the repository calls it, so only derived classes can hit this.
issues.fix: Free the old members (or use std::vector and std::unique_ptr) and copy all target positions, or delete the operator.

issues.title: Static fTotPrim is updated without synchronization by all MT worker generators
issues.description: GenerateEvent() does 'fTotPrim += fNTracks' on a static, non-atomic Int_t (FairPrimaryGenerator.h:240). In Geant4 MT mode every worker has its own generator clone, and all of them update this shared counter from different threads. This is a data race, so GetTotPrimary() can undercount. FairRoot reads the value only to scale the radiation-grid histograms in FinishRun(), and the worker applications have no radiation-grid manager.
issues.fix: Make fTotPrim a std::atomic<Int_t>, or sum per-worker counts at the end of the run.

issues.title: AddTrack() reports unknown PDG codes via cout/cerr with blink codes and a typo
issues.description: For a PDG code that is not in TDatabasePDG, AddTrack() writes its error and warning lines with std::cerr/std::cout and ANSI blink and color escape codes instead of FairLogger. These lines ignore the log level and log file settings and put raw escape codes into log files. The warning also says 'savely' instead of 'safely' (L354).
issues.fix: Use LOG(error) and LOG(warn) without escape codes and correct the spelling.

issues.title: Ts'o gen_uuid.c code under the GNU Library GPL is not listed in COPYRIGHT
issues.description: FairRunIdGenerator.cxx contains code from gen_uuid.c and uuid.h, copyright Theodore Ts'o, which 'may be redistributed under the terms of the GNU Library General Public License' (L8-17, L42-51, L297-306, L340-349). COPYRIGHT lists only GSI code under LGPL-3.0-only ('Files: *') and Catch2 under BSL-1.0, so this third-party copyright and license are missing from the project metadata.
issues.fix: Add a Files: stanza for fairroot/base/sim/FairRunIdGenerator.cxx with the Ts'o copyright and its license to COPYRIGHT.

issues.title: uuid_generate() comment says it uses random UUIDs, but that code is commented out
issues.description: The comment above uuid_generate() says it uses uuid_generate_random() when /dev/urandom is available. That branch is commented out (L287-293), and the function always calls uuid_generate_time().
issues.fix: Update the comment to say that uuid_generate() always makes a time-based UUID.

issues.title: Default run ID is the Unix time in seconds, so concurrent jobs get the same ID
issues.description: generateId() builds a UUID, throws it away and returns getTID(), which is fTimeSpec.tv_sec, the current time in seconds set by get_clock() (L232). FairRunSim, FairRunAna, FairRunAnaProof, FairRunOnline and ParameterMQServer use it as the 'unique' run ID when none is set. Jobs that start in the same second, for example a batch job array, get the same run ID, so their outputs and parameter versions cannot be told apart by run ID.
issues.fix: Derive the ID from the UUID (the commented-out XOR fold) or add process-specific bits, or document that parallel jobs must call SetRunId().

issues.title: Output sink constructor reports 'Error opening the Input file'
issues.description: FairRootFileSink(TFile*, const char*) logs the fatal error 'Error opening the Input file' when the file is null or a zombie. The file is the output file, so the message points the user to the wrong file.
issues.fix: Change the text to 'Error opening the output file' and add the file name when there is one.

issues.title: Persistent Register() before InitSink() dereferences a null fOutFolder
issues.description: RegisterImpl() calls fOutFolder->FindObjectAny() without a check, and only InitSink() creates fOutFolder. FairRunAna::Init() calls InitSource() before InitSink() (FairRunAna.cxx:142-143), while FairRunOnline::Init() uses the opposite order. So a source whose Init() registers a persistent branch under FairRunAna, or any Register(..., kTRUE) before Init(), ends in a segmentation fault instead of an error message.
issues.fix: Check fOutFolder in RegisterImpl() and fail with a clear message, or initialize the sink before the source in FairRunAna::Init() as FairRunOnline::Init() does.

issues.title: RegisterAny() says the branch 'will not be registered' but still stores it
issues.description: After CreatePersistentBranchesAny() has run, RegisterAny() warns that the branch will not be registered, but it has no return and still inserts the branch into fPersistentBranchesMap. Each run class calls WriteFolder() only once, so the entry is never used and the warning is true in practice. The code contradicts its own message.
issues.fix: Return right after the warning.

issues.title: WriteFolder() ignores a failed CreatePersistentBranchesAny() and later branches are lost
issues.description: CreatePersistentBranchesAny() walks fPersistentBranchesMap in branch-name order. It returns false at the first type without a TClass or dictionary (L271-279), right after LOG(fatal). WriteFolder() ignores this result (L247), and fPersistentBranchesDone stays false. LOG(fatal) does not stop the program by default, so the run goes on and writes a tree that lacks the bad branch and every RegisterAny() branch whose name sorts after it, even when their dictionaries are fine.
issues.fix: Skip only the bad entry in the loop instead of returning, and let WriteFolder() stop the run, for example with an exception, when a branch could not be created.

issues.title: Write() double-deletes the output TFile after ROOT switches to a new file
issues.description: When the output tree grows past TTree::GetMaxTreeSize() (100 GB by default, lower after TTree::SetMaxTreeSize()), TTree::Fill() calls TTree::ChangeFile(), which deletes the old TFile ('delete file' in ROOT 6.18, 'file->TObject::Delete()' in 6.30). fRootFile is a std::unique_ptr that still owns that deleted file. At the end of the run Write() calls fRootFile.reset(newFile), and the unique_ptr deletes the old file a second time. The comment at L315-319 shows the file split is meant to be supported.
issues.fix: Call fRootFile.release() before fRootFile.reset(fOutTree->GetCurrentFile()), because ROOT has already deleted the old file.
issues.evidence: fRootFile is a std::unique_ptr<TFile> (FairRootFileSink.h:77). The output tree is created in the top directory of that file (FairRootFileSink.cxx:240-245), which is the condition TTree::Fill() checks before it calls ChangeFile() past fgMaxTreeSize (100000000000LL by default). ChangeFile() deletes the old file: ROOT v6-18-00 TTree.cxx:2721 has 'delete file', and v6-30-00 TTree.cxx:2839 has 'file->TObject::Delete()', which runs 'delete this' (TObject.cxx:255). Write() then calls fRootFile.reset(newFile) at L323-324, which deletes the freed TFile a second time. This crashes before WriteTObject(fOutTree) at L328, so the last file part also loses its tree.

issues.title: License header says 'Licence version 3 (LGPL) version 3' in 14 files
issues.description: FairSink.h/.cxx and FairRootFileSink.h/.cxx, plus 10 files in examples/MQ/pixelDetector and examples/MQ/pixelSimSplit, have the header line 'GNU Lesser General Public Licence version 3 (LGPL) version 3'. The standard GSI header says 'GNU Lesser General Public Licence (LGPL) version 3'.
issues.fix: Replace the line with the standard header text in all 14 files.

issues.title: UInt_t identifier constructor parameter of the file sources is ignored
issues.description: All three FairFileSource constructors (L48, L81, L114) and all three FairMixedSource constructors (FairMixedSource.cxx:37, 84, 130) take a UInt_t identifier, leave it unnamed and ignore it. fSourceIdentifier is always 0 and nothing reads it. A caller that passes an identifier gets no effect and no warning.
issues.fix: Remove or deprecate the parameter and the unused fSourceIdentifier member.

excerpt.code:
using fairroot::detail::non_owning;

FairFileSource::FairFileSource(TFile* f, const char* Title, UInt_t)
    : FairFileSourceBase(maybe_owning_ptr<TFile>{f, non_owning})
    , fInputTitle(Title)

issues.title: IsInitialized is never set to kTRUE, so the 'already initialized' guard is dead
issues.description: FairFileSource::Init() and FairMixedSource::Init() (FairMixedSource.cxx:195) return early when IsInitialized is true, but the code only ever sets it to kFALSE (FairFileSource.cxx L62, L95, L128, L286). A second Init() call would add the input file to the chain again; FairMixedSource::Init() also allocates fOutHeader before the check. The run classes call Init() once, so this is latent.
issues.fix: Set IsInitialized = kTRUE at the end of a successful Init(), or remove the guard.

issues.title: FairFileSource::ReadEvent() treats an I/O error (-1) from GetEntry() as success
issues.description: ReadEvent() returns 0 whenever fInChain->GetEntry(i) is non-zero. TTree::GetEntry() returns -1 on an I/O error, and TChain::GetEntry() passes it through. So a read error does not stop the event loop: the tasks run on a partly read event and its output is stored. SpecifyRunId() (L303) has the same pattern.
issues.fix: Treat only a positive byte count as success and return an error code for 0 and for -1.

issues.title: Friend-file open error prints the input level name instead of the file name
issues.description: In AddFriendsToChain(), the fatal message for a friend file that cannot be opened prints level.Data(), an input level name such as 'InputRootFile' or 'FriendTree_1', instead of fileName. The user does not learn which file failed.
issues.fix: Print fileName.Data() in the message.

issues.title: AddFriendsToChain() puts friend files into the wrong chain (continue, not break)
issues.description: The loop over fInputLevel (L349-366) uses continue after a branch-list match, so inputLevel always ends as the last level. When friend files of two types are added interleaved (for example per run: A1, B1, A2), A2 goes into the chain of type B (L373-374), and the friend chains no longer line up with the main chain. A friend with the same branch list as the main input, added before any friend chain exists, maps to the main input title; fFriendTypeList[] then returns a null TChain* and chain->AddFile() crashes. Correction: Adding a friend with the main-input layout is close to misuse, but it should give a clear error, not a null dereference. The main impact is the interleaved case, which is a normal way to call the documented AddFriend() API (for example, in a loop over runs).
issues.fix: Break out of the level loop on the first match, look the chain up with find(), and stop with a clear error when a friend matches the main input.
issues.evidence: The continue at FairFileSource.cxx:364 is the last statement in the loop body, so the loop over fInputLevel (L349-366) always runs to the end and leaves inputLevel at the last level, not at the level that matched. A copy of the loop puts friends added as A1 B1 A2 B2 into FriendTree_1={A1} and FriendTree_2={B1,A2,B2}. The call to CheckFriendChains() is commented out (L379), so nothing catches the mismatch. If the first friend has the main-input layout, inputLevel becomes fInputTitle, fFriendTypeList[inputLevel] (L373) inserts a null TChain*, and chain->AddFile() at L374 dereferences null.

issues.title: Friend chains are never checked: the CheckFriendChains() call is commented out
issues.description: The comment of AddFriendsToChain() says the run IDs and event counts of all friend chains are checked against the main chain, but the call to CheckFriendChains() is commented out. The GetRunIdInfo() calls that would fill fRunIdInfoAll are commented out too, and CheckFriendChains() looks up a level named 'InputChain' that is never created, so re-enabling the call as is would dereference end(). Mismatched friend files are not detected.
issues.fix: Fill fRunIdInfoAll and re-enable a working check, or remove CheckFriendChains() and the comment that promises it.

issues.title: CreateNewFriendChain() has an unreachable exit(-1) and a different folder order
issues.description: CreateNewFriendChain() looks for the folder in the order GetFolderName(), cbmout, cbmroot, while Init() uses GetFolderName(), cbmroot, cbmout (L164-175). The exit(-1) after LOG(fatal) never runs, because FairLogger throws on a fatal message. Neither point changes results for normal files.
issues.fix: Share one folder lookup helper between Init() and CreateNewFriendChain() and drop the exit(-1).

issues.title: FairFileSource::CheckMaxEventNo() returns the requested end without capping it
issues.description: CheckMaxEventNo(EvtEnd) returns EvtEnd unchanged when it is not 0, so it never compares it with the number of entries. FairRunAna::Run(a, b) and FairRunOnline::Run() therefore never apply their cap or print 'File has less events than requested' for this source. The FairRunAna loop still stops at the end of the input, but only because ReadEvent() returns 1, with the less clear warning 'ReadEvent(i) returned 1. Breaking the event loop'.
issues.fix: Return min(EvtEnd, fInChain->GetEntries()) when EvtEnd is not 0, so the cap and warning in the run classes work.

issues.title: FairFileSource stores the MC event ID, not the entry number, as MCEntryNumber
issues.description: FillEventHeader() sets the MC entry number from fMCHeader->GetEventID(), and FairPrimaryGenerator numbers events from 1. FairEventHeader.h documents the field as 'The entry number in the original MC chain', and FairMixedSource fills it with the 0-based entry. FairFileSource::ReadBranchEvent(const char*) uses the value as an entry index (L674, L679) and would read the next entry; it is reachable only through FairRootManager::ReadBranchEvent(const char*), which nothing in the repository calls.
issues.fix: Store the chain entry (fCurrentEntryNo) in the MC entry number, or document that the field holds the MC event ID.

issues.title: Input-file bookkeeping is dead: SetFileHeader() and AddInputFile() are unused
issues.description: SetFileHeader() of FairFileSource and FairMixedSource (FairMixedSource.h:108) stores fFileHeader, but nothing calls the setters and no code reads the member. FairFileHeader::AddInputFile() has no callers, so the input-file list of the written FileHeader is always empty. The comment at FairFileHeader.h:64 says the list holds TObjStrings, but AddInputFile() adds FairFileInfo objects.
issues.fix: Record the input files in FairFileHeader from the sources, or remove these members and correct the comment.

issues.title: FairMixedSource(file, signalId != 0) also reads the signal file as background
issues.description: The constructor passes its file to FairFileSourceBase as fRootFile (L131) and, for signalId != 0, also adds it as a signal file (L175). Init() always adds fRootFile to the background chain (L204). Unless SetBackgroundFile() replaces fRootFile first, the signal file is silently read as the background too.
issues.fix: Fail in Init() when no background file was set, or do not add fRootFile to the background chain when it came from a signal file.
