issues.title: SpecifyRunId() fatal text has typos and names non-existent UseRunIdFromSG()
issues.description: The message reads 'Please specify where to take the from: Signal or Bcckgrand by calling UseRunIdFromBG or UseRunIdFromSG'. It misses the words 'run ID', misspells 'background', and names UseRunIdFromSG(), but the method is UseRunIdfromSG() with a lowercase f. The comment in create_digis_mixed.C:42-43 repeats the wrong name.
issues.fix: Correct the text and the method name, or add a UseRunIdFromSG() alias so the consistent spelling works.

issues.title: SpecifyRunId() calls fBackgroundChain->Dump(), a leftover debug dump
issues.description: When the run ID comes from the background (UseRunIdFromBG()), SpecifyRunId() calls fBackgroundChain->Dump(). This prints every data member of the TChain object to stdout during FairRunAna::Init(). It is leftover debug code.
issues.fix: Remove the Dump() call or replace it with a LOG(debug) line.

issues.title: Mixed source adds two time steps per event, so the mean event spacing doubles
issues.description: ReadEvent() calls SetEventTime() at the start (L349), and SetEventTime() (L662-675) has no per-entry guard, unlike FairFileSource::SetEventTime(). After fCurrentEntryNo changes at L383, GetEventTime() at L384 sees a new entry and calls SetEventTime() again. So with a time model every event after the first gets two time differences; with SetEventMeanTime(10) the mean spacing is about 20 ns (confirmed by a simulation of this code path). Without a time model the first call still draws gRandom->Uniform(0, 0) on every event. Correction: The doubling happens only when the input has no stored EventHeader. (or that header's time is negative). Otherwise GetEventTime() returns the input header time (L693-697). Without a time model, the extra gRandom->Uniform(0, 0) draw adds 0 to the time and only shifts the random sequence, so by itself it does not change results.
issues.fix: Set fCurrentEntryNo = i at the start of ReadEvent(), drop the unconditional SetEventTime() call, and give SetEventTime() the same per-entry guard as FairFileSource::SetEventTime().
issues.evidence: ReadEvent() calls SetEventTime() at FairMixedSource.cxx:349, and SetEventTime() has no per-entry guard (L662-675; FairFileSource.cxx:612-613 has one). After L383 sets fCurrentEntryNo = i, GetEventTime() at L384 sees fTimeforEntryNo != fCurrentEntryNo (L709-710) and adds a second step. The shipped CTest macro Tutorial2/macros/create_digis_mixed.C (SetEventMeanTime(10)) takes this path, because simulation input has no EventHeader. branch and the early return at L693-697 is skipped. A copy of the logic gives a mean spacing of 19.99 ns with 2 draws per event. This also halves the time-based signal rates from BGWindowWidthTime(), which assume the spacing is fEventMeanTime (L598).

issues.title: Mixed source selects signals with per-signal ratios instead of cumulative ones
issues.description: ReadEvent() draws one uniform number and takes the first signal (in identifier order) whose own ratio is at least that number. So signal k gets max(0, ratio_k - largest earlier ratio) of the events instead of ratio_k. With the Tutorial 2 settings (create_digis_mixed.C: SetEventMeanTime(10), BGWindowWidthTime(100,1) and (60,2)), signal 2 gets about 6.7 % instead of 16.7 %; a simulation of the loop gives 0.066. With the commented-out BGWindowWidthNo(20,1) and (30,2) settings, signal 2 is never read because 1/31 < 1/21. Correction: The exact share for signal 2 is 1/6 - 1/10 = 0.0667 (the report says 0.066).
issues.fix: Compare the random number with the running sum of the ratios (add mi.second to a cumulative value in the loop) instead of with each ratio alone.
issues.evidence: ReadEvent() draws one uniform number (FairMixedSource.cxx:351) and takes the first map entry whose own ratio is >= it (lines 356-359), so signal k only gets max(0, r_k - largest earlier r). BGWindowWidthTime stores mean/background (line 598), so create_digis_mixed.C:85-90 sets r1=0.1 and r2=0.167. A 10M-event copy of the loop gives shares of 0.100 and 0.0667, and with BGWindowWidthNo(20,1)/(30,2) signal 2 is never picked. CheckMaxEventNo (lines 620-625) treats each ratio as that signal's own share, so the loop is the bug, and the macro runs as a CTest (Tutorial2/macros/CMakeLists.txt:92).

issues.title: FairMixedSource::ReadEvent() returns 0 even when it read no data
issues.description: ReadEvent() ignores the return values of GetEntry() (L362, L374) and always returns 0. CheckMaxEventNo() sets the event limit from expected counts, so the random draws can read past the end of a chain; TChain::GetEntry() then reads nothing and the tasks see the previous entry again. If neither BGWindowWidthNo() nor BGWindowWidthTime() was called (check at L354), no chain is read at all and every event repeats the entry read in SpecifyRunId(), without any message.
issues.fix: Return a non-zero value with an error message when GetEntry() returns <= 0 or when no mixing ratio is set.

issues.title: GetSignalChainNo() uses a bit shift (i << fNoOfSignals) instead of a range check
issues.description: The test 'if (i << fNoOfSignals)' is false only for i = 0 and true for every practical i > 0. For an unknown positive identifier the function logs nothing and returns fSignalTypeList[i], and operator[] inserts a null TChain* into the map. ActivateObject() later loops over fSignalTypeList and dereferences that null entry. Nothing in the repository calls this public method (SpecifyRunId() uses FairRootManager::GetSignalChainNo()).
issues.fix: Look the identifier up with fSignalTypeList.find(i) and log an error when it is missing.

issues.title: AddBackgroundFile() always fails before Init(), so extra background files are impossible
issues.description: AddBackgroundFile() adds to fBackgroundChain, but only Init() creates that chain (L199-202), and SetBackgroundFile() does not. So a call in the macro before FairRunAna::Init() always ends in LOG(fatal) 'Use SetBackGroundFile first, then add files to background', even after SetBackgroundFile(). fInputChainList is never filled, so the loop in Init() that adds more input files (L269-290) is dead.
issues.fix: Store the names in fInputChainList in AddBackgroundFile() and let Init() add them, or create fBackgroundChain in SetBackgroundFile().

issues.title: OpenSignalChain() and OpenBackgroundChain() are never called
issues.description: No code calls OpenBackgroundChain() (L468) or OpenSignalChain() (L515). So the branch lists of the signal files are never compared with the background file, and a signal file with a different structure is not detected.
issues.fix: Run the branch-list check for the signal chains from Init(), or remove the two functions.

issues.title: BGWindowWidthTime() fatal message names non-existent SetSignalRateTime()
issues.description: When no event mean time is set, BGWindowWidthTime() stops with 'You have to Set the Event mean time before using SetSignalRateTime!'. No method SetSignalRateTime() exists: the user called BGWindowWidthTime() and must call SetEventMeanTime() or SetEventTimeInterval() first.
issues.fix: Name BGWindowWidthTime() and SetEventMeanTime() in the message.

issues.title: UseRunIdfromSG() doc comment says it uses the background run ID
issues.description: The comments of UseRunIdfromSG() in FairMixedSource.cxx:751 and FairMixedSource.h:123 say 'Use the Backgraund rRunID', but the method selects the run ID of a signal file. 'Backgraund' is also misspelled at FairMixedSource.h:121 and :212 and at FairMixedSource.cxx:745.
issues.fix: Say 'Use the run ID of the signal file with this identifier' and correct 'Backgraund' to 'Background'.

issues.title: FairAnaSelector::Init() reads VMCWORKDIR into vmcPath and never uses it
issues.description: Init() sets 'TString vmcPath = gSystem->Getenv("VMCWORKDIR")', but no later code reads vmcPath.
issues.fix: Remove the variable.

issues.title: AddIncludeType() logs 'AddIgnoreType' (copy-paste)
issues.description: FairLinkManager::AddIncludeType() writes the debug message 'AddIgnoreType', copied from AddIgnoreType(). Debug logs then name the wrong operation.
issues.fix: Log 'AddIncludeType' instead.

issues.title: Deprecation message misspells FairMCApplication as 'FairMCApplcation'
issues.description: The [[deprecated]] text of FairRadGridManager::Instance() says 'Maybe use FairMCApplcation::GetRadGridMan()'. Every user of Instance() sees the misspelled class name in the compiler warning. CHANGELOG.md:224 has the same typo.
issues.fix: Correct the spelling in the attribute and in CHANGELOG.md.

issues.title: FairRadMapManager prints an off-by-one volume count and writes to std::cout
issues.description: Init() prints 'calculating the masses for <lastvolume> volumes', but lastvolume is GetLast(), the last index, so the count is one too low. Init() also prints one std::cout line per volume (L114), and Reset(), called from FairMCApplication::FinishEvent(), prints a separator line at every event (L124). This output bypasses FairLogger, so the log level cannot silence it.
issues.fix: Print GetLast() + 1 (or GetEntriesFast()) as the count and use LOG(info) or LOG(debug) for all these lines.

issues.title: FairRadMapManager never computes fDoseSL, so FairRadMapPoint::GetDoseSL() is always 0
issues.description: fDoseSL is set to 0 in the constructor (L55) and at each volume entry (L134), and no code computes it. AddPoint() passes it to every FairRadMapPoint (L207), so GetDoseSL() always returns 0 and the RadMap branch stores only zeros in this field.
issues.fix: Compute fDoseSL as intended, or remove it and GetDoseSL() (with a class version bump of FairRadMapPoint).

issues.title: FairRingSorter never deletes its element clones, so every sorted element leaks
issues.description: AddElement() clones every element with CreateElement(), and WriteOutElement() hands the pointers out through fOutputData, but DeleteOutputData() only clears the vector. The Tutorial 3 and template sorter tasks copy-construct each element into the output array, and the base AddNewDataToTClonesArray() stores the pointer in a TClonesArray slot, where Delete() only runs the destructor; so every sorted element leaks and memory grows with the data volume. AddElement() also leaks the clone of an element that it rejects as too late (FairRingSorter.cxx:22-27).
issues.fix: Delete the elements in DeleteOutputData() after the task has copied them (and make the base AddNewDataToTClonesArray() copy instead of storing the pointer), and delete the clone of a rejected element in AddElement().

issues.title: FairRingSorterTask::Init() crashes unless Register(TString, ...) created the input branch
issues.description: Init() takes the input array from GetTClonesArray(fInputBranch), which only knows branches created with Register(TString, TString, TString, Bool_t) in the same run. For a branch from the input file, a branch registered with the TCollection* overload (such as FairTestDetectorDigiTask's FairTestDetectorDigi), or the empty fInputBranch of the default and named constructors, it logs 'not registered' and returns nullptr. Line 47 then calls fInputArray->GetClass() and crashes; Exec() and FinishTask() use the array without a check too.
issues.fix: Fall back to GetObject(fInputBranch) when GetTClonesArray() returns nullptr, and return kERROR with a clear message if no TClonesArray is found.

issues.title: FairRingSorterTask::FinishTask() sorts the last event twice without a writeout buffer
issues.description: FinishTask() adds every element of the input array to the sorter again (L98-101). This is right only when a writeout buffer refilled the array in StoreAllWriteoutBufferData(), because DeleteOldWriteoutBufferData() empties buffered arrays after each event. If a task fills the input branch without a writeout buffer and clears it at the start of Exec() instead of in FinishEvent(), the array still holds the last event, so that event is sorted and written twice.
issues.fix: Re-read the input array in FinishTask() only when a writeout buffer feeds the input branch (this needs a public FairRootManager::GetWriteoutBuffer()).

issues.title: FairRingSorterTask calls TObject::Print() instead of FairRingSorter::print()
issues.description: FairRingSorter defines print(std::ostream&) in lower case, so fSorter->Print() calls TObject::Print(), which prints only 'OBJ: FairRingSorter ...'. FinishTask() calls it at L102 without a verbosity check, so every run prints this line. The debug calls at L69 and L119 never show the ring buffer.
issues.fix: Call fSorter->print() inside a verbosity check, or override Print() in FairRingSorter to call print().

issues.title: InitSource() leaks the TChain that file sources replace with SetInChain()
issues.description: InitSource() always creates a TChain in fSourceChain (L118) before it calls fSource->Init(). FairFileSource::Init() (FairFileSource.cxx:156-158) and FairMixedSource (FairMixedSource.cxx:293) then pass their own chain to SetInChain() (L680-686), which overwrites fSourceChain without deleting the old one. So the first TChain is never deleted, once per run.
issues.fix: Create the chain in InitSource() only when the source sets none, or delete the replaced chain in SetInChain() when it differs from the new one.

issues.title: Typo 'Pleae' in the fatal message of RegisterImpl()
issues.description: RegisterImpl() stops with LOG(fatal) when the branch name equals the folder name. The message says 'Pleae change either the name or the folder name.'
issues.fix: Change 'Pleae' to 'Please'.

issues.title: Memory-only Register() crashes when no FairRun (and so no FairLinkManager) exists
issues.description: RegisterImpl() calls FairLinkManager::Instance()->AddIgnoreType() for every memory-only branch (toFile false). FairLinkManager::Instance() returns the fLinkManager member of FairRun (FairRun.h:217), and nullptr when no FairRun exists. So a memory-only Register() without a FairRun, for example in a unit test of a task, dereferences a null pointer, while a persistent Register() works.
issues.fix: Check FairLinkManager::Instance() for nullptr before calling AddIgnoreType().

issues.title: Register(TString, ...) records each new branch twice in FairMonitor
issues.description: Register(TString, TString, TString, Bool_t) calls FairMonitor::RecordRegister() at L211, and for a new branch it then calls the TCollection* overload of Register(), whose RegisterImpl() calls RecordRegister() again (L152). With the monitor enabled, each such branch appears twice in the monitor's records and drawn arrows. Without a current task, FairMonitor logs two 'WITHOUT TASK' lines.
issues.fix: Remove the RecordRegister() call at L211, because RegisterImpl() already records each new branch.

issues.title: Unreachable second null check of fSource in ReadEvent()
issues.description: ReadEvent() returns 0 at L411-412 when fSource is null, so the check at L418-421 (LOG(fatal) and return -1) can never run. The two checks disagree: the live one reports success for a missing source, while the dead one was meant to stop the run.
issues.fix: Remove the unreachable block, or replace the early return with the fatal check if a missing source is an error.

issues.title: ReadNextEvent() is a stub, so FairRunAna::Run(Double_t) processes no event
issues.description: FairRootManager::ReadNextEvent(Double_t) is a '/// TODO' stub that always returns kFALSE. FairRunAna::Run(Double_t delta_t) (FairRunAna.cxx:422-439) loops on it, so it never runs a task's Exec(), but it still calls StoreAllWriteoutBufferData(), FinishTask(), LastFill() and Write(). A call such as Run(10.) or Run(n) with a Double_t or Float_t n selects this overload and silently produces an output without events.
issues.fix: Implement ReadNextEvent(), or make Run(Double_t) stop with LOG(fatal) and deprecate it; also fix the typo 'timpe' in its doc comment (FairRunAna.h:44).

issues.title: GetCloneOfLinkData() and GetCloneOfTClonesArray() use GetObject() without a null check
issues.description: GetCloneOfLinkData() calls GetObject(GetBranchName(type))->Clone() (L560) and dataArray->GetEntriesFast() (L566) without checking for nullptr, and GetCloneOfTClonesArray() does the same at L644. GetObject() returns nullptr when the branch is in the input tree but has no object in the input folders, for example a branch written with RegisterAny() (FairRootFileSink::RegisterAny() adds no folder object). A link to such a branch then crashes these functions instead of giving nullptr.
issues.fix: Check the GetObject() result in both functions and return nullptr (after resetting the branch entry) when it is null.

issues.title: CheckBranch() caches its map at the first call and returns 0 for branches added later
issues.description: CheckBranch() builds fBrPerMap once, at its first call, from the branches known then (CreatePerMap()), and later calls only look in this map. A branch registered after the first call therefore gets 0 ('does not exist'). For example, FairMultiLinkedData::GetData() then prints 'Branch does not exist in Memory' and returns nullptr for a branch that exists.
issues.fix: When a name is missing from fBrPerMap, compute its status with CheckBranchSt() and add it, instead of returning 0.

issues.title: SetBranchNameList() does not reset fBranchSeqId, so branch IDs break and lookups crash
issues.description: SetBranchNameList() clears fBranchNameList and resets fMCTrackBranchId, but not fBranchSeqId, so AddBranchToList() numbers the new names after the old count. fMCTrackBranchId then no longer equals GetBranchId("MCTrack"), GetBranchName() (L255-257) accepts IDs up to the old count and dereferences a null TObjString, and CreatePerMap() (L792-796) reads past the end of the list. No code in the repository calls the function.
issues.fix: Reset fBranchSeqId (and the cached persistence map) before adding the new names, or remove the unused function.

issues.title: ActivateBranch() appends to fObj2 on every GetObject() call; the list grows forever
issues.description: ActivateBranch() calls fObj2.emplace_back() on every call, also when GetMemoryBranch() already found the branch, and nothing removes entries from this std::list (FairRootManager.h:358). GetObject() calls it each time, and some callers run per event: FairMultiLinkedData::InsertHistory() for each added link (history is on by default) and FairMQRunDevice::SendBranches() for each branch. So fObj2 grows by one node per call for the whole run, and UpdateBranches() logs and re-activates every duplicate.
issues.fix: Append to fObj2 only when ActivateBranch() activates a branch from the input folders for the first time.

issues.title: StoreAllWriteoutBufferData() can skip the final fill and lose the last buffered data
issues.description: StoreAllWriteoutBufferData() sets fFillLastData from GetNData(), which counts only fDeadTime_map (FairWriteoutBuffer.h:81), and it counts before WriteOutAllData() moves fStartTime_map into the dead-time map. The last event's buffered data are always still in the start-time map, so when the dead-time map is empty they are written to the arrays but LastFill() does not store them. The assignment also overwrites any earlier SetLastFill(): only a call in FinishTask(), as in FairRingSorterTask.cxx:121, takes effect, so time-based runs without FairRingSorterTask lose this data.
issues.fix: Count the data in both maps (or check the arrays after WriteOutAllData()) and only raise the flag, for example fFillLastData = fFillLastData || dataInBuffer.
issues.evidence: GetNData() is only fDeadTime_map.size() (FairWriteoutBuffer.h:81), and it is read before WriteOutAllData() moves the start-time map (FairRootManager.cxx:883-888). StoreWriteoutBufferData runs before ExecuteTask (FairRunAna.cxx:325-326, FairRunOnline.cxx:217-218), so the last event's data is always still in fStartTime_map. If the dead-time map is empty, that data goes into the arrays but LastFill() skips Fill (FairRootManager.cxx:340); a copy of the buffer logic loses all data of a 1-event run. Medium, not high: only the tail of a run is lost, and the in-tree example run_digi_timebased.C is safe because FairRingSorterTask::FinishTask calls SetLastFill() after the flush (FairRingSorterTask.cxx:121).

issues.title: GetNameFromFile() keeps spaces and '\r' in names read from rootmanager.dat
issues.description: GetNameFromFile() returns the rest of the first line that starts with 'treename=' or 'foldername=' and does not trim it. Spaces after '=', trailing spaces or a Windows '\r' line end become part of the tree or folder name. The output tree can then be called 'mytree\r', and plain ROOT code does not find 'mytree'.
issues.fix: Trim leading and trailing whitespace, including '\r', from the returned name.

issues.title: GetTreeName() and GetFolderName() return pointers into ROOT's circular Form() buffer
issues.description: GetTreeName() and GetFolderName() return Form("%s", ...) when the name comes from SetTreeName()/SetFolderName() or rootmanager.dat. Form() writes into ROOT's 4096-byte circular buffer, and later Form() calls overwrite it. A caller that keeps the returned const char* can later read another string; all callers inside FairRoot copy the name at once.
issues.fix: Return std::string (or the c_str() of a static std::string that holds the resolved name) instead of a Form() pointer.

issues.title: GetFolderName() dereferences FairRun::Instance() without a null check
issues.description: When neither SetFolderName() nor a foldername= line in $VMCWORKDIR/config/rootmanager.dat gives a name, GetFolderName() calls FairRun::Instance()->IsAna(). FairRun::Instance() is nullptr before a FairRun exists or after it is destroyed, so this public static function, and InitSource() and FairFileSource::Init() which call it, crash in that case. GetTreeName() works without a FairRun.
issues.fix: Check FairRun::Instance() for nullptr and use the default 'cbmroot' in that case.

issues.title: Typo 'expexted' in the warning of EmitMemoryBranchWrongTypeWarning()
issues.description: EmitMemoryBranchWrongTypeWarning(), which InitObjectAs() reaches through GetMemoryBranchAny(), prints '(expexted: <type> )'. examples/MQ/pixelDetector/src/FairOnlineSink.cxx:43 has the same typo.
issues.fix: Change 'expexted' to 'expected' in both files.

issues.title: UpdateFileName() leaves names without '.root' unchanged, so MT workers share one file
issues.description: UpdateFileName() inserts '_t<N>' at fileName.Index(".root"). For a name without '.root', Index() returns -1, and TString::Insert() then logs 'first argument out of bounds' and leaves the name unchanged. FairRootFileSink::CloneSink() (FairRootFileSink.cxx:337-347) uses it for each Geant4 MT worker, so every worker opens the master's file name with "recreate" and the threads overwrite each other's output. Index() also matches the first '.root' anywhere in the path, for example in a directory name.
issues.fix: Insert the suffix only before a trailing '.root' extension (search from the end), and append '_t<N>' when the name has no such extension.

issues.title: GetOutFile() and GetOutTree() crash without a sink and check the sink type only by assert
issues.description: GetOutFile() and GetOutTree() call GetSink()->GetSinkType() without a null check, so they crash when the run has no sink instead of returning nullptr. They check the sink type only with assert() before a static_cast to FairRootFileSink; FairRoot's own GCC flags keep asserts, but in a build with NDEBUG another sink type gives undefined behavior. FairRun::GetOutputFile() (FairRun.cxx:223-230) has the same code.
issues.fix: Return nullptr with an error message when the sink is missing or is not a FairRootFileSink, using dynamic_cast instead of assert plus static_cast.

issues.title: CheckBranch() doc says 1 means persistent, but 1 means 'found in the input file'
issues.description: The comments of CheckBranch() and CheckBranchSt() say 1 means 'Branch is Persistance' and 2 means 'Memory Branch' (also FairRootManager.h:337-342 and FairRootManager.cxx:781-784). CheckBranchSt() returns 1 when ListFolderSearch() finds the branch in the input file's folders, and 2 for any other branch in the memory map. So a branch registered in this run with toFile = kTRUE gets 2, not 1.
issues.fix: Document 1 as 'branch comes from the input file' and 2 as 'branch exists only in memory in this run, persistent or not'.

issues.title: Doc comments in FairRootManager.h sit above the wrong declarations
issues.description: Several doc comments in FairRootManager.h describe a different declaration, so Doxygen attaches them to the wrong function. 'Return a pointer to the object (collection) saved in the fInTree branch named BrName' (L112) is above GetEventTime(), and the GetData() text (L116-120) is above GetCloneOfTClonesArray(). 'Read all entries from input tree(s) with time stamp from current time to dt' (L161) is above GetRunId() instead of ReadNextEvent(), and the branch-name truncation text (L210-212) is above Write().
issues.fix: Move each comment to the declaration it describes and delete the stale ones.

issues.title: GetTSBuffer() inserts a null entry that AllDataProcessed() then dereferences
issues.description: GetTSBuffer() returns fTSBufferMap[branchName], so a name without a buffer inserts a nullptr entry. AllDataProcessed() (FairRootManager.cxx:321-329), TerminateAllTSBuffer() (314-319) and TerminateTSBuffer() (307-312) then call methods on that nullptr. FairRunAna::RunTSBuffers() calls AllDataProcessed() in its loop condition.
issues.fix: Use find() in GetTSBuffer() and return nullptr without inserting an entry.

issues.title: Memory-only RegisterAny() does not add the branch to the link ignore list
issues.description: Register() with toFile false puts the branch ID on FairLinkManager's ignore list (FairRootManager.cxx:175-177), so FairMultiLinkedData drops links to memory-only branches. RegisterAny() with persistence false does not do this. Links to memory-only RegisterAny() branches therefore stay in the output and point to data that the file does not contain.
issues.fix: In RegisterAny(), add the branch to the ignore list when persistence is false, as Register() does (with a null check on FairLinkManager::Instance()).

issues.title: Persistent RegisterAny() without a sink is fatal, but persistent Register() only warns
issues.description: Without a sink, RegisterAny() with persistence true stops the run with LOG(fatal) (L464), but Register() with toFile true only logs a warning (FairRootManager.cxx:169) and keeps a memory branch. Runs without a sink are allowed (InitSink() only logs 'No branches will be stored'). So a task that uses RegisterAny() aborts such a run, while an equal task that uses Register() does not.
issues.fix: Use the same severity in both functions, preferably a warning plus a memory-only branch, since runs without a sink are allowed.

issues.title: static_assert messages in InitObjectAs() name a function 'GetObjectAs'
issues.description: The static_assert messages in InitObjectAs() (L474 and L476) say 'Return type of GetObjectAs has to be a pointer'. FairRootManager has no GetObjectAs(), so the compile error names a function that does not exist.
issues.fix: Replace 'GetObjectAs' with 'InitObjectAs' in both messages.

issues.title: FairRun never deletes fFileHeader, and FairFileHeader never deletes its lists
issues.description: The FairRun constructor creates fFileHeader with new (L50), but ~FairRun() (L84-108) and the derived run destructors never delete it. ~FairFileHeader() is empty, so fTaskList, fFileList and their entries leak too. FairRun::SetTask() (L136-138) calls Clear() on fTaskList, which does not own its TObjStrings, so those leak as well.
issues.fix: Own fFileHeader with std::unique_ptr, and let FairFileHeader own and delete fTaskList and fFileList (SetOwner(kTRUE) plus delete in the destructor).

excerpt.code:
, fRunId(0)
, fAna(kFALSE)
, fFileHeader(new FairFileHeader())
, fGenerateRunInfo(kFALSE)
, fIsMaster(isMaster)

issues.title: GetRunId() narrows the UInt_t run ID to Int_t, so generated IDs turn negative in 2038
issues.description: FairRun stores the run ID as UInt_t, but GetRunId() returns static_cast<Int_t>(fRunId). FairRuntimeDb::addRun() and FairSource::SetRunId()/GetRunId() also use Int_t, while FairEventHeader uses UInt_t. Generated run IDs are Unix seconds (FairRunIdGenerator::generateId()), so from 2038-01-19 they pass INT_MAX and these Int_t functions see negative run IDs.
issues.fix: Use UInt_t for run IDs in FairRun::GetRunId(), FairRuntimeDb::addRun() and FairSource.

issues.title: SetOutputFileName() doc says 'without creating the file', but the function creates it
issues.description: The doc comment says SetOutputFileName() sets the name 'without creating the file'. The function (FairRun.cxx:215-221) makes a FairRootFileSink, whose constructor calls TFile::Open(name, "recreate") (FairRootFileSink.cxx:60-68). So the call creates the file at once and overwrites an existing file with that name.
issues.fix: Change the comment to say that the function creates (and overwrites) the file at once.

issues.title: SetGeomFile() dereferences a null TFile when the file cannot be opened
issues.description: TFile::Open() returns nullptr when the file is missing or unreadable, so fInputGeoFile->IsZombie() at L120 crashes before the error message is printed. When the open fails, the function also still logs 'Opening Geometry input file' and sets fLoadGeo.
issues.fix: Check for nullptr before IsZombie() and log the opening message only when the file is open.

issues.title: Without an input source, Run() and Run(n) process no events
issues.description: When InitSource() returns false, Run() calls DummyRun(Ev_start, Ev_end) before the NStart/NStop conversion at L269-291. Run() becomes DummyRun(0, 0) and Run(n) becomes DummyRun(n, 0), so no event runs; only Run(0, n) processes n events. Init() explicitly supports runs without an input, and FairRunAna.h:38-42 promises n entries for Run(n).
issues.fix: Apply the same Ev_end == 0 conversion before the call to DummyRun().

issues.title: 'File has less events than requested' warning never fires with FairFileSource
issues.description: Run() and RunEventReco() (L366) compare Ev_end with CheckMaxEventNo(Ev_end), but FairFileSource::CheckMaxEventNo() returns its argument unchanged when it is not 0 (FairFileSource.cxx:572-582). So the warning never prints, and the 'run will run from event ... to N' message shows the requested N. Run() then stops with the 'Breaking the event loop' warning, and the deprecated RunEventReco(), which ignores the ReadEvent() result, runs the tasks past the end of the file.
issues.fix: Clamp the result to fInChain->GetEntries() in FairFileSource::CheckMaxEventNo(), as FairMixedSource does.

issues.title: Run() takes over SIGINT for good, and its handler calls LOG()
issues.description: Every loop iteration of Run() calls gSystem->IgnoreInterrupt() and signal(SIGINT, FRA_handler_ctrlc), and nothing restores ROOT's handler after the loop, so after Run() Ctrl-C at the ROOT prompt or in a host program only logs a message and sets gFRAIsInterrupted. The handler (L52-56) calls LOG(info), which allocates memory and takes locks, so Ctrl-C during processing can deadlock; the flag is a plain Bool_t, not a volatile sig_atomic_t. FairRunOnline::EventLoop() (FairRunOnline.cxx:209-210) installs its handler the same way.
issues.fix: Install the handler once with sigaction() before the loop, restore the old handler after it, and only set a volatile sig_atomic_t flag in the handler.

issues.title: Run(Double_t) processes no events because ReadNextEvent() is a stub
issues.description: FairRootManager::ReadNextEvent() (FairRootManager.cxx:479-484) is a TODO stub that always returns kFALSE, so the loop in Run(Double_t) never runs. The function then calls FinishTask(), LastFill() and Write() on an empty run. A double argument such as Run(1e4) or Run(10.) silently selects this overload instead of Run(Int_t, Int_t).
issues.fix: Remove Run(Double_t), or deprecate it, until ReadNextEvent() is implemented.

issues.title: RunMQ() and RunSingleEntry() call FinishTask() after every entry and never FinishEvent()
issues.description: RunMQ() and RunSingleEntry() end each entry with fTask->FinishTask(), so Finish() of every task runs once per entry, not once per run. The Tutorial 3 sampler calls RunMQ() for each message and TerminateRun() at the end (Finish() runs N+1 times), and the event display calls RunSingleEntry() on every navigation step. Neither function calls FinishEvent(), so per-event cleanup never runs; DummyRun() and RunOnLmdFiles() skip it too. The RunMQ() comment in FairRunAna.h:57-60 mentions none of this.
issues.fix: Call fTask->FinishEvent() after each entry, leave FinishTask() to TerminateRun(), and document this in FairRunAna.h.

issues.title: RunMQ() and RunSingleEntry() check the run ID before FillEventHeader()
issues.description: Run() calls ReadEvent(), FillEventHeader() and then CheckRunIdChanged() (L313-322). RunMQ() and RunSingleEntry() call CheckRunIdChanged() and ExecuteTask() before FillEventHeader(), so the check and the tasks see the run ID and event time of the previous entry. When the input changes run, for example when the event display jumps to an entry of another run, the tasks process that entry with the old parameters and Reinit() comes one entry late. RunTSBuffers(), Run(Double_t), DummyRun() and RunOnLmdFiles() also fill the header only after ExecuteTask().
issues.fix: Call FillEventHeader() right after ReadEvent() and before CheckRunIdChanged() and ExecuteTask(), as Run() does.

issues.title: RunOnLmdFiles() runs the tasks and Fill() once more after StopProcessingLMD()
issues.description: When fFinishProcessingLMDFile is set, the loop sets i = NStop, but the rest of the body still runs ExecuteTask(), FillEventHeader() and Fill(). So the comment 'Same result like break' is wrong, and one extra, stale entry goes into the output tree. No code in the repository calls RunOnLmdFiles() or StopProcessingLMD().
issues.fix: Replace 'i = NStop;' with 'break;'.

issues.title: TerminateRun() repeats the end-of-run steps without a guard
issues.description: TerminateRun() runs StoreAllWriteoutBufferData(), FinishTask(), LastFill() and Write() and then closes the sink. It suits per-entry processing (FairAnaSelector::SlaveTerminate(), the Tutorial 3 sampler), but its comment only says 'finish tasks, write output', and it is the only FairRunAna function that closes the sink. Called after Run(), which already did these steps (L339-345), it runs Finish() of every task again and writes the tree again as a new key cycle.
issues.fix: Record that the end-of-run steps ran and skip them in TerminateRun(), or document that it must only follow RunMQ() or RunOneEvent().

issues.title: RunWithTimeStamps() after Init() logs a warning and then calls exit(-1)
issues.description: A call of RunWithTimeStamps() after Init() logs at warn severity and then ends the process with exit(-1). The user sees a warning, not an error, and exit() skips stack unwinding and cleanup. SetGeomFile() and Init() use LOG(fatal) for the same kind of misuse.
issues.fix: Log the misuse at fatal or error level, and preferably return or throw instead of calling exit().

issues.title: Deprecated Run(Long64_t) runs a single entry when called with a Long64_t count
issues.description: Run(Long64_t) is an exact match for a Long64_t argument, so Run(n) with n from TTree::GetEntries() calls RunSingleEntry(n) instead of Run(Int_t, Int_t). The run then processes only entry n, which lies past the end when n is the entry count. The only sign is a deprecation warning at compile time (checked with g++ 13 and clang++).
issues.fix: Declare Run(Long64_t) as deleted (or remove it) so such calls fail to compile.

issues.title: FairRunAna keeps unused time-model and source members
issues.description: fEventTimeMin, fEventTimeMax, fEventTime, fEventMeanTime, fTimeProb, fFileSource and fMixedSource are only initialized (FairRunAna.cxx:77-84) and never used in FairRoot; the time model now lives in the sources. They keep the <TF1.h> include in the header and the 'temporary' FairFileSource.h and FairMixedSource.h includes in FairRunAna.cxx. FairMCApplication::fEventHeader (FairMCApplication.h:312) is also only initialized and never used.
issues.fix: Remove these members and the includes that only they need.

issues.title: SetProofParName() has no effect because fProofParName is never read
issues.description: The constructor sets fProofParName to "$VMCWORKDIR/gconfig/libFairRoot.par", and SetProofParName() (FairRunAnaProof.h:55) changes it, but no code reads the member. So the PAR file name has no influence on the PROOF session.
issues.fix: Remove the member and the setter, or use the PAR file in RunOnProof().

excerpt.code:
, fRunOnProofWorker(kFALSE)
, fProofServerName(proofName)
, fProofParName("$VMCWORKDIR/gconfig/libFairRoot.par")
, fOutputDirectory("")
, fProofOutputStatus("copy")

issues.title: FairRunAnaProof::Init() calls InitTask() without AlignGeometry()
issues.description: FairRunAna::Init() calls AlignGeometry() before fTask->InitTask() (FairRunAna.cxx:232-238), so tasks see the aligned geometry. FairRunAnaProof::Init() replaces Init() and skips this step, so alignment never runs on PROOF workers and tasks use the unaligned geometry. The worker run is created in FairAnaSelector::Init(), so matrices added in the client macro do not reach it either; PROOF support is deprecated and off by default.
issues.fix: Call AlignGeometry() before fTask->InitTask() in FairRunAnaProof::Init() and send the alignment matrices to the workers.

issues.title: SetField() ownership differs between FairRunAna/FairRunOnline and FairRunSim
issues.description: FairRunAna (FairRunAna.cxx:96) and FairRunOnline (FairRunOnline.cxx:85) delete fField in their destructors, but FairRunSim does not ('Not owner of the field'), and FairMCApplication does not either. No SetField() comment states the ownership. A field that the caller still owns (a stack object or one in a unique_ptr) is deleted by FairRunAna, and FairRoot never deletes a field passed to FairRunSim.
issues.fix: Use the same, explicit ownership in all run classes, for example SetField(std::unique_ptr<FairField>), and document it.

issues.title: Init() ignores readMedia(); without SetMaterials() the run fails later with a vague error
issues.description: FairRunSim::Init() calls readMedia() (L168) and drops its result. If SetMaterials() was never called (MatFname is empty by default, L58), or if the file name does not end in .geo, .dat or .setup, connectInput() returns null and no media are read. No message reports this. The first sign is a later error for each volume, such as 'Medium ... not found in list of media' (FairGeoSet.cxx:273); a media file that does not exist is reported, because FairGeoAsciiIo::open() calls Fatal().
issues.fix: Check the result of readMedia() in Init() and stop with a message that names the media file or says that SetMaterials() was not called.

issues.title: No example or test uses the non-deprecated YAML VMC configuration
issues.description: Without SetSimulationConfig() or SetSimSetup(), SetMCConfig() uses FairGenericVMCConfig, whose Setup() always logs a deprecation warning (spelled 'DEPRACATED', FairGenericVMCConfig.cxx:28). run_tutorial1.C passes FairGenericVMCConfig explicitly, and FairVMCConfig appears only in commented-out lines (runMC.C:60, runMM.C:52, FairMQSimDevice.cxx:60) that pass a raw pointer, which SetSimulationConfig(std::unique_ptr<FairGenericVMCConfig>) does not accept. So every example prints the warning, and no test runs FairYamlVMCConfig.
issues.fix: Switch at least one tested example to SetSimulationConfig(std::make_unique<FairVMCConfig>()) and fix the commented-out calls.

issues.title: SetMaterials() never falls back to $VMCWORKDIR/geometry when GEOMPATH is set
issues.description: When GEOMPATH is set, SetMaterials() builds the media path only from GEOMPATH (L347-359) and does not check that the file is there. FairModule::SetGeometryFileName() tries GEOMPATH first and then falls back to $VMCWORKDIR/geometry (FairModule.cxx:188-209). So a GEOMPATH that holds only detector geometry files works for the modules, but the media file is not found and the run aborts in FairGeoAsciiIo::open() with 'Failed to open file'.
issues.fix: Use the same lookup as SetGeometryFileName(): try GEOMPATH first, then $VMCWORKDIR/geometry.

issues.title: SetMaterials() breaks absolute paths and does not report a missing media file
issues.description: SetMaterials() always puts $GEOMPATH or $VMCWORKDIR/geometry/ in front of the name, so an absolute path or a file in the working directory resolves to a wrong path. Unlike FairModule::SetGeometryFileName(), it does not fall back to VMCWORKDIR when GEOMPATH is set and does not check that the file exists. Init() ignores the result of readMedia() (L168), so a missing file or a name without .geo/.dat/.setup leaves the run without media, and the error shows up only later, for example as the 'Material ... is not defined' fatal in FairModule.cxx:660.
issues.fix: Resolve the path like FairModule::SetGeometryFileName() (absolute path, then GEOMPATH, then VMCWORKDIR) and fail in Init() when readMedia() returns kFALSE.

issues.title: SetGeoModel() is skipped with only info messages unless SetName("TGeant3") came first
issues.description: SetGeoModel() checks fName == "TGeant3" at call time. If the macro calls it before SetName("TGeant3"), the setting is dropped with two info-level messages, which also name FairRun instead of FairRunSim. No code in the repository calls SetGeoModel().
issues.fix: Always store the model and check the engine in Init(), with a warning if it is not TGeant3.

issues.title: SetPythiaDecayer("file.C") and SetUserDecay("file.C") call the Bool_t overload
issues.description: Both setters have a Bool_t and a const TString& overload. A string literal converts to bool by a standard conversion, which beats the user-defined conversion to TString, so the call only sets the flag; g++ 13 and clang++ pick this overload without a warning. FairMCApplication then loads the default DecayConfig.C or UserDecay.C and silently ignores the given file. The examples pass TString variables, so they are not affected.
issues.fix: Add const char* overloads that forward to the TString versions, or give the Bool_t setters a different name.

issues.title: fGen deprecation note says removal in v19.2, but the plan is v20
issues.description: The \deprecated note on FairRunSim::fGen says it will be removed in v19.2. CHANGELOG.md:238-240 schedules the 18.8 deprecations for removal in v20, and the other notes say v20 (for example FairRun.h:172).
issues.fix: Change the note to v20, or update the CHANGELOG if v19.2 is really meant.

excerpt.code:
*
 * \deprecated Use \ref GetPrimaryGenerator() / \ref SetGenerator()
 * \deprecated Deprecated in v18.8, will be removed in v19.2.
 */
[[deprecated("Use Setter/Getter")]] FairPrimaryGenerator* fGen{nullptr};   //!

issues.title: FairTask(const char*, Int_t) leaves fStreamProcessing uninitialized
issues.description: The default constructor sets fStreamProcessing to kFALSE (L29), but the named constructor does not, and FairTask.h:111 has no default member initializer. Many tasks, including templates/NewTask/NewTask.cxx:15, use the named constructor, so a task that reads fStreamProcessing without calling SetStreamProcessing() reads an indeterminate value. FairTestDetectorRecoTask reads the flag (FairTestDetectorRecoTask.cxx:78) and is safe only because it uses the default constructor.
issues.fix: Initialize fStreamProcessing to kFALSE in the named constructor or with a default member initializer in FairTask.h.

    : TTask(name, "FairTask")
    , fVerbose(iVerbose)
    , fInputPersistance(-1)
    , fOutputPersistance()
{}

void FairTask::CheckInputPersistance(TString branchName)

issues.title: InitTask() leaves an inactive task as the FairMonitor current task
issues.description: InitTask() calls FairMonitor::SetCurrentTask(this) before the fActive check and returns for an inactive task without SetCurrentTask(0). If the last task to initialize is inactive, later Register() and GetObject() calls outside any task are attributed to it in the monitor's data-flow output. This matters only when FairMonitor is enabled.
issues.fix: Call SetCurrentTask(this) after the fActive check, or reset it before the early return.

issues.title: InitTask() keeps a task active after Init() returns kFATAL
issues.description: On kFATAL, InitTask() only writes LOG(fatal) and leaves fActive at kTRUE; ReInitTask() (L71-77) does the same. fair::Logger stops the program on fatal only through a callback, and FairRoot sets that callback only in the FairLogger constructor (FairLogger.cxx:37), which runs only when code calls FairLogger::GetLogger(). In a macro that never calls it, such as Tutorial2/macros/create_digis.C, the run goes on and calls Exec() of the task whose Init() failed.
issues.fix: Set fActive = kFALSE (or throw) on kFATAL in InitTask() and ReInitTask() instead of relying on LOG(fatal) to end the program.

issues.title: Overriding FinishEvent() or FinishTask() drops the fActive check and the subtask calls
issues.description: FinishEvent() and FinishTask() are public virtual functions that hold the fActive check and the calls into the subtasks. An override replaces both, so the run calls it for inactive tasks, and its subtasks get no call unless it calls the base function. FairRingSorterTask overrides both (FairRingSorterTask.cxx:89-122): after SetActive(kFALSE) its Init() never runs, so FinishEvent() dereferences the null fOutputArray on the first event.
issues.fix: Skip inactive tasks in FinishEvents() and FinishTasks(), and give derived classes protected hooks instead of virtual entry points.

issues.title: SetOutputBranchPersistent() has no effect by itself and ignores a second call
issues.description: FairTask.h:96-98 says a branch set to false 'will not be written to the output', but FairRoot never reads the flag: only IsOutputBranchPersistent() returns it, and no code in the repository calls it. The flag works only if the task itself passes IsOutputBranchPersistent() to Register(). SetOutputBranchPersistent() also uses std::map::insert, so a second call for the same branch, for example a macro that overrides a default set in the task constructor, is ignored.
issues.fix: Assign with fOutputPersistance[branchName] = persistence, and either apply the flag in the framework or document that the task must use IsOutputBranchPersistent().

issues.title: SetVertexCut() checks the cut against twice the top-volume half-lengths
issues.description: TGeoBBox::GetDX() returns the half-length, but SetVertexCut() compares the cut values with 2 * DX (and 2 * DY, 2 * DZ) and ignores the box origin. So a region partly or fully outside the top volume passes the check. A region fully outside then stores no trajectories, and the 'invalid region' message never appears.
issues.fix: Compare against the real box extent (origin plus or minus DX, DY, DZ), or only check that each minimum is below its maximum.

issues.title: FairTrajFilter class comment names the wrong setter and the wrong track storage
issues.description: The comment says the filter is created when FairRun::SetStoreTraj(kTRUE) is called, but the setter is FairRunSim::SetStoreTraj() (FairRunSim.h:96), and FairMCApplication creates the filter. It also says trajectories go into the gGeoManager track list, but the filter keeps them in its own TClonesArray, registered as branch GeoTracks (FairTrajFilter.cxx:65, 78-81).
issues.fix: Name FairRunSim::SetStoreTraj() and the GeoTracks branch in the comment.

issues.title: FairTSBufferFunctional constructor goes on after a missing branch and then crashes
issues.description: When the branch is not in the tree, the constructor prints an -E- message and continues. If GetObject() also returns nullptr, L41 dereferences fInputArray; otherwise the null fBranch crashes later in GetData(), ReadInNextFilledEntry(), ReadInNextEntry(), ReadInEntry() and AllDataProcessed() (L117, 221, 252, 261, 278). FairRootManager::GetData() creates the buffer for any branch name a task asks for, so a typo in a branch name ends in a segmentation fault.
issues.fix: Throw an exception (or return an error that FairRootManager::GetData() checks) when fBranch or fInputArray is null.

issues.title: GetData() logs an actualTime that is never set; verbose output cannot be enabled
issues.description: The local actualTime is set to 0 and never updated, so the message at L126-127 would always print 0. That message cannot appear anyway: fVerbose is private, set to 0 in the constructor and has no setter, so no verbose block in the class runs.
issues.fix: Remove actualTime (or fill it from the last data point) and add a SetVerbose() setter or drop the verbose blocks.

issues.title: StopTime::TimeOut() can never report a request for an earlier time
issues.description: TimeOut() tests fRequestTime != fOldTime and then fRequestTime == fOldTime, so the else branch with the '-E- ... smaller than old time' message is unreachable. A request for an earlier time takes the first branch, resets the counter and returns false. The class comment warns that the buffer cannot go back in time, but this check never catches it.
issues.fix: Test fRequestTime > fOldTime in the first branch so that smaller times reach the error branch.

issues.title: Truncated date 'Feb 18, 201' in the FairTSBufferFunctional class comment
issues.description: The class comment says 'Created on: Feb 18, 201'. The year is missing its last digit.
issues.fix: Correct or remove the date.

excerpt.code:

*

issues.title: GetAllData() dereferences rbegin() of an empty dead-time map
issues.description: GetAllData() reads fDeadTime_map.rbegin()->first without checking that the map has entries. On an empty buffer rbegin() equals rend(), and dereferencing it is undefined behavior. The only caller is the deprecated FairEventBuilder::WriteOutAllDeadTimeData() (FairEventBuilder.cxx:71).
issues.fix: Return an empty vector when fDeadTime_map is empty.

issues.title: FairWriteoutBuffer leaks data that FillDataToDeadTimeMap() drops or writes out
issues.description: In the no-interference branch (L214-218), FillDataToDeadTimeMap() copies the old object into the TClonesArray and never deletes it, while WriteOutDataDeadTimeMap() deletes after copying (L90). In the interference branch, the default Modify() returns only the old object, so the new clone is dropped without delete. With fTreeSave false, WriteOutDataDeadTimeMap() takes data out of the maps (L73) and neither writes nor deletes it. Tutorial 3's FairTestDetectorDigiWriteoutBuffer uses the default Modify(), so it leaks one digi each time an element is hit again while its previous digi is still buffered.
issues.fix: Delete oldData after writing it out, delete every input object that Modify() does not return, and delete removed data when fTreeSave is false.

issues.title: ActivateBuffering() comment suggests that buffering is off by default
issues.description: The comment says fActivateBuffering 'has to be set to kTRUE to use the buffering. Otherwise the data is directly stored'. Only the default constructor sets it to kFALSE (FairWriteoutBuffer.h:57); the constructor with a branch name, which tasks use, sets kTRUE (FairWriteoutBuffer.cxx:29). So buffering is on unless the user turns it off.
issues.fix: State the default of each constructor in the comment.

issues.title: FairWriteoutBufferAbsBasis.h is an unused header outside the build
issues.description: The header has no .cxx file, so the header list that fairroot/base/CMakeLists.txt builds from the sources and LinkDef.h both leave it out, and it is not installed. No class derives from FairWriteoutBufferAbsBasis, and no file includes it.
issues.fix: Delete the header.

issues.title: FairMQLmdSampler.h is installed by default, but the MbsAPI headers it needs are not
issues.description: The header includes f_evt.h, s_bufhe_swap.h and s_filhe_swap.h from MbsAPI. BaseMQ installs it whenever BUILD_BASEMQ is on (the default; fairroot/basemq/CMakeLists.txt:14, 54), but MbsAPI and its headers are built and installed only with BUILD_MBS, which is off by default (CMakeLists.txt:126, fairroot/CMakeLists.txt:30-32, fairroot/mbsapi/CMakeLists.txt:69). In a default installation the installed header does not compile.
issues.fix: Install devices/FairMQLmdSampler.h only when BUILD_MBS is on.

issues.title: FairMQLmdSampler passes a subevent size in 32-bit words where bytes are expected
issues.description: ReadEvent() builds the data part with NewMessage(fEventData, sebuflength, ...). f_evt_get_subevent() returns sebuflength as a count of 32-bit longwords (f_evt.c:246), but NewMessage() takes bytes, so the message carries only a quarter of the subevent. FairMQUnpacker::Run() then passes the same word count to DoUnpack() (FairMQUnpacker.h:118-127), which reads up to four times more data than the message holds.
issues.fix: Pass sebuflength * sizeof(int) as the message size.
issues.evidence: f_evt_get_subevent() returns l_dlen/2-1, a count of 32-bit longwords (f_evt.c:246; l_dlen is in 16-bit words, s_ves10_1.h), and FairMQLmdSampler.h:223 and 258-260 pass that count as the message size in bytes. FairMQUnpacker::Run passes the same count to DoUnpack (FairMQUnpacker.h:118-127), which reads that many Int_t words (examples/MQ/Lmd/FairMBSUnpacker.cxx:46-49). So it reads 4x the bytes received, which is a heap over-read and gives garbage hits. Note that this code needs BUILD_MBS=ON, and MbsAPI is deprecated and off by default (CMakeLists.txt:126, CHANGELOG.md:99-101).

issues.title: FairMQLmdSampler sends MbsAPI buffer memory zero-copy with an empty deleter
issues.description: The data part points into the MbsAPI read buffer and has a deleter that does nothing. With the zeromq transport (the default, used by examples/MQ/Lmd), NewMessage() does not copy the data, and the I/O thread sends it later. The next f_evt_get_event() can refill that buffer, and Close() frees it in f_evt_get_close(), so queued messages can send overwritten or freed memory.
issues.fix: Copy the subevent into a message that owns its memory (NewMessage(size) and memcpy) before the next read.

issues.title: FairMQUnpacker::AddSubEvtKey() has a warning that can never fire
issues.description: The else branch runs only when fSubEventChanMap is empty, so fSubEventChanMap.count(fInputChannelName) is always 0 and the warning never prints. Its text also names the wrong class ('FairMQLmdSampler'), copied from the sampler.
issues.fix: Remove the dead check.

issues.title: Boost load() for FairMCPoint stores the energy loss with SetLength()
issues.description: load() reads the energy loss from the archive and passes it to SetLength() instead of SetEnergyLoss(). After a Boost round trip, the point's length holds the energy loss, and its energy loss keeps the old value of the target object (0 for a new point, FairMCPoint.cxx:21). save() writes both fields correctly, so only reading is wrong.
issues.fix: Call mcPoint.SetEnergyLoss(energyLoss) at line 57.
issues.evidence: Line 57 calls mcPoint.SetLength(energyLoss), which overwrites the length set on line 53, and SetEnergyLoss (FairMCPoint.h:70) is never called. save() writes GetLength() and GetEnergyLoss() (lines 74-75), so after each Boost round trip fLength holds the energy loss and fELoss keeps the target's old value (0 for a new point, FairMCPoint.cxx:21). The header is installed and documented as an opt-in API (basemq/CMakeLists.txt:20, CHANGELOG.md:206-215), but no in-tree code deserializes FairMCPoint with Boost yet.

issues.title: Unused trait fair::base::serialization::has_BoostSerialization
issues.description: The trait has_BoostSerialization (lines 41-60) is not used anywhere in FairRoot, its examples or templates. It is in an installed header, so downstream code may still use it.
issues.fix: Deprecate and remove the trait, or use it in a static_assert in BoostSerializer.

issues.title: BoostSerializer::Serialize() copies the archive twice and keeps its size in an int
issues.description: Each Serialize() overload calls buffer.str() twice, once for the length and once for the data, and each call copies the whole archive. The size is kept in an int, so an archive larger than 2 GiB would pass a wrong size to Rebuild() and memcpy().
issues.fix: Call buffer.str() once into a local std::string and use size_t for the size.

issues.title: BoostSerializer.h uses std::memcpy without including <cstring>
issues.description: Serialize() calls std::memcpy (lines 77, 87, 97), but the header does not include <cstring> (includes at lines 19-35). It compiles today only because another header includes it.
issues.fix: Add #include <cstring>.

issues.title: BoostSerializer::Serialize() takes std::unique_ptr<TClonesArray> by value and deletes it
issues.description: This overload takes the unique_ptr by value, so the caller must std::move the array into it, and the array is destroyed when Serialize() returns. RootSerializer takes const std::unique_ptr<T>&, so code written for one serialization policy does not compile with the other, and the obvious fix (std::move) loses the array.
issues.fix: Take const std::unique_ptr<TClonesArray>& as RootSerializer does.

issues.title: BoostSerializer::Deserialize() handles archive errors inconsistently
issues.description: Deserialize(msg, DataType&) creates the binary_iarchive outside its try block, so a bad header (for example an empty message or a wrong signature) still throws. An error in the body is caught and only logged, and the void function gives the caller no way to see that the object is incomplete. The vector and TClonesArray overloads catch nothing, so the same error throws there.
issues.fix: Use one policy for all overloads: let archive exceptions propagate, or report failure through a return value.

issues.title: RootSerializer::Serialize() sends the TMessage buffer capacity, not the data length
issues.description: Both Serialize() overloads pass tm->BufferSize(), the allocated buffer size, to msg.Rebuild() instead of tm->Length(), the bytes written. A TMessage buffer starts at 1032 bytes and doubles when it grows, so a message can be up to about twice as large as its data. For small objects the extra bytes are uninitialized heap memory that is sent over the network.
issues.fix: Pass tm->Length() to msg.Rebuild().

issues.title: RootSerializer::Deserialize() casts the read object to T* without a class check
issues.description: All three Deserialize functions call ReadObjectAny(tm.GetClass()), which uses the class stored in the message, and static_cast the result to T*. If the message holds another class, the caller gets a wrongly typed pointer instead of nullptr, and ROOT applies no base-class offset. Deserialize(msg, T*&) also deletes the object the pointer refers to first (line 62), so the pointer must own its object or be nullptr.
issues.fix: Pass TClass::GetClass<T>() to ReadObjectAny(), so ROOT checks the class, adjusts the pointer and returns nullptr on a mismatch.

issues.title: Comment on test_prefix says it prefixes all test executables
issues.description: The comment says test_prefix 'Shall be prefixed to all test executables', but only fairroot/tools/tests/CMakeLists.txt uses it. Suites made with fairroot_add_catch2_test_suite() are named test_<suite>, and fairroot_discover_catch2_tests() (cmake/private/FairRootTargets.cmake:61-63) uses a local variable of the same name for the Catch2 TEST_PREFIX, with another meaning.
issues.fix: Reword the comment to name its real scope, or apply the prefix in fairroot_add_catch2_test_suite().

excerpt.code:
################################################################################

# Shall be prefixed to all test executables
set(test_prefix fairroot_test)

add_subdirectory(tools)

issues.title: FairMCDataCrawler::GetNextStage() leaks the cloned entry of every followed link
issues.description: GetEntry() returns FairRootManager::GetCloneOfLinkData(), a new Clone() that the caller owns (FairRootManager.cxx:569). GetNextStage() keeps it in tempStage, recurses, and never deletes it, so each GetInfo() call leaks one object per followed link. FairMCMatch::RemoveStage() (FairMCMatch.cxx:82) also erases a stage from fList without deleting it.
issues.fix: Hold the clone in a std::unique_ptr in GetNextStage(), and delete the stage in RemoveStage() before erasing it.

issues.title: datamatch link containers keep InsertHistory() on and collect extra links
issues.description: FairMultiLinkedData turns fInsertHistory on by default, and datamatch never turns it off. So fFinalStageML in AddToFinalStage(), the FairMCEntry objects filled by FairMCObject::AddLink() (FairMCObject.cxx:63) and SetEntry(), and the crawler's fFinalStage (FairMCDataCrawler.cxx:251) run InsertHistory() on every AddLink(). For a target in memory this also copies all links of that object, so results hold links beyond the stop stage and duplicate links whose weights add up. FairMultiLinkedData_Interface turns history off when it copies links (FairMultiLinkedData_Interface.cxx:45, 56).
issues.fix: Call SetInsertHistory(kFALSE) on these containers, for example in the FairMCEntry constructors and for fFinalStageML and fFinalStage.

issues.title: FairMCMatch::ClearMCList() drops all stages, so the match tasks produce no results
issues.description: ClearMCList() clears each stage and then calls fList.clear(), which drops all stages from the map without deleting them. FairMCMatchCreatorTask::Exec() and FairMCMatchLoaderTask::Exec() call it at the start of every event, but the stages are created only once, in Init() through InitDataStages(). From the first event on GetNMCStages() is 0, so MCLink stays empty, GetMCInfo() returns empty results, and the stages leak. Correction: Removing fList.clear() alone is not a full fix. fList[type] in GetEntry() (FairMCMatch.cxx:337) and in GetMCStageType() (FairMCMatch.h:98) can add null stages, for example during the selector's GetMCInfo() call. The creator loop (FairMCMatchCreatorTask.cxx:101), FindLinksToStage() (FairMCMatch.cxx:237) and LoadInMCLists() (FairMCMatch.cxx:379-381) use these stages without a null check. The fix should clear the entries of the non-null stages and erase only the null ones with iter = fList.erase(iter).
issues.fix: Remove fList.clear() (or erase only null entries if that was its purpose).
issues.evidence: ClearMCList() ends with fList.clear() (FairMCMatch.cxx:362). Both tasks call it at the start of each Exec() (FairMCMatchCreatorTask.cxx:96, FairMCMatchLoaderTask.cxx:110), but the stages are made only in Init() (creator line 39, loader line 33). From the first event, GetNMCStages() is 0 (FairMCMatch.h:77), so the creator loops (lines 100-124) add nothing to MCLink, GetMCInfo() returns early (FairMCMatch.cxx:102-104), and the destructor (lines 35-37) no longer deletes the stages. The defect is real, but DataMatch is deprecated (FairMCMatch.h:18-20) and no example or test uses these tasks, so I rate it medium.

issues.title: InitStage() parameter names in FairMCMatch.h are swapped against the definition
issues.description: The header declares InitStage(const std::string& fileName, const std::string& branchName = ""), but FairMCMatch.cxx:67 defines InitStage(branchName, fileName) and uses the first argument as the branch name. A caller who follows the header passes the file name as the branch name and gets only the warning 'Branch name ... not persistant!'.
issues.fix: Rename the header parameters to (branchName, fileName = "").

issues.title: FairMCMatch::GetMCStageType(TString) never finds the stage of branch ID 0
issues.description: GetMCStageType(TString) returns a stage only if GetBranchId(branch) > 0. FairRootManager::GetBranchId() counts from 0 and returns -1 for an unknown name (FairRootManager.cxx:264-277), so the first registered branch always gets nullptr. InitStage() and CreateArtificialStage() in the same class correctly test > -1.
issues.fix: Test GetBranchId(branch) >= 0, and call GetBranchId() only once.

issues.title: FairMCMatch inserts null stages via std::map::operator[] and later dereferences them
issues.description: GetMCStageType(Int_t) returns fList[type], and GetEntry() (FairMCMatch.cxx:337) tests fList[type] == 0, so a lookup of a type without a stage inserts a null entry. Code that walks all stages then dereferences it: operator<< (FairMCMatch.h:111-116), FindLinksToStage() (FairMCMatch.cxx:236-238), FindStagesPointingToLink() (FairMCMatch.cxx:225), and LoadInMCLists(), whose IsTypeInList() is true for the null entry. FairMCMatchSelectorTask::SetWeights() (FairMCMatchSelectorTask.cxx:96) calls SetWeight() on the returned pointer without a check; while ClearMCList() empties the map, this crashes for every type passed to SetWeightStage().
issues.fix: Look stages up with fList.find() in GetMCStageType() and GetEntry(), and check the result in SetWeights().

issues.title: datamatch static_casts FairMultiLinkedData_Interface objects to FairMultiLinkedData
issues.description: FairMCMatchCreatorTask::Exec() (line 104) and FairMCDataCrawler::GetEntry() (FairMCDataCrawler.cxx:123) static_cast branch objects to FairMultiLinkedData*. FairMCPoint, FairTimeStamp and FairHit derive from the sibling class FairMultiLinkedData_Interface, so the cast is invalid, and the next virtual call (GetLinks(), GetNLinks()) uses the wrong vtable slot: undefined behavior, in practice garbage or a crash. The crawler path runs today; the creator-task loop runs only once ClearMCList() is fixed. The bypass branch of FairMultiLinkedData::AddLink() (FairMultiLinkedData.cxx:166) has the same cast, but no FairRoot caller reaches it. Correction: The fix must also handle a null GetPointerToLinks(). It is null when the object holds no links, for example when FairRootManager::GetUseFairLinks() is false (FairMultiLinkedData_Interface.cxx:64-75), so the fix must treat null as zero links.
issues.fix: Check for FairMultiLinkedData_Interface (InheritsFrom() or dynamic_cast) and use GetPointerToLinks(), as FairMultiLinkedData::InsertHistory() already does.
issues.evidence: Both casts exist (FairMCMatchCreatorTask.cxx:104, FairMCDataCrawler.cxx:123). FairMCPoint, FairTimeStamp and FairHit derive from FairMultiLinkedData_Interface, which derives from TObject next to FairMultiLinkedData, not from it (FairMCPoint.h:21, FairTimeStamp.h:22, FairMultiLinkedData_Interface.h:22). The crawler then makes the virtual call tempStage->GetNLinks() (FairMCDataCrawler.cxx:205), which is undefined behavior; a mock with the same class shapes crashed with SIGSEGV (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8ce3faed-3785-59d4-9dc9-2418f32b8a1f/scratchpad/issues/work-high-05/castdemo.cxx). The creator loop is dead today because of the ClearMCList() bug, and no caller reaches the AddLink() bypass branch (FairMultiLinkedData.cxx:158-172), because every caller that passes bypass=true has the persistence check turned off. The bug is real, but only in the deprecated DataMatch library, which nothing in the tree uses, so I rate it medium.

issues.title: 42 C/C++ files in fairroot/, examples/ and templates/ have no license header
issues.description: 42 of the 966 .h, .cxx, .C and .c files under fairroot/, examples/ and templates/ contain no license or copyright text. Examples are all 12 files in fairroot/eventdisplay/datasource/, fairroot/alignment/FairAlignmentHandler.cxx, fairroot/base/event/FairMultiLinkedData_Interface.cxx and run_sim.C/eventDisplay.C of both project templates. Only the 'Files: *' paragraph of COPYRIGHT covers them, while the other files carry the LGPL header.
issues.fix: Add the standard LGPL header to these files.

issues.title: FairTimebasedMC(Hit)Source::Init() tests a result that is always kSUCCESS
issues.description: Init() logs 'Branch EventTimes not present' when FairGetEventTime::Init() fails, but that function always returns kSUCCESS (FairGetEventTime.cxx:24-41). For a source that is not kFILE it silently keeps an empty time list, so RetrieveData() never finds an event and the display stays empty without an error. FairTimebasedMCHitSource.cxx:27-28 has the same check, and its fEventTime member is set but never read.
issues.fix: Return kERROR from FairGetEventTime::Init() when it cannot fill the time list, and fix the message.

issues.title: FairTimebasedMC(Hit)Source comment gives the wrong sign for holdTime
issues.description: The RetrieveData() comment says it 'deletes data which is older than time + holdTime'. RemoveOldTracks() deletes data older than time - holdTime (FairTimebasedDataHandlerT.h:136, 154). FairTimebasedMCHitSource.h:30 has the same wrong comment.
issues.fix: Change the comment to 'older than time - holdTime'.

issues.title: FairTimebasedSource constructor swaps windowMinus and windowPlus
issues.description: The constructor stores windowMinus in fTimeWindowPlus and windowPlus in fTimeWindowMinus. RetrieveData() reads data in [time - fTimeWindowMinus, time + fTimeWindowPlus] (FairTimebasedSource.cxx:24-25), so windowMinus sets the window after the event time and windowPlus the window before it. The member comments at lines 36-37 are swapped too.
issues.fix: Initialize fTimeWindowMinus from windowMinus and fTimeWindowPlus from windowPlus, and fix the comments.

issues.title: FairBoxSetDraw.cxx defines unused globals fq, fX, fY and fZ
issues.description: The file defines 'FairBoxSet* fq;' and 'Double_t fX, fY, fZ;' at file scope. All uses are in member functions, where the members with the same names (FairBoxSetDraw.h:98-101) hide them. The globals only add symbols with external linkage that can clash with other code.
issues.fix: Delete lines 29-30.

issues.title: RPhi and RhoZ views are not projections: the projection managers stay empty
issues.description: Init() creates fRPhiProjManager and fRhoZProjManager and their axes, but nothing calls ImportElements(), and the managers are only added to the list tree, not to a scene. 'RPhi View' and 'RhoZ View' show the unprojected 3D scenes through orthographic cameras; the default RhoZ camera kCameraOrthoZOY (line 66) gives a z-y side view, not a rho-z projection. The projection axes belong to the empty managers.
issues.fix: Import the global and event scenes into the projection managers and show those, or rename the views and drop the unused managers.

issues.title: AddParticlesToPdgDataBase() gives the stable Alpha the decay width of the triton
issues.description: The Alpha entry is marked stable (kTRUE) but gets the width khShGev / (12.33 * kYear2Sec), the triton half-life copied from the line above. ROOT's own PDG table has no light ions, so this entry is the one the event display uses.
issues.fix: Give Alpha a width of 0.

issues.title: SetRPhiPlane() and SetRhoZPlane() store plane equations that are never used
issues.description: The clip-plane calls in SetViewers() are commented out, so fRPhiPlane and fRhoZPlane are written but never read. SetRPhiPlane() and SetRhoZPlane() document a plane equation Ax+By+Cz+D=0 (FairEventManager.h:59, 68), but only their camera-type argument has an effect. The propagator example passes a plane that changes nothing (examples/advanced/propagator/macros/eventDisplay.C:51).
issues.fix: Restore the clip-plane calls, or document that only the camera type is used.

issues.title: LoadXMLSettings() and LoadXMLDetector() crash when an XML attribute is missing
issues.description: Both functions call GetAttrib(name)->GetValue() without a null check (lines 313-314, 324, 326, 329-330, 338-339, 354), and GetAttrib() returns nullptr for a missing attribute. A <detector> without name, recursive, transparency or color, or an <mctrack> without pdg or color, crashes the event display, although the code treats an empty value as 'not set'. FairXMLPdgColor::SetColorsFromXML() has the same pattern.
issues.fix: Check each GetAttrib() result and treat a missing attribute like an empty value.

issues.title: FairEventManager::SwitchBackground(Bool_t) ignores its argument
issues.description: SwitchBackground() only toggles the color set with SwitchColorSet(), but the header says the argument means 'use white if true' (FairEventManager.h:100-101). The editor's check box stays in sync because it toggles once per click, but a program that calls SwitchBackground(kTRUE) twice gets the dark background back.
issues.fix: Choose the light or dark color set from the argument, or fix the documentation.

issues.title: GetEvtTime() and SetEvtTime() narrow the absolute event time in ns to Float_t
issues.description: fTimeEvent is a Double_t, but GetEvtTime() returns Float_t and SetEvtTime() takes Float_t (line 113). A float holds whole nanoseconds only up to 2^24 ns (about 16.8 ms), so later event times are rounded to steps of 2 ns, 4 ns and more. In time-based runs FairGetEventTime::GetEvent() and the data sources get the rounded time, and a time rounded down can select the previous event.
issues.fix: Use Double_t for GetEvtTime() and SetEvtTime().

issues.title: 'Current Event' accepts one entry past the end, and navigation has no range check
issues.description: The TGNumberEntry is limited to [0, Entries], but the last valid entry is Entries - 1. GotoEvent(), NextEvent() and PrevEvent() (FairEventManager.cxx:177-199) do not check the range, and FairRunAna::RunSingleEntry() ignores the failed read. The display then shows stale data under an invalid event number, for example after Next on the last event or Prev on event 0.
issues.fix: Limit the field to Entries - 1 and clamp the entry number in GotoEvent(), NextEvent() and PrevEvent().

issues.title: Event-by-event animation: SetTimeLimits(0, -1) is undone by GotoEvent()
issues.description: StartAnimation() calls SetTimeLimits(0, -1) to disable drawing by time slice, but each SelectEvent() calls GotoEvent(), which resets the limits to 0 and DBL_MAX (FairEventManager.cxx:180-181). The animation therefore draws like normal navigation. The SetAnimatedTracks(kFALSE) call is also without effect, because no draw class reads GetDrawAnimatedTracks().
issues.fix: Remove both calls, or let GotoEvent() keep limits that the caller set.

issues.title: FairHitDraw declares GetTime(TObject*) but never defines or uses it
issues.description: FairHitDraw.h declares 'double GetTime(TObject* obj);', but FairHitDraw.cxx has no definition and nothing calls it. It is not virtual in FairBoxSetDraw, so it overrides nothing, and any call would fail at link time.
issues.fix: Remove the declaration.

issues.title: FairPointSetDraw::SetUseTimeOffset() has no effect: the offset is always 0
issues.description: Exec() declares a local timeOffset = 0.0 and adds it to each point time when fUseTimeOffset is set (lines 98-99), so the addition does nothing. The comment says the offset should turn a time of flight into event time plus time of flight, but no code computes it.
issues.fix: Compute the offset from the event time, or remove timeOffset and SetUseTimeOffset().

issues.title: FairXMLNode::Copy() keeps XML comments as children, which crashes the XML loaders
issues.description: Copy() skips only child nodes named 'text', so an XML comment becomes a child FairXMLNode named 'comment' without attributes. LoadXMLSettings() and LoadXMLDetector() treat every child as an element and call GetAttrib(...)->GetValue() on it. A comment inside <MCTracksColors> or a <detector>, or before the first <detector>, therefore dereferences a null pointer.
issues.fix: Copy only element nodes (GetNodeType() == TXMLNode::kXMLElementNode) as children.

issues.title: FairXMLNode::Copy() drops the last child when it is an element node
issues.description: The do/while loop moves to the next child and then tests HasNextNode() of that child, so it never processes the last child of an element with two or more children. Pretty-printed files work by chance, because TDOMParser keeps the whitespace text node after the last element, and Copy() skips text nodes. Compact XML such as loses , so the last detector or color entry of such a file is silently ignored.
issues.fix: Loop with for (child = node->GetChildren(); child; child = child->GetNextNode()).

issues.title: FairXMLFile ignores ParseFile() errors and dereferences a null document
issues.description: The read constructor does not check the return value of TDOMParser::ParseFile(). For a missing or malformed file, GetXMLDocument() returns nullptr, and line 142 calls GetRootNode() on it. FairEventManager::Init() therefore crashes with a segmentation fault, not an error message, when SetXMLConfig() names a wrong path.
issues.fix: Check the ParseFile() result and the document pointer, log an error and leave the root node empty, and let LoadXMLSettings() stop on an empty root node.

issues.title: FairEveGeoTracks::Init() reads and logs every input entry, also in event-based runs
issues.description: Init() always calls FairGetEventTime::Instance().Init(). For a file source, that reads every entry of the input once and logs one info line per entry (FairGetEventTime.cxx:29-35), but Repaint() uses the event times only in time-based runs (line 159). Event displays of large files therefore start slowly and flood the log.
issues.fix: Call FairGetEventTime::Init() only when FairRunAna::Instance()->IsTimeStamp() is true, and log the times at debug level.

issues.title: DrawAnimatedTrack() drops points at exactly fTMin, so primary tracks miss the vertex
issues.description: The loop keeps a point as 'previous' only if t < fTMin and draws it only if t > fTMin && t < fTMax, so a point with t == fTMin is lost. GotoEvent() sets the limits to [0, DBL_MAX], and primaries usually start at t = 0 (PreTrack() adds the vertex point, and FairPrimaryGenerator::AddTrack() defaults tof to 0). In event-based runs every primary track therefore starts at its second point instead of the vertex.
issues.fix: Use inclusive limits (t >= fTMin && t <= fTMax) for drawn points.

issues.title: FairEveGeoTracks::Repaint() reads fContainer with handler indices when fTMin > fTMax
issues.description: In time-based runs nTracks is the size of fGeoTrackHandler's data (lines 176-177), but when fTMin > fTMax the loop calls DrawTrack(iTrack), which reads fContainer->UncheckedAt(iTrack) (line 67). With SetClearHandler(kFALSE) the handler holds tracks of several events, so the index runs past the current event's array. No GUI path reaches this today, because GotoEvent() resets the limits, but it is the branch that the editor's event-by-event animation means to use.
issues.fix: In this branch, draw the handler's TGeoTrack (GetData()[iTrack].first), for example by passing the track pointer to DrawTrack().

issues.title: FairFastSimModel::DoIt() crashes when the model neither moved nor stopped the particle
issues.description: The stack sets the moved index to -1 for a stopped particle and keeps -2 when FastSimProcessParticle() neither moved nor stopped it (FastSimClearMovedIndex(), FairGenericStack.h:184). DoIt() tests only movedParticleIndex != -1, so for -2 it calls particles->At(-2), which returns nullptr, and line 122 dereferences it. A user model that skips some particles or only adds secondaries crashes; the shipped examples always move the particle.
issues.fix: Test movedParticleIndex >= 0.

issues.title: FairFastSimModel::DoIt() converts times with a factor 1e10 instead of 1e9
issues.description: DoIt() converts TParticle::T() with the factor 10.e9 (= 1e10) for the moved particle (line 125) and for each secondary (line 104). The stack holds VMC times in seconds (the example passes TrackTime(), and detector code converts with TrackTime() * 1.0e09), and Geant4 works in ns, so the factor must be 1e9.
