Geant4 therefore continues these tracks with times 10 times too large, and all their later hits get wrong times. The comment 'change from ns to s' is also backwards.
issues.fix: Multiply by 1e9 (CLHEP::second) in both places and correct the comment.
issues.evidence: Lines 104 and 125 multiply TParticle::T() by 10.e9, which is 1e10 (I checked this with a small compiled program). The stack holds the time in seconds: the example passes TrackTime() and fPos.T() (FairFastSimExample.cxx:79-90, FairFastSimExample2.cxx:76), FairStack stores the time unchanged (FairStack.cxx:115), and detectors convert TrackTime() to ns with * 1.0e09 (FairTutorialDet1.cxx:61). Geant4 works in ns, so the factor must be 1e9. With 1e10, the moved track and the new secondaries continue with a time 10 times too large, and all their later MC points carry this error. FastSim is a supported Geant4 feature that is not deprecated, and the wrong times are written without any warning, so high is right.

issues.title: FairFastSimModel::DoIt() uses FairTrajFilter::Instance() without a null check
issues.description: After a move, DoIt() calls FairTrajFilter::Instance()->IsAccepted(particle) and GetCurrentTrk(). Instance() returns nullptr unless a FairTrajFilter exists (FairTrajFilter.cxx:32), and FairMCApplication creates one only when SetStoreTraj(kTRUE) is set (FairMCApplication.cxx:857-859); the default is false. So a Geant4 fast-simulation run without stored trajectories crashes at the first moved particle; run_tutorial1_fastsim.C hides this because it stores trajectories. Correction: The fix should also check GetCurrentTrk(). It is nullptr until a track is accepted (FairTrajFilter.cxx:66), and Reset() does not clear it (FairTrajFilter.cxx:83). So it can be null or point to an old track when the moved particle passes the filter but the current track did not.
issues.fix: Check FairTrajFilter::Instance() for nullptr before the call, as FairMCApplication::PreTrack() does with fTrajFilter.
issues.evidence: Instance() returns fgInstance, which stays nullptr until a filter is constructed (FairTrajFilter.cxx:30-32, 73). FairMCApplication makes the filter only when GetStoreTraj() is true (FairMCApplication.cxx:279-281, 857-859), and the default is false (FairRunSim.h:262). With Geant4 and a detector that calls FastSimMoveParticleTo(), DoIt() reaches line 139, and IsAccepted() reads fVxMin through a null this pointer (FairTrajFilter.cxx:92), so the run crashes; run_tutorial1_fastsim.C:114 avoids this only because it calls SetStoreTraj(kTRUE). Other code, such as FairRunAna (FairRunAna.cxx:334), checks Instance() for nullptr first.

issues.title: geane/CMakeLists.txt says FairPropagator comes from FairRoot::Base
issues.description: The comment on the FairRoot::Base line lists FairPropagator, but FairPropagator is built in TrackBase (fairroot/trackbase/CMakeLists.txt:17). The TrackBase line (29) names only FairTrackPar.
issues.fix: Move FairPropagator to the comment of the FairRoot::TrackBase line.

excerpt.code:
target_link_libraries(${target}
  PUBLIC
  FairRoot::Base # FairField, FairTask, FairPropagator
  FairRoot::TrackBase # FairTrackPar

issues.title: FairGeane's UserCuts argument has no effect; Init() resolves a cuts file it never loads
issues.description: Init() looks up the cuts macro (lines 113-117) and logs 'User path for Cuts and Processes (SetCuts.C) is used', but the LoadMacro()/ProcessLine() calls are commented out (lines 125-126). The lookup also tests AbsPath of the config macro and falls back to SetCuts.C, not fUserCuts. GEANE takes its cuts from Geane.C, so the UserCuts constructor argument is silently ignored.
issues.fix: Remove or deprecate the UserCuts argument and the dead lookup, or warn when it is set.

issues.title: FairGeane::Init() crashes when the run has no magnetic field
issues.description: Init() calls FairRunAna::Instance()->GetField() and then field->Print() with no null checks. FairRunAna has a field only after SetField() or a field factory, so a run without a field (or a run that is not a FairRunAna) crashes here. FairGeane::SetField() does not help, because it only prints a warning (lines 140-145).
issues.fix: Check the run and the field for nullptr and stop with a clear LOG(fatal), or skip Print() if field-free propagation should work.

issues.title: FairGeane("Config.C") selects the geometry-import constructor, not the config one
issues.description: A string literal or const char* matches FairGeane(const char* name, TString, TString) exactly, while FairGeane(TString UserConfig, TString UserCuts) needs a conversion. So FairGeane("MyGeane.C") passes the macro to TGeoManager::Import() as a geometry file and keeps the default Geane.C. Only a TString or std::string argument reaches the config constructor (checked with a mock of both signatures).
issues.fix: Give the geometry constructor a distinct signature, for example a named factory function, so a plain string cannot select it by accident.

issues.title: FairGeanePro() static_casts any VMC engine to TGeant3 without a type check
issues.description: The constructor does static_cast<TGeant3*>(TVirtualMC::GetMC()) and only checks for nullptr. With another engine, for example TGeant4, gMC3 is an invalid pointer, line 60 reads gMC3->fErtrio from it, and every later GEANE call works on garbage. The 'throw;' at line 58 is dead code, because LOG(fatal) already throws fair::FatalException.
issues.fix: Use dynamic_cast<TGeant3*>, LOG(fatal) when it returns nullptr, and remove the bare 'throw;'.

excerpt.code:
FairGeanePro::FairGeanePro()
    : FairPropagator("Geane", "Propagate Tracks")
    , gMC3(static_cast<TGeant3*>(TVirtualMC::GetMC()))
    , fPropOption("")
    , nepred(1)

issues.title: FairGeanePro keeps PCA mode after SetDestinationLength() and targets (0,0,0)
issues.description: SetPCAPropagation(1 or 2) sets fPCA, and SetDestinationLength() does not reset it. Propagate(FairTrackParH*, FairTrackParH*) with option 'L' and fPCA != 0 then runs FindPCA() towards fpoint, fwire1 and fwire2 instead of using the length. Only the deprecated SetPoint() and SetWire() set these targets, so with the current API they stay at (0,0,0).
issues.fix: Reset fPCA in SetDestinationLength(), SetDestinationPlane() and SetDestinationVolume(), and let SetPCAPropagation() take the point or wire.

issues.title: Propagate(P,P) says 'to Volume' for length and PCA modes; 'implimented' typo
issues.description: Propagate(FairTrackParP*, FairTrackParP*) prints 'Propagate Parabola parameter to Volume is not implimented yet' for every ProMode 1 setting. SetDestinationLength(), SetPCAPropagation() and BackTrackToVertex() also set ProMode 1, so the text is wrong for them. The message at line 201 has the same typo.
issues.fix: Say that parabola tracks support only plane destinations, and write 'implemented'.

issues.title: FairGeanePro plane-to-plane propagation ignores the start plane stored in TStart
issues.description: Propagate(FairTrackParP*, FairTrackParP*) calls Eufilp(nepred, ein, pli, plo). ein holds TStart's covariance in the SD frame of TStart's own plane, but pli comes from SetOriginPlane() or the constructor default (1,0,0),(0,1,0). Unless the caller first calls SetOriginPlane(TStart->GetJVer(), TStart->GetKVer()), GEANE reads the errors in the wrong frame and the output errors are silently wrong.
issues.fix: Set pli from TStart->GetJVer() and GetKVer() inside Propagate(), as the PCA branch already does at line 328.

issues.title: Propagate(P,P) with option L and fPCA 0 warns but still runs ERTRAK with stale settings
issues.description: For ProMode 3, option 'L' and fPCA == 0, Propagate(FairTrackParP*, FairTrackParP*) logs 'Propagate Parabola to Parabola in Length not yet implemented' but does not return. It calls Propagate(PDG) without Eufill() or Eufilp(), so ERTRAK uses the target and errors of an earlier call and can return true. Only the deprecated PropagateToVirtualPlaneAtPCA(0) and BackTrackToVirtualPlaneAtPCA(0) reach this state.
issues.fix: Return kFALSE after the warning.

issues.title: FairGeanePro::Propagate(float*...) ignores the destination and overwrites xlf
issues.description: The float overload always propagates 1000 cm with option 'L', whatever SetDestinationPlane(), SetDestinationVolume() or SetDestinationLength() set. It stores the 1000 in the member xlf[0], so a later Propagate(FairTrackParH*, FairTrackParH*) with a length destination also uses 1000 cm instead of the user's length.
issues.fix: Use a local length array (or honor the configured destination) and leave xlf unchanged.

issues.title: SetPCAPropagation(pca, 0) logs an error but returns true and keeps a stale option
issues.description: With dir == 0, SetPCAPropagation() logs 'ERROR: no direction set' as a warning. It still sets ProMode = 1 and fPCA, keeps the previous fPropOption (for example 'PE' or 'VE'), and returns kTRUE. The next Propagate() call then mixes PCA mode with the old option.
issues.fix: Return kFALSE for dir == 0 before changing any state.

issues.title: [[deprecated]] messages in FairGeanePro.h misspell 'deprecated' as 'depracated'
issues.description: The 11 [[deprecated(...)]] messages between lines 72 and 160 say 'depracated', and the section comments at lines 70 and 131 say 'Depracated functions'. Compilers show these texts to every user of the functions. The same typo is in fairroot/base/sim/FairModule.h:109 and in the warnings at FairGenericVMCConfig.cxx:28 and 179.
issues.fix: Replace 'depracated' with 'deprecated' in all these places.

issues.title: FairAsciiGenerator aborts with LOG(fatal) at the normal end of the input file
issues.description: ReadEvent() checks fInputFile->fail() right after '>> ntracks'. When the run asks for more events than the file holds, this read hits the end of file, fail() is true, and LOG(fatal) throws instead of stopping the run. The clean branch that closes the file and returns kFALSE (so FairMCApplication calls StopRun()) is reached only for a truncated header; a replica of the read sequence on a two-event file confirms this. Correction: LOG(fatal) throws only when FairRoot's fatal handler is installed, which happens when the macro calls FairLogger::GetLogger() (FairLogger.cxx:37, 201). FairLogger itself only calls a handler if one is set. With no handler, the fatal line is printed, the reads at line 63 do nothing, and the eof() branch at line 66 still closes the file and returns kFALSE. So 'only for a truncated header' is true only when the handler is installed.
issues.fix: Check eof() directly after '>> ntracks' and return kFALSE there; keep LOG(fatal) for a real parse error.
issues.evidence: At the normal end of the file, `>> ntracks` (FairAsciiGenerator.cxx:60) reads nothing, so fail() is true and lines 61-62 log the fatal error before the eof() branch at line 66 runs. I copied the read sequence of lines 59-89 into a small program and ran it on a two-event file. The third call reaches the fatal line whether or not the file ends with a newline, and only a truncated header reaches the clean branch. With FairRoot's fatal handler the exception skips StopRun() and FinishRun() (FairMCApplication.cxx:302-304, 614-622), so the run's output is never written.

issues.title: Fatal message says 'number of events' where the generators read the track count
issues.description: The LOG(fatal) after reading the track count says 'Error reading the number of events from event header.' The same text is at FairShieldGenerator.cxx:76 and 135 and FairUrqmdGenerator.cxx:157 and 305. In all five places the value is the number of tracks in the event.
issues.fix: Change the text to 'Error reading the number of tracks from the event header.'

issues.title: FairAsciiGenerator.h asks for Geant3 particle codes, but the code expects PDG codes
issues.description: The class comment says each track line starts with G3PID, the Geant3 particle code. ReadEvent() passes the value unchanged to AddTrack() as a PDG code, because the conversion at FairAsciiGenerator.cxx:82 is commented out. A file written as documented gets wrong particle types.
issues.fix: Say 'PDG code' in the comment, or restore the Geant3-to-PDG conversion.

excerpt.code:
where NTRACKS is the number of tracks in the event, IEV the event number,
and VX, VY, VZ the event vertex coordinates in cm. The header line is
followed by NTRACKS lines of the format G3PID, PX, PY, PZ, where
G3PID is the Geant3 particle code, and PX, PY, PZ the cartesian
momentum coordinates in GeV.
Derived from FairGenerator.

issues.title: FairAsciiGenerator and FairEvtGenGenerator keep the caller's file-name pointer
issues.description: Both classes store fFileName as a raw const Char_t* to the constructor argument (also FairEvtGenGenerator.h:118). They read it later in the CloseInput() log message (FairAsciiGenerator.cxx:95, also called from the destructor; FairEvtGenGenerator.cxx:179). If the caller passed a temporary such as TString(...).Data(), the message reads freed memory; FairShieldGenerator already stores a std::string.
issues.fix: Store the file name as std::string in both classes.

issues.title: FairBoxGenerator() leaves phi range 0..0 and multiplicity 0 without a warning
issues.description: Unlike FairBoxGenerator(pdg, mult), the default constructor does not call SetPhiRange(), so all particles get phi = 0 unless the user sets a range. Its multiplicity is 0, so FairBaseMCGenerator::Init() returns kFALSE; FairPrimaryGenerator::Init() ignores that result, and the generator silently produces nothing.
issues.fix: Call SetPhiRange() in the default constructor, and let FairPrimaryGenerator::Init() report a generator whose Init() fails.

excerpt.code:
#include <cstdio>   // for printf

FairBoxGenerator::FairBoxGenerator()
    : FairBaseMCGenerator()
    , fPtMin(0)
    , fPtMax(0)
    , fPhiMin(0)
    , fPhiMax(0)
    , fEtaMin(0)
    , fEtaMax(0)
    , fYMin(0)
    , fYMax(0)
    , fPMin(0)
    , fPMax(0)
    , fThetaMin(0)
    , fThetaMax(0)
    , fEkinMin(0)
    , fEkinMax(0)
    , fEtaRangeIsSet(0)
    , fYRangeIsSet(0)
    , fThetaRangeIsSet(0)
    , fCosThetaIsSet(0)
    , fPtRangeIsSet(0)
    , fPRangeIsSet(0)
    , fEkinRangeIsSet(0)

issues.title: FairBoxGenerator makes zero-momentum particles with SetPRange() but no angle range
issues.description: ReadEvent() turns pabs into pz and pt only inside the theta/eta branch. With SetPRange() or SetEkinRange() but no SetThetaRange() or SetEtaRange(), every particle gets p = (0,0,0); with SetPtRange() alone, pz stays 0. Init() rejects conflicting ranges but does not report missing ones.
issues.fix: In Init(), LOG(fatal) when a P or Ekin range has no theta or eta range, and warn when pz would always be 0.

issues.title: FairBoxGenerator::SetDebug() is empty, but example macros still call SetDebug(kTRUE)
issues.description: SetDebug() has an empty body (L117-121) and is kept only for backward compatibility. The Tutorial1 macros (run_tutorial1.C:111, run_tutorial1_binary.C:107, run_tutorial1_pythia6.C:100, run_tutorial1_pythia8.C:100, run_tutorial1_mesh.C:95, run_tutorial1_fastsim.C:102) and the propagator macros (runMM.C:86 and 95, runMC.C:95) still call SetDebug(kTRUE). This suggests debug output that never comes. The comment also says 'please user FairLogger' instead of 'please use'.
issues.fix: Remove the SetDebug(kTRUE) calls from the macros, mark SetDebug() [[deprecated]], and fix the comment typo.

issues.title: FairEvtGenGenerator gas-target mode gives each particle its own random vertex
issues.description: In gas-target mode (the constructor with Rsigma and a density TF1), ReadEvent() draws the beam-spot offset and the z offset from fDensityFunction inside the per-particle loop. So each final-state particle of one event starts at a different random vertex. All particles of one event should share one smeared vertex.
issues.fix: Draw the x, y and z offsets once per event, before the track loop, and add the same offsets to every particle.
issues.evidence: The loop at FairEvtGenGenerator.cxx:107-151 runs once for each particle line. For each final-state particle (line 131), lines 138-146 draw a new Gaus radius, a new Circle() point and a new fDensityFunction->GetRandom() value. So particles of one event get different origins, even daughters that share the same x, y, z in the file. AddTrack() only adds the common event vertex (FairPrimaryGenerator.cxx:301-304), and the gas mode is a public constructor (FairEvtGenGenerator.h:103-105).

issues.title: FairIonGenerator(name, ...) leaves fIon null for a FairParticle; ReadEvent() crashes
issues.description: If the name matches a user particle (FairParticle) and not a user ion, the constructor sets the momenta but leaves fIon == nullptr. ReadEvent() then calls fIon->GetName() (line 159), and SetExcitationEnergy() and SetMass() (lines 144, 149) also dereference fIon. So this branch crashes at the first event.
issues.fix: Keep the particle's PDG code for this branch and use it in ReadEvent(), or LOG(fatal) when the name is not a FairIon.
issues.evidence: When the name is found only among the user particles, fIon stays nullptr (FairIonGenerator.cxx:60, 67-74), and the check at line 76 passes because part is set. FairBaseMCGenerator::Init() does not block it (FairBaseMCGenerator.cxx:56-67), so ReadEvent() dereferences the null fIon at line 159, and SetExcitationEnergy() and SetMass() do the same at lines 144 and 149. I lowered the severity to medium because the header documents this constructor only for a pre-defined FairIon (FairIonGenerator.h:33-41) and no example uses a FairParticle. The crash also happens at the first event, so no wrong data is written without notice.

issues.title: FairIonGenerator divides by 0.92827231, a typo for the proton mass 0.93827231
issues.description: For a FairParticle, the constructor converts the per-nucleon momentum with GetMass()/0.92827231. The proton mass is 0.93827231 GeV, so the momentum comes out about 1.1% too high. Today the error is hidden only because this branch crashes later in ReadEvent() (null fIon, see the high-severity issue).
issues.fix: Use the proton mass from TDatabasePDG, as FairIon does.

issues.title: FairIonGenerator::SetCharge() has no effect
issues.description: SetCharge() stores the value in fQ, but nothing reads fQ, and the copy constructor resets it to 0. The ion keeps the charge given to its FairIon at construction, and the user gets no warning.
issues.fix: Remove SetCharge() and fQ, or apply the charge to the FairIon (which needs a setter) before the ions are registered.

issues.title: FairShieldGenerator::RegisterIons() loops forever on a malformed input file
issues.description: The ion scan in the constructor loops on while (!fInputFile.eof()) and never checks fail(). A non-numeric token sets failbit without eofbit, every later read does nothing, and the loop never ends (reproduced with a replica of the loop). The locals nTracks, iPid, iMass and iCharge are not initialized, so after a failed read, also at the normal end of file, line 134 reads an indeterminate nTracks.
issues.fix: Loop on successful extraction of the event header, initialize the locals, and LOG(fatal) on a parse error.

issues.title: FairUrqmdGenerator::ReadEvent() computes ee, aa and pp but never uses them
issues.description: After the boost to the lab frame, ReadEvent() computes ee and fills a TVector3 aa and a TLorentzVector pp. None of them is used; AddTrack() gets only px, py and pz.
issues.fix: Delete lines 226-233.

issues.title: FairUrqmdGenerator's default table $VMCWORKDIR/input/urqmd_pdg.dat does not exist
issues.description: Without a table argument, ReadConversionTable() opens $VMCWORKDIR/input/urqmd_pdg.dat. In FairRoot, VMCWORKDIR is the examples directory, the table is at examples/common/input/urqmd_pdg.dat, and the install rule (examples/CMakeLists.txt:58-62) does not install common/input. So in a plain FairRoot setup the one-argument constructor always ends with 'Could not open Urqmd->PDG input file' (line 337).
issues.fix: Also search $VMCWORKDIR/common/input, install the table, and document the expected path.

issues.title: ReadConversionTable() loops forever when the UrQMD-to-PDG table cannot be opened
issues.description: When the table file cannot be opened, ReadConversionTable() logs LOG(fatal) (L336-338) but does not return. LOG(fatal) does not stop the program by default, and the loop while (!pdgconv->eof()) (L344) never ends, because a stream that failed to open never sets eofbit; a small test program confirmed this. The one-argument constructor looks for $VMCWORKDIR/input/urqmd_pdg.dat. That path does not exist in FairRoot (the file is in examples/common/input), so new FairUrqmdGenerator(file) hangs in its constructor.
issues.fix: Return right after the fatal message, and read the table with while (*pdgconv >> index >> pdgId) instead of testing eof().

issues.title: FairYPtGenerator::Init() skips the last pT bin in its negative-content check
issues.description: The check loops with j < GetNbinsY(), so pT bin GetNbinsY() is never tested. A negative entry there escapes the LOG(fatal), and GetRandom2() later samples a histogram with a negative bin.
issues.fix: Loop with j <= GetNbinsY().

issues.title: FairYPtGenerator gives pz >= 0 to every particle, so negative rapidity goes forward
issues.description: ReadEvent() computes pz = Sign(e/2, y) * exp(-y) * (exp(2y) - 1), where e is the transverse mass mT. The factor exp(-y)*(exp(2y)-1) = 2 sinh(y) already has the sign of y, so Sign() applies it twice and pz = mT*|sinh(y)|. Bins with y < 0 therefore produce forward particles: a numeric check for a pion with pT = 0.5 GeV/c and y = -2 gives pz = +1.88 instead of -1.88.
issues.fix: Use pz = mT * TMath::SinH(y).
issues.evidence: Line 71 sets e = sqrt(pt^2 + m^2), which is mT. Line 73 multiplies Sign(e/2, y) by exp(-y)(exp(2y)-1) = 2 sinh(y), so pz = mT*|sinh(y)| and is never negative. I ran a copy of line 73 in a small program: for a pi+ with pT = 0.5 GeV/c and y = -2 it gives pz = +1.8828, but mT*sinh(y) = -1.8828. FairBoxGenerator uses pz = mt*SinH(y) (FairBoxGenerator.cxx:203), and the Rutherford example fills a histogram whose y axis goes from -2 to 2 (run_rutherford.C:111), so negative y is a normal input.

issues.title: FairGeoAsciiIo::read(FairGeoSet*) returns kTRUE even when the read failed
issues.description: read(FairGeoSet*, FairGeoMedia*) ignores the result of set->read() and always returns kTRUE. FairGeoLoader::LoadAndCreate() (FairGeoLoader.h:75-78), used by FairModule::ConstructASCIIGeometry(), then calls create() after errors such as 'Medium ... not found' or 'Failed for module ...'. The run continues with only the volumes read before the error.
issues.fix: Return the result of set->read(), and let FairGeoMedia::read() (now void) return a status too.

issues.title: Shape readPoints() functions ignore sscanf() results and accept broken point lines
issues.description: readPoints() reads each point with sscanf(buf, '%lf%lf%lf', ...) into uninitialized x, y, z and never checks the result. An empty or short line keeps the previous values (indeterminate for the first point), and an extra empty line shifts the following points and the transform, all without a message. The shape-specific readPoints() (FairGeoTube, FairGeoCons, FairGeoPcon, FairGeoPgon and others) do the same; Pcon and Pgon also use an unchecked point count n.
issues.fix: Check the sscanf() return value, log the volume name, and return 0 so readVolumeParams() fails.

issues.title: MakeGeoBuilder() calls exit(0) for 'G3Native' and returns null for unknown names
issues.description: For the loader name 'G3Native', which FairRunSim::SetGeoModel() accepts with TGeant3, the library prints an info line and calls exit(0). A batch job then stops early with a success code. Any other name that does not start with 'TGeo' gives a null builder without a message, and later code such as FairModule::ReAssignMediaId() dereferences it.
issues.fix: Replace exit(0) with LOG(fatal), and also LOG(fatal) for unknown loader names.

issues.title: FairGeoMedia::read() loops forever when a medium entry lacks a value
issues.description: read() loops on while (!fin.eof()), and neither it nor FairGeoMedium::read() checks fail(). When an entry lacks a value, the next medium name is read as a number, failbit is set, and all later reads do nothing. buf keeps the old name, so the loop adds empty media with that name forever (reproduced with a replica of both functions on tests/geobase/data/testmedia.geo).
issues.fix: Check the stream after each medium, LOG(fatal) with the medium name on failure, and stop the loop.

issues.title: FairGeoNode leaves labTransform dangling after an error and leaks it on recalculation
issues.description: For a node without a mother, calcLabTransform() (lines 278, 285) and setLabTransform() (lines 307, 314) delete labTransform but do not reset it. getLabTransform() then returns freed memory, and the destructor or clear() deletes it again. calcLabTransform() also allocates a new object without freeing the old one, so FairModule::ProcessNodes() leaks a transform that the copy constructor already computed; setLabTransform() also reports its errors as 'calcLabTransform()'.
issues.fix: Set labTransform to nullptr after each delete, reuse or delete the old object in calcLabTransform(), and fix the function name in the messages.

issues.title: FairGeoRootBuilder::createMedium() guards with && instead of ||; null medium crashes
issues.description: The guard if (!geoManager && !med) returns only when both are null, so a null med reaches med->getNComponents() at line 150. A null medium comes from FairGeoMedia::getMedium() for an unknown name. For example, FairPipe::ConstructGeometry() asks for 'steel' and 'Al+Be', which examples/common/geometry/media.geo does not define (no example uses FairPipe today).
issues.fix: Use || and log an error; callers such as FairPipe should check getMedium() for nullptr.

issues.title: FairGeoRootBuilder::createMedium() builds a duplicate medium on every call
issues.description: createMedium() does not check med->getMediumIndex(), so each call creates a new TGeoMaterial and TGeoMedium with the same name and the next number, and overwrites the stored index. createNode() checks the index first (lines 80-83), but FairPipe::ConstructGeometry() calls createMedium() unconditionally. The test if (medium) at line 181 is always true because it follows new.
issues.fix: Return the existing index when med->getMediumIndex() > 0, and remove the dead test.

issues.title: FairGeoSet::readModule() matches 'xxx1' to 'xxx10'..'xxx19', so modules are read twice
issues.description: readModule() selects volumes with name.BeginsWith(modName), and getModuleName(m) returns fName + (m+1). With 10 or more modules, the pass for 'xxx1' also reads 'xxx10' to 'xxx19', and the pass for 'xxx10' reads 'xxx10' again, so these nodes are added and built twice at the same place. Examples and templates declare maxModules = 10 (Tutorial4: 100), so the limit is reachable.
issues.fix: Match the exact module name, or the name followed by '#', instead of a prefix.

issues.title: f_evt_get_open() refuses file names of 128 characters or more
issues.description: f_evt_get_open() compares strlen(pc_server) with the size of c_channel[128] (f_evt.h:84) and fails with 'file name to long!', although c_file holds 256 and nothing ever reads c_channel. So longer LMD paths cannot be opened: the MQ Lmd example (startMQExLmd.sh.in) passes @CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR@/examples/advanced/MbsTutorial/sample_data_2.lmd and fails when the source path has 80 or more characters. The message also misspells 'too long' (lines 615, 625).
issues.fix: Enlarge or drop the unused c_channel copy, keep room for the '.lmd' suffix in c_file, and fix the typo.

issues.title: f_ut_utime.c and f_ut_utime.h refer to a Go4License.txt that FairRoot does not ship
issues.description: Unlike the other mbsapi files, which carry the FairRoot LGPL header, these two files say they can be used under Go4License.txt, which is not in the repository. Both files are also ISO-8859-1 encoded (byte 0xFC for 'ü' in line 6), not UTF-8.
issues.fix: Clarify the license with the Go4 authors, use the standard FairRoot header, and convert both files to UTF-8.

issues.title: FairYamlVMCConfig passes unchecked paths to YAML::LoadFile()
issues.description: ObtainYamlFileName() and SetupPostInit() fall back to $VMCWORKDIR/gconfig/<name> without checking that the file exists. A missing file makes YAML::LoadFile() (lines 49 and 105) throw a yaml-cpp BadFile exception instead of a FairRoot LOG(fatal) that names CONFIG_DIR and the searched paths.
issues.fix: Check the final path with gSystem->AccessPathName() and LOG(fatal) with the searched locations before calling YAML::LoadFile().

issues.title: SetupPostInit() OFF message has no separator before the file name
issues.description: When post-init is off, SetupPostInit() logs 'OFF.' directly followed by fPostInitName. With the defaults it prints 'FairYamlVMCConfig::SetupPostInit() OFF.g4ConfigPostInit.C', so the name runs into the period and shows the .C name inherited from FairGenericVMCConfig.
issues.fix: Add a separator, for example 'OFF (file: ...)', or omit the name when post-init is off.

issues.title: SetupPostInit() with Geant3 goes on after its fatal and calls a null TGeant4 pointer
issues.description: SetupPostInit() logs LOG(fatal) 'only valid for TGeant4' when post-init is on and the engine is not TGeant4, but it does not return (L69-71). FairLogger stops the program only after FairLogger::GetLogger() has installed the fatal handler, so by default the function goes on and loads the post-init YAML file. The shipped g4ConfigPostInit.yaml has Geant4_PostInit_Commands, so L111-112 call ProcessGeantCommand() on the null result of dynamic_cast<TGeant4*>(), and TGeant4::ProcessGeantCommand() reads fRunManager through this null pointer. A Geant3 run with UsePostInitConfig() therefore crashes with a segmentation fault instead of stopping cleanly.
issues.fix: Return right after the fatal message (or skip post-init with a warning for other engines), and check the dynamic_cast result before calling ProcessGeantCommand().

issues.title: SetupGeant3() indexes short G3_SWIT and G3_DEBU lists after its fatal size check
issues.description: SetupGeant3() logs LOG(fatal) when G3_SWIT does not have 2 values or G3_DEBU does not have 3 values (L136, L142), but then calls SetSWIT(intVect[0], intVect[1]) and SetDEBU(intVect[0], intVect[1], intVect[2]) anyway (L137, L143). Without a fatal handler, a shorter list reads past the end of the std::vector: an empty list dereferences a null data pointer, and one or two values pass heap garbage to Geant3. The shipped g3Config.yaml has the right sizes, so only an edited file hits this.
issues.fix: Call SetSWIT() and SetDEBU() only when the list has the expected size, for example in an else branch after the LOG(fatal).

issues.title: Typo 'Special processy not provided' in a FairYamlVMCConfig fatal message
issues.description: SetupGeant4() logs 'Special processy not provided' when the Geant4_SpecialProcess key is missing. The text has a typo and does not name the missing YAML key.
issues.fix: Change it to 'Special process (Geant4_SpecialProcess) not provided'.

issues.title: Geant4_Multithreaded in the YAML file silently overrides FairRunSim::SetIsMT()
issues.description: SetupGeant4() starts from FairRunSim::IsMT() but replaces it with the Geant4_Multithreaded key when the key exists. The shipped examples/common/gconfig/g4Config.yaml sets the key to false (line 5), so SetIsMT(true) has no effect with that file, and nothing tells the user.
issues.fix: Warn when the YAML value and IsMT() disagree, or let an explicit SetIsMT() win.

issues.title: FairYamlVMCConfig::StoreYamlInfo() crashes when the run has no sink
issues.description: Setup() always calls StoreYamlInfo(), which calls FairRunSim::Instance()->GetSink()->WriteObject() without a null check. A run without a sink is allowed (FairRootManager::InitSink() only logs 'The output sink is not set'), and FairGenericVMCConfig works in that case. The YAML configuration dereferences nullptr instead.
issues.fix: Skip the write, with an info message, when GetSink() returns nullptr.

issues.title: UsePostInitConfig() defaults differ, so FairYamlVMCConfig may load the .C macro as YAML
issues.description: The virtual UsePostInitConfig() defaults to 'g4ConfigPostInit.yaml' here but to 'g4ConfigPostInit.C' in FairGenericVMCConfig.h:27, and C++ takes default arguments from the static type (checked with a mock). A call without a name through a FairGenericVMCConfig pointer, for example FairRunSim::GetSimulationConfig(), sets the .C name; the empty-name fallback in SetupPostInit() (FairYamlVMCConfig.cxx:84-86) does the same. SetupPostInit() then gives the C++ macro to YAML::LoadFile() (line 105), which cannot parse it.
issues.fix: Use one default in both classes (or none in the override), and use g4ConfigPostInit.yaml in the YAML class's constructor and empty-name fallback.

issues.title: Step logger sources carry a GPL v3+ header that conflicts with COPYRIGHT (LGPL-3.0-only)
issues.description: MCStepInterceptor.cxx and MCStepLoggerImpl.cxx (lines 1-21) carry the CERN/ALICE O2 notice: GPL v3 'or (at your option) any later version', 'copied verbatim in the file COPYING'. No COPYING file exists, and COPYRIGHT (lines 6-10) and codemeta.json declare all files except Catch2 as LGPL-3.0-only. The library is always built (fairroot/CMakeLists.txt:13) and installed (fairroot/mcsteplogger/CMakeLists.txt:41).
issues.fix: Ask the authors to relicense the two files as LGPL-3.0-only, or list them as GPL-3.0-or-later in COPYRIGHT and point the header to LICENSE.

issues.title: #undef NDEBUG comes after <cassert>, so the dlopen()/dlsym() asserts vanish with NDEBUG
issues.description: assert() is defined when <cassert> is included (line 38); the #undef NDEBUG at lines 45-47 comes later and has no effect. With -DNDEBUG (CMake's default for Release and RelWithDebInfo, for example with Clang on Linux, because cmake/modules/CheckCompiler.cmake only replaces the GCC-on-Linux and macOS flags), the checks at lines 152/154, 185/187 and 218/220 disappear. A failed dlopen() then leads to dlsym(NULL), which is RTLD_DEFAULT on glibc and can return the interceptor itself (endless recursion), or to a call through a null member pointer.
issues.fix: Replace the asserts with explicit checks that print an error and abort.

issues.title: Step logger reports one step too few per volume
issues.description: addStep() inserts 0 for the first step in a volume and adds 1 only for later steps. So every per-event and per-run 'COUNT' line and every bin of stepLoggerHistogram is the real count minus 1, and a volume with a single step shows 0. The volume counts therefore do not add up to the 'did N steps' total.
issues.fix: Count with ++volumetosteps[id] and ++volumetostepsGlobal[id].

issues.title: flushFinal() does not check TFile::Open(); a crash there skips the real FinishRun()
issues.description: flushFinal() opens stepLogger.root in the current directory and calls stepLoggerFile->Write() (line 122) without a null check. If the directory is not writable, TFile::Open() returns nullptr and the program crashes. The interceptor calls flushFinalLog() before it dispatches to FairMCApplication::FinishRun(), so the original FinishRun(), which writes the simulation output, then never runs.
issues.fix: Check the returned TFile pointer and skip the file output with an error message when it is null.

issues.title: Step logger is not thread-safe and breaks with multithreaded Geant4
issues.description: All threads share one global StepLogger without a lock, and performLogging() caches TVirtualMC::GetMC() of the first calling thread in a function-local static (line 230). In Geant4 MT mode (the default in run_rutherford.C and run_tutorial2.C), workers insert into the same std::set and std::map at the same time and read another thread's MC state. FinishRunOnWorker() calls FinishRun() (FairMCApplication.cxx:483), so each worker also recreates stepLogger.root, and README.dox does not say that only sequential mode works.
issues.fix: Keep per-thread logger state (thread_local) and call TVirtualMC::GetMC() on each step, or document and check that the logger needs sequential mode.

issues.title: AddPath() leaks the TRegexp, TSystemDirectory, iterator and file list on every call
issues.description: AddPath() allocates re (line 82), sdir (line 83) and iter (line 90) with new and never deletes them. The TList from GetListOfFiles() is emptied with Delete() (line 101), but the list itself is not deleted.
issues.fix: Create re and sdir on the stack and delete iter and list (or hold them in std::unique_ptr).

issues.title: AddPath() crashes when the directory cannot be listed
issues.description: AddPath() only checks that the path exists. TSystemDirectory::GetListOfFiles() returns nullptr when the directory cannot be opened, for example without read permission or when the path is a regular file, and line 90 then calls list->MakeIterator() on the null pointer.
issues.fix: Log an error and return when GetListOfFiles() returns nullptr.

issues.title: AddPath() adds the matching files in directory order, not sorted
issues.description: TSystemDirectory::GetListOfFiles() returns the entries in readdir() order and does not sort them. AddPath() adds the matching files in that order, so the files of one run can be read out of sequence, and the order can change between file systems.
issues.fix: Collect the matching names, sort them, then call AddFile().

issues.title: OpenNextFile() and ConnectToServer() allocate the s_evt_channel without initializing it
issues.description: FairLmdSource::OpenNextFile() and FairMbsStreamSource::ConnectToServer() (FairMbsStreamSource.cxx:45) create the channel with `new s_evt_channel`, which leaves this C struct uninitialized. f_evt_get_open() keeps a non-zero l_timeout as a timeout set by the user (f_evt.c:608), so the stream source passes a random timeout to f_stc_read() (f_evt.c:759) and to the DABC reader. Depending on old heap contents, reads can time out after a random number of seconds.
issues.fix: Value-initialize the channel with `new s_evt_channel()` in both places.

issues.title: FairLmdSource and FairMbsStreamSource log each other's class names
issues.description: FairLmdSource::ReadEvent() logs 'FairMbsStreamSource::ReadEvent()' when f_evt_get_event() fails or a file ends. The debug2 messages of FairMbsStreamSource::ReadEvent() (FairMbsStreamSource.cxx:73, 77, 97) say 'FairLmdSource::ReadEvent'. The code was copied between the two classes.
issues.fix: Use the right class name in each message.

issues.title: CloseLmd() passes freed buffer memory to -4 unpackers after closing the file
issues.description: CloseLmd() calls f_evt_get_close(), which frees the channel's I/O buffer (f_evt.c:1216), and then deletes the channel. After that it calls Unpack(fxBuffer, sizeof(s_bufhe), -4, ...), but fxBuffer points into the freed buffer, or into s_bufhe_1 inside the deleted channel for a spanned event. So every unpacker registered for type -4 reads freed memory at each file change (OpenNextFile()), at end of file and at Close(); for DABC-format files fxBuffer is NULL instead (f_evt.c:1029). Correction: The proposed fix is not complete: CloseLmd() should also set fxBuffer to nullptr. Otherwise, if the next file ends before its first event, fxBuffer still points to the previous file's buffer, which is already freed. For the last file, the bad call comes from Close() (FairRunOnline.cxx:312) or from the destructor (FairLmdSource.cxx:57), not at end of file, because ReadEvent() returns at lines 169-171 before it reaches line 174.
issues.fix: Call the -4 Unpack() before f_evt_get_close() and the delete, and skip it when fxBuffer is null.
issues.evidence: CloseLmd() frees the I/O buffer in f_evt_get_close() (f_evt.c:1216) and deletes the channel (FairLmdSource.cxx:252-254). Only then does it pass fxBuffer to Unpack() at line 255, and fxBuffer points into that buffer (f_evt.c:1133) or, for a spanned event, to s_bufhe_1 inside the channel (f_evt.c:1164, f_evt.h:82). I built the unchanged FairLmdSource and FairMbsSource::Unpack code with the real MbsAPI and a type -4 unpacker, then read sample_data_2.lmd twice. ASan reports heap-use-after-free at the file change (line 174, then line 255), and without ASan the unpacker gets garbage (l_dlen=-1157608672, time 0). Only type -4 unpackers read the pointer, so the MbsTutorial unpacker (type 94) is not affected, but the -4 header hook is a deliberate feature (lines 148, 188, 255).

issues.title: ConnectToServer() lets f_evt_get_open() cut the port off fServerName
issues.description: ConnectToServer() passes const_cast<char*>(fServerName.Data()) to f_evt_get_open(). For a 'host:port' name, f_evt_get_open() runs strtok() on it (f_evt.c:582) and writes a null character over the colon inside the TString buffer. After the connection, GetServerName(), the 'connection ... established' log line and the copy constructor see only 'host', so a copy would use the default port.
issues.fix: Pass a writable copy of the name to f_evt_get_open().

issues.title: FairOnlineSource copy constructor shares the unpackers, so both copies delete them
issues.description: The copy constructor creates fUnpackers with the TObjArray copy constructor, which copies only the pointers. The destructor calls fUnpackers->Delete(), so when the original and the copy are destroyed, each FairUnpack is deleted twice. The copy constructors of FairLmdSource, FairMbsStreamSource and FairRemoteSource all use this one.
issues.fix: Delete the copy constructor, or give the copy its own clones of the unpackers.

issues.title: FairRemoteSource stores the caller's node pointer instead of copying the string
issues.description: The constructor keeps the `char* node` argument in fNode, and the copy constructor copies the same pointer. Init() later passes fNode to RevOpen(). If the caller passed the buffer of a temporary or of a string that is gone at Init() time (for example TString::Data() of a local in a helper function), RevOpen() reads freed memory.
issues.fix: Store the node name in a TString member and take `const char*` in the constructor.

issues.title: MRevBuffer never frees its REvent or the TSocket from RevOpen()
issues.description: The destructor calls pEvt->~REvent() instead of delete pEvt, so the REvent memory leaks. RevOpen() creates pTSocket with new (line 193) and nobody deletes it, not even when the connection is invalid and RevOpen() returns 0 (lines 194-196).
issues.fix: Use delete pEvt, and delete pTSocket when RevOpen() fails and when the connection is closed.

issues.title: RevGet() overflows REvent's 100-entry subevent arrays for events with over 100 subevents
issues.description: RevGet() walks the subevents while ielen > 0 and writes subEvtSize[ii-1] up to pSubEvt[ii-1] without checking ii against the array size 100 (MRevBuffer.h:55-61). An event with more than 100 subevents, or a corrupt subevent length, writes past the arrays and corrupts the REvent object and the heap. The table is also filled only when iDebug is 1 or 5; FairRemoteSource happens to use MRevBuffer(1).
issues.fix: Stop with an error when ii reaches 100, and fill the subevent table independent of iDebug.

issues.title: FairRunOnline::Init() ignores a failed InitSource(); the first ReadEvent() then crashes
issues.description: Init() calls fRootManager->InitSource() and drops the result. If FairLmdSource has no file (AddFile() only warns about a missing file) or cannot open the first one, fxInputChannel stays null and the first ReadEvent() passes it to f_evt_get_event(), which dereferences it (f_evt.c:995). For FairRemoteSource, a failed RevOpen() leaves fSocket null, and RevGet() calls pSocket->SendRaw() on it (MRevBuffer.cxx:289).
issues.fix: Check the result of InitSource() and stop with a clear error (and let Run() refuse to start) when it fails.

issues.title: After a failed InitUnpackers(), Init() returns early but Run() still runs the tasks
issues.description: When InitUnpackers() fails, Init() logs LOG(fatal) and returns before fTask->InitTask(), WriteFolder() and WriteFileHeader(). LOG(fatal) only calls a registered fatal callback, and FairRoot registers one only when the legacy FairLogger object exists (fairroot/tools/FairLogger.cxx:37), so the program usually continues. Run() does not know that Init() failed and executes tasks whose Init() never ran.
issues.fix: Throw (or set a flag that Run() checks) instead of only logging and returning.

issues.title: Init() calls InitSink() and WriteFileHeader() twice
issues.description: Init() calls fRootManager->InitSink() at lines 117 and 202; for FairRootFileSink the second call only logs 'FairRootFileSink already initialized'. It also calls WriteFileHeader() at lines 181 and 204, and each call writes with kSingleKey (FairRootManager.cxx:816), so the output file gets two cycles of the FileHeader key.
issues.fix: Remove the InitSink() call at line 202 and the WriteFileHeader() call at line 181.

issues.title: ActivateHttpServer(0) makes EventLoop() divide by zero
issues.description: EventLoop() computes fNevents % fServerRefreshRate whenever an HTTP server exists, and ActivateHttpServer() (lines 317-323) stores the rate without a check. With a rate of 0, the first event raises an integer division by zero (SIGFPE). A negative rate does not crash; it acts like its absolute value.
issues.fix: Reject or clamp a refresh rate below 1 in ActivateHttpServer().

issues.title: FairRunOnline::Run() prints a warning that names FairRunAna
issues.description: Run() prints ' -W FairRunAna : File has less events than requested!!' when the source has fewer events than requested. The block was copied from FairRunAna::Run(). It runs only for sources whose CheckMaxEventNo() is not -1, so not for the FairRoot online sources.
issues.fix: Name FairRunOnline in the message, and use LOG(warn) like the rest of the class.

issues.title: Run() skips the Ctrl-C check when the source skips an event (status 2)
issues.description: In both loops of Run(), status 2 jumps to continue before the gIsInterrupted check (lines 275-276 and 290-292). EventLoop() installs handler_ctrlc from the first processed event on; if the source then skips every event, for example a stream with no matching unpacker, Ctrl-C only sets the flag and the loop does not stop.
issues.fix: Check gIsInterrupted before the continue, at the top of each iteration.

issues.title: FairRunOnline::Run() has no default arguments, and Run(0, 0) or Run(n, 0) process no event
issues.description: FairRun::Run(Int_t = 0, Int_t = 0) has defaults, but the override FairRunOnline::Run(Int_t, Int_t) has none: run->Run() does not compile on a FairRunOnline*, and through a FairRun* it means Run(0, 0). The online sources keep FairSource::CheckMaxEventNo(), which returns -1, so Run() skips the range fix-up (FairRunOnline.cxx:242-265). Run(0, 0) and Run(n, 0) therefore process no event, while the same calls on FairRunAna process all entries or n events.
issues.fix: Give the override the same default arguments and map Run(0, 0) and Run(n, 0) for online sources to 'until the source ends' and 'n events', as FairRunAna does.

issues.title: FairDetParRootFileIo::write() logs 'No output open' after 'Output is not writable'
issues.description: When the file is open but not writable, write() logs 'Output is not writable' (line 92) and then falls through to the second Error() 'No output open' (line 95). The second message is wrong for this case.
issues.fix: Return -1 right after the 'not writable' error.

issues.title: readData() drops the character before a continuation backslash
issues.description: readData() cuts each continued line with s = s(0, m - 1), which removes the backslash and also the character before it. Files written by FairRoot have a space there, but a hand-written value right before the backslash loses its last character without a message: the line '10 11 12\' reads as 10 11 1. A replica of the parser confirms this.
issues.fix: Cut with s = s(0, m) so that only the backslash is removed.

issues.title: readData() ignores sscanf() failures and stores a stale value for a bad token
issues.description: readData() does not check the return value of sscanf() (lines 85 and 106). A token that is not a number gives no error: the reader stores the previous value again, or the initial value (0, or '0' for Char_t) for the first token. A replica of the parser confirms this.
issues.fix: Check that sscanf() returns 1 and fail the read with an error that names the parameter.

issues.title: readData() consumes the '#' terminator after a trailing backslash, so the block runs on
issues.description: When the last line of an array ends with a backslash, readData() reads the next line, the '#' block terminator, into its own local buffer. readGenericSet() never sees it and keeps parsing after the block: a following [block] line fails with 'Missing backslash for parameter <name>', and a parameter line is silently added to this container. A replica of the parser confirms both cases.
issues.fix: Let readData() tell readGenericSet() that it reached the terminator.

issues.title: ASCII parameter reader hangs on a line of 8000 or more characters
issues.description: readGenericSet() and readData() read lines with istream::getline(buf, 8000). For a line of 8000 or more characters, getline() sets failbit; every later call stores a null character in buf[0] and eof() never becomes true. The loop at line 156 then skips the empty buffer forever and the initialization hangs; a g++ replica of the loop confirms this. A long single-line Text_t value written by writeGenericSet() is enough to trigger it.
issues.fix: Read lines with std::getline() into a std::string, or stop with an error when pFile->fail() is set.

issues.title: readGenericSet() fails on a line with only spaces and blames a missing backslash
issues.description: readGenericSet() skips only empty lines (line 162). Any other line without a colon, such as a line with only spaces or a [block] line read after a lost terminator, gives 'Missing backslash for parameter <previous name>', and the container fails to load. The message names the wrong cause and the wrong parameter; a replica of the parser confirms this.
issues.fix: Skip lines that contain only white space, and report a line without a colon together with its text.

issues.title: Error locations in FairGenericParAsciiFileIo still name readCond/writeCond
issues.description: The Error() calls at lines 165, 243, 318 and 330 pass 'readCond(FairParGenericSet*)' or 'writeCond(FairParGenericSet*)' as the location. The functions are readGenericSet() and writeGenericSet(), so the messages point to functions that do not exist.
issues.fix: Use readGenericSet and writeGenericSet as the locations.

issues.title: A single Char_t value written by writeGenericSet() reads back as a space
issues.description: For a single value, the writer puts two spaces between the type and the value (line 303). The reader skips only one character after the type (line 202), and sscanf("%c") at line 85 does not skip white space. So a TArrayC of size 1 written by FairRoot reads back as ' '; a replica of the parser confirms this.
issues.fix: Strip leading white space before readData(), or read Char_t with the format " %c".

issues.title: writeGenericSet() writes no value and no line end for UInt_t and Bool_t parameters
issues.description: UInt_t and Bool_t parameters are basic types, so writeGenericSet() prints 'name:  UInt_t  ', but its type chain (lines 307-315) has no branch for them. No value and no newline follow, so the next parameter or the closing '#' line lands on the same line and the block cannot be read back. readGenericSet() also rejects both types (lines 242-249); FairBaseParSet::putParams() adds "Random Seed" as UInt_t, for example.
issues.fix: Add UInt_t and Bool_t branches to writeGenericSet() and readGenericSet().

issues.title: fill(Text_t*) logs 'Could not find parameter' after 'char array too small'
issues.description: When the parameter exists but the target buffer is too small, fill(const Text_t*, Text_t*, Int_t) logs 'char array too small' and then falls through to 'Could not find parameter <name>'. The second message is wrong. The size check l < length - 1 is also one byte too strict.
issues.fix: Return kFALSE right after the 'too small' error, and accept l <= length - 1.

issues.title: FairParamList::fill(UInt_t*) matches type "Int_t" instead of "UInt_t"
issues.description: add(name, UInt_t) stores the type "UInt_t", but fill(const Text_t*, UInt_t*, Int_t) only accepts objects of type "Int_t". So a UInt_t value cannot be read back from a FairParamList, for example "Random Seed" in FairBaseParSet::getParams() (fairroot/base/sim/FairBaseParSet.cxx:71), and the call fails with 'Could not find parameter'. Today only an ASCII "Int_t" line can fill a UInt_t member.
issues.fix: Accept "UInt_t" in fill(UInt_t*), and keep accepting "Int_t" for existing ASCII files.

issues.title: FairParAsciiFileIo::open() reports 'Could not open input file' also for output files
issues.description: open() prints '-E- Could not open input file' and calls Fatal("open", "Could not open input file") also when the mode is "out". FairParRootFileIo::open() (FairParRootFileIo.cxx:144-145) uses the same 'input' text for every option, for example "RECREATE".
issues.fix: Say 'parameter file' or name the mode in both messages.

issues.title: MergeFiles() keeps only the newest cycle of each key and renumbers the cycles
issues.description: MergeFiles() iterates GetListOfKeys(), which has one entry per cycle, but copies inFile->Get(name), which is always the highest cycle, and writes it as a new cycle (line 221). Older versions are lost, and the cycle numbers shift across files. The run tables copied from the second and later files still point to their old cycle numbers, which now hold another file's containers, so runs read from allParams_*.root can get the wrong parameters.
issues.fix: Copy each key with inpKey->ReadObj() and rewrite the FairRtdbRun version tables to the new cycle numbers.

issues.title: FairParSet::init() warns 'failed for first input' even when the second input succeeds
issues.description: init() calls CallInitIO() for the first input (line 67), and CallInitIO() logs a warning (line 50) when that input does not hold the container. The documented fallback to the second input then often succeeds, for example with the ROOT file plus ASCII file setup of read_digis.C, but the warning stays in the log and looks like a problem.
issues.fix: Log the first-input miss at debug level and warn only when the second input fails too.

issues.title: ~FairRuntimeDb() closes the first input before the output's auto-save
issues.description: The destructor calls closeFirstInput() before closeOutput(). When one FairParRootFileIo object is both first input and output (the create_digis.C pattern), closeFirstInput() closes and deletes its file first. closeOutput() then runs saveOutput(), but output->check() is false, so pending containers and the run table are lost.
issues.fix: Call closeOutput() before closing the inputs.

issues.title: addParamContext() always reports 'Unknown context', even on success
issues.description: addParamContext() calls Error("addParamContext(const char*)", "Unknown context") after the factory loop without looking at found. Every call therefore prints an error, also when a factory accepted the context and the function returns kTRUE.
issues.fix: Call Error() only when found is kFALSE.

issues.title: findOutputVersion() treats input version 1 as a key cycle when input 1 is also the output
issues.description: When firstInput == output and in2 == -1, findOutputVersion() returns in1 and assumes it is the key cycle the container was read from, so a container read from that file and then changed in code is never written. The macros mark changed containers with setInputVersion(runId, 1) (create_digis.C:89, read_digis.C:109). With the same file as input and output, writeContainer() then skips the write and records the run ID as ROOT version in the run table.
issues.fix: Use this shortcut only when in1 is an existing cycle in the output file, and mark changed containers with setInputVersion(-1, 1) instead of the run ID.

issues.title: writeContainer() says '<name> written to output' for ASCII output that wrote nothing
issues.description: For an ASCII output, writeContainer() checks only cv < 0 and then prints '*** <name> written to output'. A container without its own write(FairParIo*) uses the FairParSet default, which returns 0 and writes nothing, but the message still appears. The ROOT branch treats 0 as 'no write function' and prints nothing.
issues.fix: Print the message only when cv > 0.

issues.title: writeContainer() clears the changed flag even when there is no output
issues.description: writeContainer() calls cont->setChanged(kFALSE) after the output block, also when there is no output or it is not auto-writable. A saveOutput() call before setOutput() (read_digis.C:94 calls saveOutput() with no output at all) therefore drops all pending writes without a message. A later setOutput() plus saveOutput() writes none of these containers and no run table.
issues.fix: Keep the changed flag, and log a warning, when there is no usable output.

issues.title: setOutput() and writeContainer() handle a FairParTSQLIo class that does not exist
issues.description: setOutput() compares the output class name with "FairParTSQLIo" (line 761), and writeContainer() has a RootTSQLOutput case (lines 418-429; enum value in FairRuntimeDb.h:51). No such class exists in the repository, so this branch never runs. It is also the only place in the runtime database that calls FairParSet::print().
issues.fix: Remove the TSQL branch and the RootTSQLOutput enum value.

issues.title: closeOutput() comment says it deletes the output, but the code only closes it
issues.description: The comment at L834 says that closeOutput() 'calls saveOutput() and deletes then the output'. The code calls saveOutput() only when the output is auto-writable, then calls output->close() and sets the pointer to 0 (L835-842). It never deletes the FairParIo object, so the caller keeps the ownership.
issues.fix: Reword the comment: closeOutput() saves an auto-writable output, closes it and resets the pointer, and the caller still owns the FairParIo object.

issues.title: A malformed parameter request makes stoi() throw and stops the server
issues.description: ProcessRequest() parses the run ID with stoi(reqStr.substr(pos + 1)) and never checks pos. A request without a comma, or without a number after it, makes stoi() throw std::invalid_argument. The exception leaves the data callback, FairMQ moves the device to the Error state and DeviceRunner ends the process, so one bad request stops the server for all clients. ProcessUpdate() has the same unchecked stoi() at line 193.
issues.fix: Check that a comma and a number exist (or catch std::exception around stoi()) and answer a bad request with an empty reply.

issues.title: The parameter-name cache in ProcessRequest() is dead logic with a misleading comment
issues.description: parameterName is a local variable that is set to an empty string at the start of every call (line 119). So 'if (newParameterName != parameterName)' is true for every non-empty name, and the comment about avoiding repeated getContainer() calls describes caching that never happens. getContainer() runs on every request.
issues.fix: Remove the local variable and the check and call getContainer() directly.

issues.title: ProcessRequest() sends no reply and stops the server when initContainers() fails
issues.description: If fRtdb->initContainers(runId) fails, ProcessRequest() logs an error and returns false without a reply. initContainers() fails when any non-static container in the runtime database has no data for that run ID in either input. A false return from a FairMQ data callback ends the RUNNING state, so the REQ client blocks forever and no further request is served. ProcessUpdate() does the same at lines 198-201.
issues.fix: Send an empty reply, as the code already does for an unknown parameter, and return true.

issues.title: ProcessUpdate() error log names ProcessRequest()
issues.description: The error message inside ProcessUpdate() says 'ParameterMQServer::ProcessRequest: fRtdb->initContainers failed'. A user who reads the log looks in the wrong function.
issues.fix: Change the prefix to 'ParameterMQServer::ProcessUpdate:'.

issues.title: ProcessUpdate() sends no reply and stops the server when initContainers() fails
issues.description: When fRtdb->initContainers(runId) fails, ProcessUpdate() logs an error and returns false (L198-201) without sending SUCCESS or FAIL. FairMQ leaves the RUNNING state when a data handler returns false, so the server stops serving. The simulation device that sent the parameter waits in Receive() with no timeout (FairMQRunDevice::SendObject(), examples/MQ/pixelDetector/src/devices/FairMQRunDevice.cxx:54-55), so it hangs. ProcessRequest() has the same flaw, which is tracked separately.
issues.fix: Send a FAIL reply and return true on this path, so the client gets an answer and the server keeps running.

issues.title: ProcessUpdate() leaks the deserialized parameter set when it is not added
issues.description: RootSerializer().Deserialize() allocates newPar, and only fRtdb->addContainer() takes ownership. addContainer() returns false when a container with that name already exists, for example when a second simulation device sends the same containers; ProcessUpdate() then replies FAIL and never deletes newPar. The early return after a failed initContainers() (line 200) leaks it too, and a leaked FairGeoParSet carries a whole TGeoManager.
issues.fix: Hold newPar in a std::unique_ptr and release it only when addContainer() succeeds.

issues.title: Update mode without --output-name aborts the server at the first parameter
issues.description: InitTask() does not check --output-name when --update-channel-name is set, and its default is empty. At the first parameter update, ProcessUpdate() calls FairParRootFileIo::open(""); TFile::Open() returns nullptr for an empty name, and open() then calls ROOT Fatal() (FairParRootFileIo.cxx:144-145), which aborts the process. So the server dies when the first simulation device sends its parameters.
issues.fix: In InitTask(), reject an empty --output-name when --update-channel-name is set, with a clear error message.

issues.title: --channel-name defaults to empty, so the server registers no request handler
issues.description: The option default is empty, and Init() always copies it over the constructor default "data" and over any SetChannelName() call (ParameterMQServer.cxx:41, 47). With the default, Init() registers no OnData() handler and logs nothing, so the device leaves RUNNING at once and no request is ever answered. The README says the default is "data", and the help text calls the option 'Output channel name' although it is the REQ/REP channel that receives the requests.
issues.fix: Make "data" the option default (or fail in Init() when both channel names are empty) and change the help text to 'Request (REQ/REP) channel name'.

issues.title: Configuring with -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF fails in fairroot/tools/tests
issues.description: fairroot/tools/CMakeLists.txt adds the tests subdirectory without an if(BUILD_TESTING) guard. tests/CMakeLists.txt:19 calls catch_discover_tests() and links Catch2::Catch2WithMain, but third_party/CMakeLists.txt:15-33 fetches Catch2 and includes the Catch module only when BUILD_TESTING is ON. So configuring with -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF stops with 'Unknown CMake command "catch_discover_tests"' (reproduced with a minimal CMake project).
issues.fix: Wrap add_subdirectory(tests) in if(BUILD_TESTING), as the top-level CMakeLists.txt does for its tests.

excerpt.code:
install(FILES ${headers} ${extra_headers} DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR})

add_subdirectory(tests)

issues.title: LOG(fatal) stops the program only after FairLogger::GetLogger() was called
issues.description: Only the FairLogger constructor installs LogFatalMessage() with fair::Logger::OnFatal(), and only GetLogger() (gLogger) creates that object. fair::Logger has no default fatal action, no code in fairroot/ calls GetLogger(), and tools/README.dox presents the call as optional. Without it LOG(fatal) only prints, and library code that expects a stop goes on: FairTask::InitTask() keeps a task active after Init() returns kFATAL, and FairMCApplication::InitMC() dereferences a null fMC right after LOG(fatal) << 'No MC engine defined'.
issues.fix: Install the fatal handler when FairTools is loaded (for example with a static initializer), so that LOG(fatal) always throws.

issues.title: LogFatalMessage() closes stderr for the rest of the process
issues.description: LogFatalMessage() redirects stderr to core_dump_<pid> with freopen(), writes the stack trace, and then calls fclose(stderr). It never restores stderr. If a caller catches the fair::FatalException and goes on, as an interactive ROOT session does, all later stderr output, including ROOT error messages and std::cerr, is lost.
issues.fix: Save the descriptor with dup() before the redirect and restore it with dup2() after the stack trace.

issues.title: Typo "occured" in the FatalException text; comment says the process aborts
issues.description: LogFatalMessage() throws fair::FatalException("Fatal error occured. Exiting..."), and users see this text; the correct spelling is 'occurred'. The comment at lines 185-186 says 'the process is aborted', but the code throws an exception that a caller can catch.
issues.fix: Fix the spelling and change the comment to say that a fair::FatalException is thrown.

issues.title: SetLogToFile(false) silences the console, SetLogToScreen(false) the log file
issues.description: SetLogToScreen(false) and SetLogToFile(false) set the sink severity to fair::Severity::fatal instead of nolog. In current FairLogger (checked v1.9.0 to v2.2.0), UpdateMinSeverity() uses std::max(console, file) as the global filter when the file severity is not nolog. So SetLogToFile(kFALSE) leaves only fatal messages on the console, and SetLogToScreen(kFALSE) leaves only fatal messages in an open log file.
issues.fix: Use fair::Severity::nolog for the disabled sink.

issues.title: Memory monitor stores resident memory in bytes as Int_t
issues.description: StartMemoryMonitor() and StopMemoryMonitor() cast FairSystemInfo::GetCurrentMemory() (size_t, in bytes) to Int_t and keep it in a std::map<TString, Int_t>. Above 2 GiB the value wraps, and memoryAtEnd - iti->second (lines 146 and 149) can overflow, which is undefined behavior. In practice the per-task difference stays right unless one Exec() changes the memory by more than 2 GiB.
issues.fix: Store the values as Long64_t.

issues.title: RecordRegister() log lines miss the closing parenthesis for kFALSE
issues.description: RecordRegister() prints ', kTRUE)' when toFile is true but ', kFALSE' without the closing parenthesis when it is false (lines 184 and 188). This gives malformed lines such as '*** FM::RecordRegister(name, folder, kFALSE WITHOUT TASK'.
issues.fix: Print ', kFALSE)' in the false branch.

issues.title: FairMonitor::Print() and Draw() find no tasks outside FairRunAna
issues.description: Print() and Draw() look for the task tree only as a top-level 'FairTaskList' in gROOT->GetListOfBrowsables(). Only FairRunAna (FairRunAna.cxx:177) and FairRunAnaProof (FairRunAnaProof.cxx:146) put it there. In FairRunSim it is a child of 'Task List' (FairRunSim.cxx:188, FairMCApplication.cxx:1179-1185), and FairRunOnline never adds it. So Print() lists no tasks, and Draw(), which StoreHistograms() also calls, returns silently and writes no canvas.
issues.fix: Have every run class register its main task with FairMonitor (for example a new SetMainTask() called from FairRun) instead of looking up a fixed top-level name.

issues.title: PrintTask(TString) prints the unit of the previous histogram
issues.description: PrintTask(TString) declares unitString once, before the loop, and sets it only for names that end in _TIM (' s') or _MEM (' B'). A histogram that the user filled with RecordInfo() under another ending, for example _NHITS, is printed with the unit of the histogram before it.
issues.fix: Declare unitString inside the loop.

issues.title: FairMonitor.h declares extern gMonitor, but nothing defines it
issues.description: FairMonitor.h declares 'extern FairMonitor* gMonitor;', but no source file defines it and LinkDef.h does not export it. Code that uses gMonitor compiles and then fails to link, and a ROOT macro cannot resolve it. The working access path is FairMonitor::GetMonitor().
issues.fix: Remove the declaration.

issues.title: fscanf() reads an unsigned long with the signed %ld conversion
issues.description: GetCurrentMemory() reads /proc/self/statm with fscanf(fp, "%*s%ld", &rss), but rss is unsigned long. The conversion does not match the argument type, which the C standard leaves undefined. It has no visible effect today, and GCC and Clang do not warn about it with -Wall.
issues.fix: Use %lu.

issues.title: Unsupported-OS branch in GetCurrentMemory() is dead code
issues.description: Lines 27-28 stop the build with #error "Unknown OS." on every system other than macOS and Linux. So the #else branch 'AIX, BSD, Solaris, and Unknown OS' at lines 79-81 can never compile. The doc comment at lines 45-48 ('zero if the value cannot be determined on this OS') suggests that other systems are supported.
issues.fix: Remove the dead branch and reword the comment, or drop the #error and keep the fallback.

issues.title: Wrong TO lines and variable lists in FairGeaneUtil conversion comments
issues.description: Several function comments say FROM ... FROM where the second line should be TO: FromPtToSC() (41-42), FromPtToSD() (124-125), FromSCToPt() (266-267) and FromSDToPt() (694-695). FromPtToSD() and FromSDToPt() name SC variables (Lambda, Phi, Yt, Zt) for SD inputs and outputs at lines 127, 697 and 711. FromSCToMars() and FromSDToMars() list the MARS variables as (px, py, pz, z, y, z) at lines 1161 and 1511.
issues.fix: Fix the TO lines, the SD variable names and the MARS list (px, py, pz, x, y, z).

issues.title: memset(ptr, 0, sizeof(*ptr)) in FairGeaneUtil clears only one element
issues.description: The conversion functions reset their outputs with memset(RD, 0, sizeof(*RD)) and similar calls (lines 63, 288, 384-385, 552-553, 885-886, 1110-1111, 1197, 1305-1306, 1554). The arguments are Double_t*, so sizeof(*RD) is 8 and only the first element is cleared. On the error paths (IERR = 1) the other outputs keep stale or uninitialized values, and the FairTrackParP LAB constructors ignore IERR and copy them.
issues.fix: Clear the real array length, for example with std::fill_n(RD, 15, 0.).

issues.title: GetChargeFromPDG() crashes for a PDG code unknown to TDatabasePDG
issues.description: GetChargeFromPDG() calls TDatabasePDG::GetParticle(pdg)->Charge() without a null check. GetParticle() returns nullptr for a code that is not in the database (for example an ion that was never added), and every Propagate() and FindPCA() call starts with GetChargeFromPDG(). FairEveMCTracks checks the same pointer and uses charge 0 instead.
issues.fix: Check the pointer, log an error, and let the callers return false.

issues.title: Propagate(float*, ...) returns true with NaN output when no plane is set
issues.description: The float overload Propagate(x1, p1, x2, p2, PDG) does not check fPropagationFlag. Without SetDestinationPlane() the plane vectors are zero, the normal in PropagateToPlane() is 0/0, and all outputs are NaN, yet the function returns true (confirmed with a test build of the code). The four track-parameter overloads check the flag and return false with a warning.
issues.fix: Return false with a warning when fPropagationFlag is not TOPLANE, as the other overloads do.

issues.title: SetOriginPlane() warning names SetLengthToPropagateTo
issues.description: SetOriginPlane() logs 'FairRKPropagator::SetLengthToPropagateTo not implemented yet'. No function with that name exists, so the warning points to the wrong place.
issues.fix: Change the text to 'FairRKPropagator::SetOriginPlane not implemented yet'.

issues.title: FindPCA() dereferences fPCAPropagationPar without a null check
issues.description: FindPCA() reads the start track from fPCAPropagationPar without checking it. The member is nullptr after construction, and SetPCAPropagation() has par = nullptr as its default argument (FairRKPropagator.h:114). So SetPCAPropagation(1) followed by FindPCA() crashes.
issues.fix: Return the default PCAOutputStruct (status 1) with a warning when fPCAPropagationPar is null, or reject a null par in SetPCAPropagation().

issues.title: FindPCA() returns (0,0,0) with success status when the start is closer than about 1 cm
issues.description: FindPCA() sets res_old = diff (a distance in cm) but compares it with res = newDiff / diff (a ratio). When the start distance is below about 1 cm, res > res_old after the first step, the loop breaks, and vecOut is restored from vecOutT, which is still all zero. The result is OnTrackPCA = (0,0,0), TrackLength = 0, a Distance computed from (0,0,0), and PCAStatusFlag = 0 (success). A straight-line test with the start 0.5 cm before the PCA reproduces this; a start 5 cm away gives the right point.
issues.fix: Initialize res_old to 1.0 (the ratio at the start) and initialize vecOutT with vecIn.
issues.evidence: res_old starts as a distance in cm (FairRKPropagator.cxx:272), but res is the ratio newDiff/diff (line 295). So when the start is closer than about 0.96 cm, the first step already gives res > res_old and the loop breaks (line 296). vecOutT is still all zero (lines 276-279), so lines 310-313 copy zeros into vecOut. The result is OnTrackPCA = (0,0,0), TrackLength 0, a Distance measured from the origin, and PCAStatusFlag 0 (lines 315-326). I ran the unchanged code with no field: a start 0.5 cm from the PCA gives (0,0,0) for both the point case and the wire case, while 0.975 cm and 5 cm give the right point, and with the proposed fix every case is right. No active FairRoot code calls FindPCA (the call in FairTutPropTr.cxx:190-208 is commented out), but it is the public FairPropagator API.

issues.title: PropagateToPlane() has a cross-product typo in the plane normal
issues.description: Line 377 computes Norm[0] = vec1[1] * vec2[2] - vec2[2] * vec2[1]; the second term must be vec1[2] * vec2[1], as the comment a2b3 - a3b2 says. The normal is wrong whenever vec2[1] != 0 and vec1[2] != vec2[2]. A straight-line test of the code confirms it: the x plane given as vec1 = (0,0,1), vec2 = (0,1,0) gives a zero normal and NaN output, and the tilted plane x - z = -10 given as vec1 = (1,0,1)/sqrt2, vec2 = (0,1,0) is treated as the plane z = 10. Planes whose two vectors both have z = 0 (FairEveMCTracks, FairTutPropTr) are not affected. Correction: More exactly, Norm[0] is off by vec2[1]*(vec1[2] - vec2[2]). In one corner case the plane is still right: when the true normal lies along x and the wrong Norm[0] is not zero, for example v1 = (0,2,1), v2 = (0,1,3). There only the length or the sign of the normal changes, and the run gives the correct point.
issues.fix: Write Norm[0] = vec1[1] * vec2[2] - vec1[2] * vec2[1] (or use TVector3::Cross()).
issues.evidence: Line 377 computes Norm[0] = vec1[1]*vec2[2] - vec2[2]*vec2[1], but the cross product (and the comment a2b3 - a3b2) needs vec1[2]*vec2[1]. I ran the unchanged code. The plane x = 10 given as v1 = (0,0,1), v2 = (0,1,0) gives a zero normal and NaN output. The plane x - z = -10 given as v1 = (1,0,1)/sqrt2, v2 = (0,1,0) is handled as z = 10: a track from (5,0,0) along z stops at (5,0,10). Both cases are right after the fix. SetDestinationPlane() with Propagate() also uses this code (lines 176-179). The in-tree callers use z planes whose vectors have z = 0 (FairTutPropTr.cxx:93-97, FairEveMCTracks.cxx:122-123, FairEveRecoTracksExample.cxx:123-124), so they are not affected.

issues.title: PropagateToPlane() cannot reach a plane behind the track but reports success
issues.description: PropagateToPlane() uses the unsigned distance as the step length, and Step() always moves along the momentum. For a plane behind the track the first step moves away, the loop stops when the distance grows, and the function returns the point after that first step. In a straight-line test with the plane z = -10 and a track along +z from the origin, the result is z = +10 (20 cm from the plane), and the Propagate() overloads still return true.
issues.fix: Use the signed distance to choose the step direction, or return false when the plane cannot be reached.

issues.title: PropagateToPlane() measures the distance to a tilted plane wrongly
issues.description: Inside the loop the code uses sqrt(sum(((x_i - p_i) * N_i)^2)) as the distance to the plane, not the dot product |sum((x_i - p_i) * N_i)| that it uses for the start value at line 398. The two agree only when the normal lies along an axis. For a tilted plane the loop stops at the minimum of the wrong measure: in a straight-line test with the plane x - z = -10 (vec1 = (0,1,0), vec2 = (1,0,1)/sqrt2, so the cross-product typo plays no role), a track along z from (5,0,0) ends at z = 10.6 instead of z = 15.
issues.fix: Use fMaxStep = TMath::Abs(dist[0] + dist[1] + dist[2]) as the distance inside the loop.
issues.evidence: Inside the loop, the distance is sqrt(sum(((x_i - p_i)*N_i)^2)) (FairRKPropagator.cxx:411-414), while the start value uses the real plane distance |sum((x_i - p_i)*N_i)| (lines 394-398). The two are equal only when the normal has one non-zero component. I ran the unchanged code with v1 = (0,1,0), v2 = (1,0,1)/sqrt2 and the point (0,0,10); vec2[1] = 0, so the typo at line 377 plays no role. A track along z from (5,0,0) stops at z = 10.61 instead of 15, and a track along x from (0,0,20) stops at x = 7.07 instead of 10. With the proposed fix, both end within 0.01 cm of the plane. Planes with a normal along an axis, like the z planes in the examples, are not affected.

issues.title: Public Propagate(Charge, vecRKIn, Pos) only prints its result
issues.description: FairRKPropagator.h:60-66 documents this public function as 'Propagate to closest approach of a point', with parameters STEP and vecOut that it does not have. The code uses only Pos[2], keeps the result in a local array, and prints it with printf, so the caller gets no result. Nothing in the repository calls it.
issues.fix: Remove the function, or give it an output argument and a correct doc comment.

issues.title: FairTrackPar(x, y, z, px, py, pz, q) sets the errors to the values
issues.description: The 7-argument constructor initializes fDX, fDY, fDZ with x, y, z and fDPx, fDPy, fDPz with px, py, pz. So GetDX() returns the position and GetDPx() the momentum. The FairTrackParH and FairTrackParP LAB constructors overwrite these fields, but a FairTrackPar built directly keeps them, and FairTrackParH(FairTrackPar&) then builds its covariance matrix from them.
issues.fix: Initialize the six error members with 0.

, fZ(z)
