issues.title: FairTrackPar::GetFieldValue() crashes when no FairRunAna exists
issues.description: GetFieldValue() calls FairRunAna::Instance()->GetField() without a null check. FairRunAna::Instance() is nullptr under FairRunSim and FairRunOnline (both derive from FairRun, not FairRunAna) and in standalone code. Every valued constructor and every SetTrackPar() of FairTrackParH and FairTrackParP calls GetFieldValue(), so creating track parameters there dereferences a null pointer.
issues.fix: Use FairRun::Instance() (GetField() is virtual in FairRun), check it for null, and return a zero field when there is no run.
issues.evidence: FairTrackPar.cxx:110-111 calls FairRunAna::Instance()->GetField() with no null check. fgRinstance is set only in the FairRunAna constructor (FairRunAna.cxx:60-64, 86). FairRunSim (FairRunSim.h:39) and FairRunOnline (FairRunOnline.h:29) derive from FairRun, and FairRun.cxx:55-58 stops a second run object from being made, so under them the pointer is always null. Every valued constructor and both SetTrackPar() calls GetFieldValue (for example FairTrackParP.cxx:148, 383, 641 and FairTrackParH.cxx:136, 229, 372), so a task under FairRunOnline, a task inside an MQ processor device, or a standalone macro that uses FairRKPropagator will segfault. I lower it to medium because every shipped user runs under FairRunAna (runProp.C:50, runTF.C:34), GEANE also needs FairRunAna (FairGeane.cxx:128), and the failure is a loud crash, not silent bad data.

issues.title: FairTrackParH LAB and copy constructors leave the q/p, lambda and phi errors at 0
issues.description: The LAB constructor (lines 157-248) and FairTrackParH(FairTrackPar&) (lines 545-640) fill the SC covariance matrix but never set fDQp, fDLm and fDPhi, which Reset() sets to 0. So GetDQp(), GetDLambda() and GetDPhi() return 0 although fCovMatrix[0], [5] and [9] hold the errors. The SC constructor and both SetTrackPar() overloads do set these members.
issues.fix: Set fDQp, fDLm and fDPhi from fCovMatrix[0], [5] and [9] after the conversion, as SetTrackPar() does.

issues.title: FairTrackParH LAB constructor divides by zero for charge 0
issues.description: The LAB constructor computes fq = q / TMath::Abs(q) with Int_t q. For q = 0 (a neutral particle) this is an integer division by zero, which kills the process with SIGFPE on x86. SetTrackPar() (lines 319-321) and the FairTrackParP LAB constructors guard this case with if (Q != 0).
issues.fix: Guard the division with if (q != 0), as SetTrackPar() does.

issues.title: Typo "contructor" in conversion error messages printed with cout
issues.description: FairTrackParH.cxx:300 prints 'FairTrackParH(FairTrackParP *) contructor ERROR: CANNOT convert parabola to helix', and FairTrackParP.cxx:577 has the same typo. Both messages go to cout instead of LOG(error), so they ignore the log settings.
issues.fix: Spell 'constructor' and print both messages with LOG(error).

issues.title: Self-assignments fDPx = GetDPx() in FairTrackParH::SetTrackPar()
issues.description: fDPx = GetDPx(); fDPy = GetDPy(); fDPz = GetDPz(); assign the members to themselves, because the getters return the same members. Lines 378-380 overwrite them anyway. The same lines appear at 434-436 and in CalCov() at 477-479.
issues.fix: Delete these lines.

issues.title: Private CalCov() in FairTrackParH and FairTrackParP is never called
issues.description: FairTrackParH::CalCov() is private (FairTrackParH.h:145) and nothing calls it. FairTrackParP::CalCov() (FairTrackParP.cxx:771-774) is empty ('not needed') and is also never called.
issues.fix: Remove both functions and their declarations.

issues.title: FairTrackParH(FairTrackPar&) prints a debug line to cout on every call
issues.description: The constructor starts with cout << 'FairTrackParH::FairTrackParH(FairTrackPar &Trkbase)'. Every conversion prints this line, which floods the output in a loop over tracks.
issues.fix: Remove the line or use LOG(debug).

issues.title: FairTrackParH(FairTrackPar&) does not normalize the charge to +1 or -1
issues.description: The copy constructor sets fq = Trkbase.GetQ() and fQp = fq / p without normalizing fq. All other FairTrackParH constructors normalize, and callers rely on that: FairTutPropTr passes the TDatabasePDG charge (3 for a mu+) to the FairTrackParP constructor. A FairTrackPar built the same way gives fq = 3 and a q/p three times too large after this conversion.
issues.fix: Normalize fq to the sign of the charge, with a guard for 0, as the other constructors do.

issues.title: FairTrackParH::Print() prints the object address and an unbalanced ')'
issues.description: Print() writes the object address (this) first and again in each of the 15 covariance lines. The position line ends with ')' without an opening '('. It writes to cout, ignores the option, and leaves std::cout at precision 2 for the rest of the program.
issues.fix: Print with LOG(info) like FairTrackPar::Print(), without the pointer and with balanced parentheses.

issues.title: FairTrackParH SC SetTrackPar() takes q/p before the angles, the SC constructor after
issues.description: The SC constructor takes (x, y, z, lambda, phi, qp, cov) (FairTrackParH.h:35-41), but the SC overload of SetTrackPar() takes (x, y, z, qp, lm, phi, cov). All of them are Double_t, so a call with the constructor's order compiles and silently mixes up q/p, lambda and phi.
issues.fix: Give both the same parameter order, for example by adding a correctly ordered setter and deprecating the old one.

issues.title: No guard for q/p = 0 in FairTrackParH/P SC and SD constructors and setters
issues.description: P = TMath::Abs(1 / fQp) has no check for q/p = 0 in the SD constructor (FairTrackParP.cxx:100), the SC constructor (FairTrackParH.cxx:87) and the SD and SC SetTrackPar() (FairTrackParP.cxx:698, FairTrackParH.cxx:403). For q/p = 0 the momentum becomes inf, products such as inf * 0 become NaN, and no message appears. The SD constructor with spu (FairTrackParP.cxx:216) has the guard.
issues.fix: Add the same if (fQp != 0) guard, with an error message, in these four places.

issues.title: FairTrackParP SD constructor without spu computes the momentum sign in mixed frames
issues.description: The SD constructor without spu sets SP1 = sign(momsd . (fjver x fkver)), but momsd = (fPx_sd, fPy_sd, fPz_sd) holds plane components (u, v, w) while fjver x fkver is a MARS vector. For a plane with j = x and k = y, SP1 becomes the sign of w', so a track with negative w' gets a reversed momentum, and w' = 0 gives 0/0 = NaN. fPx_sd is built as a positive root, so the only consistent value is +1; the constructor with spu and SetTrackPar() have this formula commented out and use 'SP1 = fSPU; // correct calculation of SP1'. Correction: Only the constructor with spu has 'SP1 = fSPU;   // correct calculation of SP1' (line 274). The SD SetTrackPar() has the old formula commented out at line 749 and a plain 'SP1 = fSPU;' at line 750, and the LAB SetTrackPar() gets SP1 from FromMarsToSD. Also, a track along the plane normal (v' = w' = 0) gives NaN for this plane.
issues.fix: Use SP1 = +1 and document that this constructor assumes a positive u momentum (or require spu as an argument).
issues.evidence: momsd at FairTrackParP.cxx:152 holds SD components (|pu|, v'|pu|, w'|pu|), built from the positive root at line 107, but line 153 dots it with fjver x fkver, which is the MARS u-axis set by SetPlane (lines 894-909). FromSDToMars multiplies the whole momentum by SP1 (FairGeaneUtil.cxx:1579-1595). For j = x and k = y, a track with w' < 0 therefore gets a reversed momentum, and w' = 0 gives NaN momentum and covariance. A standalone rerun of this math (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8ce3faed-3785-59d4-9dc9-2418f32b8a1f/scratchpad/issues/work-high-08/sp1check.cpp) gives SP1 = -1 and P = (-0.099, 0.099, -0.990) for v' = 0.1, w' = -0.1. The bug is real, but nothing in FairRoot calls this 9-argument constructor (all callers use the LAB constructor: FairTutPropTr.cxx:154/176, FairTutPropTrackFinder.cxx:134/164), so I rate it medium.

issues.title: FairTrackParP::Print() labels v' and w' as dx/dz and dy/dz
issues.description: Print() labels fTV and fTW as 'dx/dz' and 'dy/dz'. They are v' = dv/du and w' = dw/du in the plane frame, which equal dx/dz and dy/dz only for a plane with j = x and k = y.
issues.fix: Label them 'dv/du' and 'dw/du'.

issues.title: FairTrackParP::SetPlane() does not normalize k after making it orthogonal
issues.description: When j and k are not orthogonal, SetPlane() replaces k with (j x k) x j, whose length is sin(angle between j and k), and only normalizes i afterwards. fkver and fDK are then not unit vectors, but FromMARSToSDCoord(), FromSDToMARSCoord() and the FairGeaneUtil conversions treat them as unit vectors. So w, w' and the covariance come out scaled.
issues.fix: Call k.SetMag(1.) after the orthogonalization.

issues.title: FairTrackParP header comment describes a helix instead of the parabola (SD)
issues.description: The header comment of the parabola (SD) class says 'GEANE parameters (q/p, v', w', v, w) of Helix track' and 'Helix parameter (1/p, v', w', v, w) in SC reference'. The text was copied from FairTrackParH.h, and FairTrackParP.cxx:13-15 repeats it.
issues.fix: Describe the parabola track and the SD reference instead.

issues.title: Installed unpack_mbs.C cannot find sample_data_2.lmd and then crashes
issues.description: The install step puts sample_data_2.lmd into .../MbsTutorial/data and unpack_mbs.C into .../MbsTutorial/macros, but the macro opens 'sample_data_2.lmd' by a relative path (unpack_mbs.C:14). Run in the installed macros folder, as README.md says, FairLmdSource::AddFile() logs 'FairLmdSource: not found' and FairLmdSource::Init() returns kFALSE. FairRunOnline::Init() ignores the result of InitSource() (FairRunOnline.cxx:118), so the first ReadEvent() calls f_evt_get_event() with a null channel and crashes. The macro computes 'tutdir' (line 11) but never uses it.
issues.fix: Install the data file next to the macro (or open it through 'tutdir'), and make FairRunOnline::Init() stop when InitSource() fails.

install(TARGETS ${target} LIBRARY DESTINATION ${PROJECT_INSTALL_LIBDIR})
install(FILES ${headers} DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR})
install(FILES sample_data_2.lmd DESTINATION ${PROJECT_INSTALL_DATADIR}/examples/advanced/MbsTutorial/data)

GENERATE_ROOT_TEST_SCRIPT(${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/unpack_mbs.C)

issues.title: FairMBSUnpack::DoUnpack() reads past the subevent for odd or corrupt block sizes
issues.description: DoUnpack() takes the block size from the low 9 bits of each header word and reads p1[i1] and p1[i1 + 1] (lines 82-87) with no check against 'size'. A corrupt header word makes it read up to 511 words past the subevent. An odd block size makes the last pair read one word past the block and moves l_i one word too far for the next header. examples/MQ/Lmd/FairMBSUnpacker.cxx:46-88 has the same code; the sample file has only even, in-range blocks.
issues.fix: Before the inner loop, check that l_i + l_da_siz <= size and that l_da_siz is even, and return kFALSE otherwise.

issues.title: FairMBSUnpack adds the running event count to fNHitsTotal after each subevent
issues.description: Reset() clears fNHits only once per event (FairRootManager::ReadEvent() calls FairSource::Reset()), but DoUnpack() runs once per matching subevent and adds the running fNHits to fNHitsTotal each time. So when two subevents of one event match the unpacker (for example with subCrate -1), GetNHitsTotal() counts the items of the first subevent twice. The sample file has at most one matching subevent per event (parsed: 100 of 300 events, 9086 items), and examples/MQ/Lmd is safe because FairMQUnpacker calls Reset() after each DoUnpack().
issues.fix: Add only the items of the current call to fNHitsTotal, for example by counting them in a local variable.

issues.title: unpack_mbs.C turns off auto-finish but never calls Finish(), so output.root has no tree
issues.description: The macro calls run->SetAutoFinish(kFALSE), so FairRunOnline::Run() skips Finish(), and the macro never calls run->Finish() itself. So FinishTask(), FairRootManager::LastFill(), FairRootManager::Write() (which writes the cbmsim tree), the source Close() and CloseSink() never run, and output.root gets no tree. The CTest test does not notice, because it checks only GetNHitsTotal().
issues.fix: Call run->Finish() after run->Run(0, 400), or remove the SetAutoFinish(kFALSE) call.

issues.title: propagator conf.xml styles Pixel101_0 to Pixel104_0, which do not exist
issues.description: FairEventManager::LoadXMLDetector() matches the entries by exact node name. The second detector (tutProp2.geo) has the volumes Pixel5 to Pixel8, so the entries Pixel101_0 to Pixel104_0 match nothing, and the second detector gets none of the configured colors and transparency.
issues.fix: Rename the entries to Pixel5_0 to Pixel8_0.

        <detector name="Pixel4_0" color="kRed+3" transparency="30"  recursive="0"></detector>
        <detector name="Pixel101_0" color="kCyan" transparency="30"  recursive="0"></detector>

        <detector name="Pixel104_0" color="kCyan+3" transparency="30"  recursive="0"></detector>
    </detector>
</Detectors>

issues.title: propagator eventDisplay.C crashes when conf.xml is not in the working directory
issues.description: eventDisplay.C passes the relative path "conf.xml" to SetXMLConfig(), but macros/CMakeLists.txt does not copy conf.xml to the build folder, where the tests write prop.mc.root and prop.par.root. When the file is missing, TDOMParser::ParseFile() fails, and FairXMLFile dereferences the null GetXMLDocument() result because it does not check the return code (fairroot/eventdisplay/FairXMLNode.cxx:141-142). So the macro crashes in any folder except the source macros folder.
issues.fix: Copy conf.xml to the build folder with configure_file() (or build its path from VMCWORKDIR), and make FairXMLFile check the ParseFile() result.

issues.title: Commented-out SetSimulationConfig(new FairVMCConfig()) no longer compiles
issues.description: FairRunSim::SetSimulationConfig() takes a std::unique_ptr<FairGenericVMCConfig> (FairRunSim.h:188), and a raw pointer does not convert to it. So a user who uncomments the line gets a compile error. The same line is in runMM.C:52 and examples/MQ/pixelDetector/src/devices/FairMQSimDevice.cxx:60.
issues.fix: Change it to run.SetSimulationConfig(std::make_unique<FairVMCConfig>()); or remove it in all three files.

issues.title: Comment '// 1 cm' is wrong for SetStepSizeCut(0.01), which means 0.1 mm
issues.description: FairMCApplication compares the cut with TVirtualMC::TrackStep(), which is in cm (FairMCApplication.cxx:571), so SetStepSizeCut(0.01) means 0.1 mm, not 1 cm. The same wrong comment is in examples/simulation/Tutorial4/macros/run_tutorial4.C:138, examples/simulation/rutherford/macros/run_rad.C:115 and run_rutherford.C:134, and examples/advanced/Tutorial3/macro/run_sim.C:119 and run_sim_sep.C:96.
issues.fix: Change the comment to '// 0.1 mm' in all six macros.

issues.title: runMM.C gives both FairTutPropDet modules the name "TutPropDetector"
issues.description: Lines 68 and 72 create two FairTutPropDet modules with the same name, while runMC.C names the second one "TutPropDetector2". The points still go to separate branches, but logs and the module list cannot tell the detectors apart, and FairMCApplication::GetDetector("TutPropDetector2") returns null.
issues.fix: Name the second detector "TutPropDetector2", as runMC.C does.

issues.title: runProp.C("geane") crashes: Geant3_FOUND is never defined, so no propagator is set
issues.description: The Geane code sits inside '#ifdef Geant3_FOUND' (lines 67 and 83), but nothing defines this macro for the ROOT interpreter, so these blocks never run. With "geane" the macro adds no FairGeane task and never calls SetPropagator(). FairTutPropTr::Exec() then calls InitPropagator(), which dereferences the null fPro (FairTutPropTr.cxx:97). CTest runs only the default "rk" mode, so no test sees this.
issues.fix: Replace the #ifdef blocks with a run-time check (for example TClass::GetClass("FairGeanePro")), and let FairTutPropTr::Init() return kFATAL when no propagator is set.

issues.title: runPull.C fills residuals, not pulls, and returns 0 when its check fails
issues.description: The macro and its CTest test are named 'Pull', but the histograms get final minus propagated values (residuals); the pull lines 69-74 are commented out. The macro also returns 0 when the mean or sigma check fails (line 114). The test still works through PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION, but a caller that checks the return code sees success.
issues.fix: Call the histograms residuals (or fill real pulls once errors are propagated) and return 1 when the check fails.

issues.title: propagator/src/CMakeLists.txt passes the unset variable defs
issues.description: target_compile_definitions(${target} PUBLIC ${defs}) uses the variable defs, which nothing in this directory scope sets (only examples/advanced/Tutorial3/CMakeLists.txt sets its own). So the call adds no definition; a scratch test confirms the target gets no COMPILE_DEFINITIONS.
issues.fix: Remove the line.

excerpt.code:
set_target_properties(${target} PROPERTIES ${PROJECT_LIBRARY_PROPERTIES})

target_compile_definitions(${target} PUBLIC ${defs})

target_include_directories(${target} PUBLIC

issues.title: FairEveRecoTracksExample dereferences a null MCTrack array when the branch is missing
issues.description: Init() only logs a warning when the MCTrack branch is missing (lines 213-216) and keeps fDrawMC at its default kTRUE (line 55). SetDrawMC() cannot clear it then, because it changes fDrawMC only when fContainerSim is set. DrawTrack() then calls fContainerSim->UncheckedAt() on a null pointer for each track with an MC index, so the display crashes on input without MC tracks.
issues.fix: Set fDrawMC to kFALSE in Init() when fContainerSim is null, or check fContainerSim in DrawTrack().

issues.title: FairTutPropTr::Exec() uses an unrelated end point when a track has none at z >= 35
issues.description: The inner loop assigns point2 before it checks z >= 35 and the track ID. If the track has no such point, point2 ends as the last point of the array, which can belong to another track, and the task stores it as the MC truth at the end plane. The check 'if (point2 == 0) break;' never fires, and its 'break' would end the whole event instead of skipping one track.
issues.fix: Set point2 only when a point passes both checks, and continue with the next track when none does.

issues.title: FairTutPropTr propagates every track as mu+ (PDG -13), also the generated electrons
issues.description: Exec() uses PDGCode = -13 (charge +1) for the start parameters and for Propagate() of every track. runMC.C generates pi+ (211), e- (11) and protons (2212), so the electrons, one third of the tracks, bend the wrong way, and the 'wrong charge' array holds their correct result. The comment at runMC.C:28 calls them 'eplus'. Most of these tracks fall outside the 0.1 cm window of the runPull.C histograms, so the test does not notice.
issues.fix: Take the PDG code and charge of each track from its MCTrack, or generate e+ (-11) in runMC.C as its comment says.

issues.title: FairTutPropTrackFinder starts a track first seen in the second hit array at count 2
issues.description: Exec() counts the hits of each track in a map. A track whose first hit is in fHitsArray2 enters the map with count 2 instead of 1. So a track with only two hits, both in the second detector, passes the 'at least 3 hits' cut at line 114.
issues.fix: Insert the new track with count 1 at line 107.

issues.title: Tutorial3 CMakeLists.txt adds the include directory MQ/run, which does not exist
issues.description: target_include_directories() of ExTestDetector lists ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/MQ/run, but this directory no longer exists. The build still works, because the compiler ignores a missing -I path, but the entry is stale.
issues.fix: Remove the MQ/run line.

excerpt.code:
$<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/MQ/fileSink>
$<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/MQ/processorTask>
$<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/MQ/run>
$<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/MQ/samplerTask>
$<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/reconstruction>

issues.title: FairTestDetectorDigiTask is named "TestDetectorDigTask" and logs with std::cout
issues.description: The constructor passes the name "TestDetectorDigTask" (an "i" is missing) to FairTask, and FairRoot prints this name in its task messages. Init() also prints its errors with std::cout and "-E-"/"-W-" prefixes (lines 34-35 and 41-42) instead of LOG, as its own TODO says, so the logger settings do not apply to them.
issues.fix: Rename the task to "FairTestDetectorDigiTask" and replace the std::cout calls with LOG(error) and LOG(warn).

excerpt.code:
FairTestDetectorDigiTask::FairTestDetectorDigiTask()
    : FairTask("TestDetectorDigTask")
    , fTimeResolution(0.)
    , fPointArray(nullptr)

issues.title: Digi time-stamp error is sqrt(resolution), not the Gaussian width used for the smearing
issues.description: Exec() sets the time-stamp error to fTimeResolution / TMath::Sqrt(fTimeResolution), which is sqrt(fTimeResolution) and not even in ns. CalcTimeStamp() smears the time with gRandom->Gaus(0, fTimeResolution), so the real width is fTimeResolution. FairTestDetectorTimeDigiTask.cxx:77 uses the same formula, and with its default resolution of 100 ns every time-based digi gets an error of 10 instead of 100.
issues.fix: Set the time-stamp error to fTimeResolution in both tasks.

issues.title: CalcPad() truncates toward zero, so the hits of negative pads land outside their pad
issues.description: CalcPad() computes static_cast<Int_t>(posIn + posOut) / 2. Both the cast and the integer division round toward zero, so pad 0 covers -1 to +1 cm and a pad n < 0 covers (n-1, n]. The reco tasks put the hit at pad + 0.5 (FairTestDetectorRecoTask.cxx:74, FairTestDetectorTimeRecoTask.cxx:85), so a point at x = -1.5 cm gets a hit at -0.5 cm, outside its pad (checked with a copy of the function). run_sim.C shoots in all phi directions, so about half of the x and y values are negative, and FairTestDetectorTimeDigiTask::CalcPad() (timeBasedSimulation/FairTestDetectorTimeDigiTask.cxx:93) has the same code.
issues.fix: Use static_cast<Int_t>(std::floor((posIn + posOut) / 2)) in both CalcPad() functions.

issues.title: FairTestDetectorHitProducerSmearing::Init() aborts: branch and folder names are equal
issues.description: Init() calls ioman->Register("FairTestDetectorHit", "FairTestDetectorHit", fHitsArray, kTRUE). FairRootManager::RegisterImpl() stops with LOG(fatal) when the object name equals the folder name (fairroot/base/steer/FairRootManager.cxx:158-162), so every run that adds this task aborts in Init(). The class is built and listed in FairTestDetectorLinkDef.h, but no macro or test uses it, so the error stays hidden.
issues.fix: Register the hits in a different folder, for example "FairTestDetector" as FairTestDetectorRecoTask::Init() does.

issues.title: run_digi_timebased.C sets the screen level to DEBUG, but the log file caps output at info
issues.description: SetLogFileName("MyLog.log") opens the file sink with FairLogger's default file severity "info", and line 21 then sets the console severity to DEBUG. Since FairLogger 1.9.0, fair::Logger::UpdateMinSeverity() takes std::max(console, file), but 1.9.0 reversed the severity order, so the global threshold becomes info. LOG(debug) then writes nothing, to the console or to the file, so the requested debug output never appears. Every macro that opens a log file and raises only the screen level hits the same trap.
issues.fix: Also call SetLogFileLevel("DEBUG") in the macro (or drop SetLogFileName()), and ask FairLogger to use std::min in Logger::UpdateMinSeverity().

issues.title: AddIncludeType(0) keeps only links to GeoTracks, so the digis and hits store no links
issues.description: run_digi.C:51 and run_reco.C:47 call FairLinkManager::Instance()->AddIncludeType(0), so FairMultiLinkedData::InsertLink() drops every link whose branch ID is not 0. FairFileSource::Init() takes the branch IDs from the input BranchList, and the simulation registers GeoTracks first: run_sim.C:110 turns on trajectories, and FairMCApplication::InitGeometry() calls FairTrajFilter::Init() before RegisterOutput() registers MCTrack and FairTestDetectorPoint (FairMCApplication.cxx:857-875). So branch 0 is GeoTracks, and no digi or hit links to it. The digis and hits store empty link sets, although both macros call SetUseFairLinks(kTRUE).
issues.fix: Remove the AddIncludeType(0) calls, or call AddIncludeType() after Init() with IDs from FairRootManager::GetBranchId() for the wanted branches.

issues.title: run_reco_timebased.C never calls SetSource(), so its CTest passes without reading data
issues.description: The macro creates a FairFileSource at line 44 but never passes it to fRun->SetSource(). Without a source, GetObject("FairTestDetectorSortedDigi") returns nullptr, so FairTestDetectorTimeRecoTask::Init() logs a warning and returns kERROR, which switches the task off. RunTSBuffers() then makes one empty pass, and the macro still prints "Macro finished successfully." (line 88). The ex_tutorial3_reco_timebased_* tests match only that line, so they pass without processing any digi.
issues.fix: Call fRun->SetSource(fFileSource) after line 44, and make the test check real output (for example the number of hits), not only the final message.

issues.title: Tutorial 3 macros default to different MC engines, so a run without arguments fails
issues.description: run_sim.C:31 and run_digi.C:17 default to "TGeant4", but run_reco.C:13, run_digi_timebased.C:13, run_reco_timebased.C:13, eventDisplay.C:8 and the split-file macros default to "TGeant3". MQ/start.sh.in reads TGeant3 files, while MQ/test.sh.in reads TGeant4 files. Run without arguments, run_reco.C opens data/testdigi_TGeant3.root, which run_digi.C did not write, and FairFileSourceBase stops with LOG(fatal) "Error opening the Input file". The CTests pass the engine explicitly, so they do not catch it.
issues.fix: Use one default engine in all Tutorial 3 macros and in MQ/start.sh.in, preferably TGeant4, which the CTests always run.

issues.title: run_sim.C comment "13 = muon; 1 = multipl." does not match FairBoxGenerator(2212, 10)
issues.description: Line 101 creates FairBoxGenerator(2212, 10), which makes 10 protons per event. The comment on the same line describes a muon (PDG code 13) with multiplicity 1.
issues.fix: Change the comment to "2212 = proton; 10 = multiplicity".

excerpt.code:
// Box Generator
FairBoxGenerator *boxGen = new FairBoxGenerator(2212, 10);   // 13 = muon; 1 = multipl.
boxGen->SetPRange(2., 2.);                                   // GeV/c //setPRange vs setPtRange
boxGen->SetPhiRange(0, 360);                                 // Azimuth angle range [degree]

issues.title: MQRecoTask Exec() checks fDigiArray for null only after it has used it
issues.description: MQRecoTask<TestDetectorBin>::Exec() calls fRecoTask.fDigiArray->Clear() at line 24 and fills the array at lines 26-30, and only then tests the pointer for null at line 32. The check can never fire: a null pointer would crash first, and MQRecoTask::Init() always creates the array. MQRecoTaskFlatBuffers.h:39 and MQRecoTaskProtobuf.h:35 have the same dead check.
issues.fix: Remove these checks, or move them before the first use of fDigiArray.

issues.title: MQ binary path sends uninitialized hit time stamps, and the sink output loses the times
issues.description: MQRecoTask<TestDetectorBin>::Exec() calls Rebuild(hitsSize) and fills every Payload::Hit field except fTimeStamp and fTimeStampError, which Payload::Hit inherits from Payload::TimeStamp, so 16 bytes per hit go out uninitialized. FileSink<TestDetectorBin> ignores them, so the stored hits keep the FairTimeStamp default of -1 instead of the times that FairTestDetectorRecoTask::Exec() set. The protobuf processor (MQRecoTaskProtobuf.h:48-56) also never sets the time fields, and the protobuf and flatbuffers sinks drop them. Only the boost and tmessage formats keep the hit times.
issues.fix: Fill output[i].fTimeStamp and output[i].fTimeStampError (and the protobuf time fields), and call SetTimeStamp() and SetTimeStampError() on the hits in the binary, protobuf and flatbuffers sinks.

issues.title: Sampler class comment says the digis go out as a "UDP stream"
issues.description: The class comment says the sampler sends the digis "as a time-series UDP stream". The device sends one FairMQ message per tree entry on its output channel, and the channel configuration picks the transport (ipc in test.sh, tcp in start.sh); no UDP is involved.
issues.fix: Describe the output as FairMQ messages, one per event, on the configured output channel.

excerpt.code:
/**
 * Reads simulated digis from a root file and samples the digi as a time-series UDP stream.
 * Must be initialized with the filename to the root file and the name of the sub-detector
 * branch, whose digis should be streamed.

issues.title: Tutorial 3 sampler never deletes its FairRunAna, so a second InitTask() aborts the device
issues.description: Sampler::InitTask() creates a new FairRunAna (line 75), but ResetTask() (lines 145-151) only calls TerminateRun() and deletes the task, and the destructor deletes nothing. FairMQ allows INIT TASK again after RESET TASK, for example by key press in the default interactive control mode that start.sh uses. The second new FairRunAna() then hits Fatal("Singleton instance already exists.") in the FairRun constructor (fairroot/base/steer/FairRun.cxx:55-58), and ROOT aborts the device. FairMQPixelSampler::InitTask() (examples/MQ/pixelDetector/src/devices/FairMQPixelSampler.cxx:53) has the same problem.
issues.fix: Delete fFairRunAna in ResetTask() and reset both pointers (the run's task list already owns the sampler task, so drop the separate delete), or set the run up only once so InitTask() never builds a second FairRunAna.

issues.title: Error text "Invalid valid data format provided" repeats a word in all three MQ devices
issues.description: fairGetDevice() throws "Invalid valid data format provided (--data-format): ..." when --data-format has an unknown value. The same text is in MQ/processor.cxx:122 and MQ/sink.cxx:60.
issues.fix: Change the text to "Invalid data format provided (--data-format)" in all three files.

issues.title: test.sh prints "Usage: start.sh ..." in its own usage message
issues.description: test.sh.in was copied from start.sh.in and kept its usage line. So test.sh prints "Usage: start.sh [data_format[=binary]]" when it gets more than one argument.
issues.fix: Change the text to "Usage: test.sh [data_format[=binary]]".

excerpt.code:
dataFormat=$1
elif (($# > 1)); then
    echo "Usage: start.sh [data_format[=binary]]"
    exit
fi

issues.title: Reco tasks warn "No Point array!" when the missing input is the digi branch
issues.description: FairTestDetectorRecoTask::Init() warns "No Point array!" when GetObject("FairTestDetectorDigi") fails, and FairTestDetectorTimeRecoTask.cxx:51 prints the same text when FairTestDetectorSortedDigi is missing. The text sends the user to the wrong branch. MQRecoTaskBin.h:33, MQRecoTaskBoost.h:23, MQRecoTaskFlatBuffers.h:40 and MQRecoTaskProtobuf.h:36 use the same text for the digi array.
issues.fix: Name the missing branch in the messages, for example "No FairTestDetectorDigi array!".

issues.title: Clear() on the point and hit arrays leaks each object's FairMultiLinkedData every event
issues.description: FairTestDetector::EndOfEvent() (line 118) and FairTestDetector::Reset() (line 142) empty the point array with TClonesArray::Clear(), and FairTestDetectorRecoTask::Exec() does the same with the hit array (reconstruction/FairTestDetectorRecoTask.cxx:59). Clear() runs no destructors, and the next placement new into the same slot overwrites the old object. With links on (run_sim.C:49, run_reco.C:46), every point and hit owns a heap FairMultiLinkedData through the std::unique_ptr fLink, so one link set leaks per reused slot per event. Clear("C") does not help, because FairMultiLinkedData_Interface has no Clear() that frees fLink.
issues.fix: Use Delete() instead of Clear() in FairTestDetector::EndOfEvent(), FairTestDetector::Reset() and FairTestDetectorRecoTask::Exec(), as FairTestDetectorDigiTask::Exec() already does.

issues.title: FairTestDetectorTimeDigiTask::Exec() leaks one digi per MC point
issues.description: Exec() creates each digi with new (line 75) and passes it to FairWriteoutBuffer::FillNewData() (line 87). FillNewData() stores a Clone() of the digi (fairroot/base/steer/FairWriteoutBuffer.cxx:140) and does not take the original. Nothing deletes the original, so each MC point of each event leaks one FairTestDetectorDigi, and also its link set when links are on.
issues.fix: Create the digi on the stack, or delete it after FillNewData(), because the buffer keeps its own clone.

issues.title: FairTestDetectorTimeRecoTask adds the hit-to-digi link twice, so it gets weight 2
issues.description: Exec() calls hit->AddLink(digi->GetEntryNr()) and then hit->AddInterfaceData(digi). AddInterfaceData() adds digi->GetEntryNr() a second time (fairroot/base/event/FairMultiLinkedData_Interface.cxx:179-180), and InsertLink() adds up the weights of equal links. So the link from each hit to its digi gets weight 2 instead of 1.
issues.fix: Remove the AddLink(digi->GetEntryNr()) call and keep only AddInterfaceData(digi).

issues.title: FairTestDetectorTimeRecoTask::Exec() sorts the hit array again after every digi
issues.description: fHitArray->Sort() sits inside the loop over the digis, so the array is sorted again after each new hit. Each new slot resets the sorted flag of the TClonesArray, so every one of these sorts really runs, and all but the last one are wasted work (O(n^2 log n) per Exec()).
issues.fix: Move fHitArray->Sort() after the loop.

issues.title: ExEventDisplay is built only when Geant3 is found, although it does not use Geant3
issues.description: examples/CMakeLists.txt adds common/eventdisplay (library ExEventDisplay, which holds FairMCTracksDraw) only inside if(Geant3_FOUND). The library links FairRoot::EventDisplay, FairRoot::TrackBase, ExMCStack and ROOT, but not Geant3. In a build without Geant3, the eventDisplay.C macros of rutherford, Tutorial1, Tutorial3, Tutorial4, propagator and pixelDetector fail because FairMCTracksDraw is unknown.
issues.fix: Move the if(TARGET FairRoot::EventDisplay) block out of the if(Geant3_FOUND) block.

issues.title: examples/common/input is not installed, so the installed run_tutorial1_urqmd.C fails
issues.description: The install() rule copies only common/gconfig and common/geometry to share/fairbase/examples/common. examples/simulation/Tutorial1/macros/CMakeLists.txt:72 installs run_tutorial1_urqmd.C, which reads urqmd.ftn14 and urqmd_pdg.dat from $VMCWORKDIR/common/input. With the installed config, VMCWORKDIR is <prefix>/share/fairbase/examples, where common/input does not exist, so the installed macro cannot find its input.
issues.fix: Add common/input to the install(DIRECTORY ...) list.

excerpt.code:
endif()

install(DIRECTORY
  common/gconfig
  common/geometry
  DESTINATION ${PROJECT_INSTALL_DATADIR}/examples/common
)

issues.title: FairMCTracksDraw.h declares three methods that are never defined
issues.description: CheckCuts(), DrawTrack() and GetTrackGroup() are declared, but they have no definition and no caller. The real code is in FairEveMCTracks, and a derived class that calls them gets a link error.
issues.fix: Remove the three declarations and the forward declarations that only they need.

issues.title: flConfig.C and UserDecay.C call TVirtual::GetMC(); class TVirtual does not exist
issues.description: flConfig.C (lines 19-20) and UserDecay.C (line 40) call TVirtual::GetMC() instead of TVirtualMC::GetMC(), so Cling cannot compile either macro. For TFluka, FairGenericVMCConfig::Setup() then finds no Config(), no engine is created, and the run stops; with SetUserDecay(kTRUE), FairMCApplication::AddDecayModes() skips UserDecayConfig() after the load error. The header comment of flConfig.C (line 8) also calls this Fluka macro a Geant3 configuration.
issues.fix: Replace TVirtual::GetMC() with TVirtualMC::GetMC() in both macros and fix the comment on line 8.

issues.title: g3Config_new.C has a syntax error (1. e - 3) and nothing loads it
issues.description: 'Float_t cut = 1. e - 3;' does not parse, so the macro fails if a user selects it with SetUserConfig(). No code or example refers to the file, and the Tutorial4 copy has the same error.
issues.fix: Delete both copies, or write 1.e-3.

issues.title: g4Config.C and g4ConfigPostInit.C hard-code $VMCWORKDIR/common/gconfig
issues.description: Config() reads g4config.in from $VMCWORKDIR/common/gconfig, and g4ConfigPostInit.C:13 does the same for g4configPostInit.in. This is right for FairRoot's own examples, but in a copy in a project with another layout, or with an edited g4config.in in CONFIG_DIR, the file is silently not used; only Geant4 prints that it cannot open the macro file. The Tutorial4 copy builds the path from CONFIG_DIR (Tutorial4/gconfig/g4Config.C:58).
issues.fix: Build both paths from CONFIG_DIR.

Nothing reads the link: FairGenericVMCConfig::Setup() loads flConfig.C by full path from CONFIG_DIR or $VMCWORKDIR/gconfig. Tutorial4/gconfig/run_fluka.sh has the same line.

issues.title: SetCuts.C defines cutb (10 TeV) but never uses it
issues.description: The comment describes a GEANE setup with BCUTE, BCUTM, DCUTE, DCUTM and PPCUTM at 10 TeV, but all SetCut() calls use cut1. So cutb is an unused variable.
issues.fix: Remove cutb, or use it in a commented GEANE variant of the cuts.

issues.title: double_sector.geo comment says tutdet2 is at z = 300 mm, but it is at 302 mm
issues.description: The comment line before tutdet2 (line 16) repeats 'WAFER z= 300 mm' from tutdet1. The position line of tutdet2 (line 29) places it at z = 302 mm.
issues.fix: Change the comment on line 16 to z= 302 mm.

issues.title: kTutProp and kPixel come after kSTOPHERE, so FairStack ignores their points
issues.description: The comment on line 14 says that all detectors must come before kSTOPHERE, but kTutProp and kPixel come after it. SelectTracks() and FillTrackArray() loop only from kREF to kSTOPHERE (FairStack.cxx:414, 223), so the AddPoint() calls of FairTutPropDet (line 111) and Pixel (line 126) never count, and FairMCTrack has no bits for these IDs. With SetMinPoints(n > 0) (the FairStack default is 1; the shipped configs set 0), secondaries with points only in these detectors are dropped from the MCTrack output.
issues.fix: Move kSTOPHERE after kPixel and add bit ranges for kTutProp and kPixel in FairMCTrack::GetNPoints() and SetNPoints().

issues.title: FairMCTrack.h documents another experiment's fNPoints bit layout
issues.description: The comment on fNPoints lists CBM detectors (REF, MVD, STS, RICH, MUCH, TRD, TOF, ECAL, ZDC) up to bit 25. The code packs only kREF in bit 0, kTutDet in bits 1-3 and kFairRutherford in bits 4-8 (FairMCTrack.cxx:115-161, which says 'TODO: Where does this come from').
issues.fix: Describe the real layout: REF bit 0, TutDet bits 1-3, Rutherford bits 4-8, bits 9-31 free.

 **  RICH:        Bit  9      (1 bit,  max. value  1)

issues.title: PopPrimaryForTracking() ignores toBeDone, so Geant4 transports untracked primaries
issues.description: PushTrack() puts a particle on fStack only when toBeDone is 1, but PopPrimaryForTracking() returns every primary from fParticles. TVirtualMCStack documents that it must pop only primaries with toBeDone 1, and Geant4 VMC (TG4PrimaryGeneratorAction::TransformPrimaries()) transports every non-null particle it gets for i < GetNtrack(). So FairPrimaryGenerator::DoTracking(kFALSE) and AddTrack(..., wanttracking=false) work with Geant3, which uses PopNextTrack(), but have no effect with Geant4. The template stacks (MyProjStack.cxx:197-216) have the same code.
issues.fix: Store toBeDone per particle in PushTrack() and return nullptr from PopPrimaryForTracking() when it is 0.

issues.title: UpdateTrackIndex() leaks one TIterator per event on Geant4 MT worker stacks
issues.description: When fDetList is null, UpdateTrackIndex() assigns detList->MakeIterator() to fDetIter at every call and never deletes the old iterator. Worker stacks always have a null fDetList: CloneStack() uses the default constructor, and only FairMCApplication::RunMC() on the master calls SetDetArrayList() (FairMCApplication.cxx:299). So in a Geant4 multi-threaded run each worker leaks one iterator per event (FinishEvent() calls UpdateTrackIndex(), FairMCApplication.cxx:648).
issues.fix: When fDetList is null, call SetDetArrayList(detList) once (or delete fDetIter first); MyProjStack.cxx:303-306 in the templates has the same code.

issues.title: FairStack.h class comment has a cut-off sentence and typos
issues.description: The filter description stops in the middle of a sentence ('...and a minimal energy, or are the', line 28), and lines 20-21 have the typos 'functunality' and 'arry'. It also says that the point minimum uses the 'sum of all detectors', which is true only for detector IDs before kSTOPHERE.
issues.fix: Finish the sentence (for example '...or are the mother of a stored track'), fix the typos, and mention the kSTOPHERE limit.

issues.title: FairCave::world[3] is set and copied but never read
issues.description: The name constructor sets world[] to 0 and the copy constructor copies it, but no code reads it. The default constructor leaves it uninitialized, and as a persistent member it is still streamed with every FairCave.
issues.fix: Remove world[] and increase the ClassDef version of FairCave.

issues.title: Loading libExPassive makes every FairRunAna job request FairConstPar
issues.description: The static gFairConstFieldCreator registers itself as FairFieldFactory::Instance() when libExPassive is loaded. FairRunAna::Init() and FairRunAnaProof::Init() call SetParm() before they check fField, so the job requests 'FairConstPar' even when the macro sets its own field. If the parameter input has no FairConstPar, initContainers() then logs 'FairConstPar(FairConstPar)::init(): failed' and 'FairRunAna::Init: fRtdb->initContainers failed'.
issues.fix: Call SetParm() only when no field is set, or create the field creator in the macros that need it instead of as a static global.

issues.title: createFairField() logs as 'FairRunAna::GetField' and prints 'New field at 0'
issues.description: The warning for an unknown field type in FairConstFieldCreator::createFairField() names the wrong function: 'FairRunAna::GetField: Unknown field type'. Line 52 then logs 'New field at 0, type N' although no field was created.
issues.fix: Name FairConstFieldCreator::createFairField() in the warning, and log 'New field' only when fMagneticField is set.

issues.title: FairGeoCave::read() silently uses an empty medium when the cave medium is unknown
issues.description: When getMedium() does not find the cave's medium name (a typo, or trailing blanks on the line), read() adds an unnamed, empty FairGeoMedium and uses it without a message. FairGeoSet::readVolumeParams() reports the same case as an error and returns kFALSE. templates/project_*_containers/passive/MyGeoCave.cxx:68 has the same code.
issues.fix: Log an error with the medium name and return kFALSE, as FairGeoSet::readVolumeParams() does.

issues.title: FairPipe crashes with the example media.geo: 'steel' and 'Al+Be' are missing
issues.description: ConstructGeometry() takes 'steel' and 'Al+Be' from the media list, but examples/common/geometry/media.geo does not define them (only the template media.geo files do). getMedium() returns nullptr, and FairGeoRootBuilder::createMedium() dereferences it, because its guard is '!geoManager && !med'. Lines 61-63 also call createMedium() unconditionally, so a medium that another module already created (for example 'vacuum') gets a second TGeoMedium. No example uses FairPipe now.
issues.fix: Check the three pointers (or add the two media to the example media.geo) and call createMedium() only when getMediumIndex() <= 0.

issues.title: Histogram device and server break after ResetTask and a second InitTask
issues.description: FairMQExHistoDevice::InitTask() adds the four histograms to fArrayHisto without clearing it, and the device has no ResetTask(). After ResetTask and a new InitTask, each histogram is in the array twice, so the server adds it twice per message. On the server, a second InitTask() calls CreateCanvases() again, and assert(!fCanvas) (FairMQExHistoCanvasDrawerExample.cxx:27) aborts, because FairRoot's RelWithDebInfo flags ('-O2 -g', CheckCompiler.cmake:72) do not define NDEBUG.
issues.fix: Clear fArrayHisto in InitTask() (or add ResetTask()), and let CreateCanvases() handle an existing canvas.

issues.title: Histogram device sends one message object on every channel; later sends are empty
issues.description: ConditionalRun() serializes once and calls Send(message, ...) for every channel. The zeromq transport passes the same zmq_msg_t to zmq_msg_send(), which empties it after a successful send, so every channel after the first gets a 0-byte message, and the server does not check the size. It works only because fairmq-start-ex-histo.sh gives each device one channel.
issues.fix: Serialize (or Copy()) a new message for each channel inside the loop.

issues.title: Histogram server dereferences a null object when deserialization gives nullptr
issues.description: ReceiveData() calls tempObject->ClassName() without a null check. RootSerializer().Deserialize() returns nullptr, for example for a serialized null pointer, and the server then crashes. The example's own devices always send a TObjArray, so only foreign or malformed input triggers it.
issues.fix: Log a warning and return true when tempObject is nullptr.

issues.title: Histogram server leaks the four received histograms on every message
issues.description: ReceiveData() gets a TObjArray that is not an owner, because TObject::Streamer() restores the kIsOwner bit of the device's plain TObjArray. So arrayHisto->Clear() (line 67) and delete tempObject (line 72) free only the array, and the deserialized TH1 objects belong to no directory (TH1::Streamer() sets fDirectory to nullptr). With the shipped script (four devices, one message about every 10 ms each), the server loses about 20 KB per message and runs out of memory.
issues.fix: Call arrayHisto->Delete() instead of Clear() (or SetOwner(kTRUE) before delete tempObject).
issues.evidence: The device array is a plain TObjArray (FairMQExHistoDevice.cxx:33-36), and TObject::Streamer reads fBits back, so the received array is not an owner. ROOT's TObjArray::Clear() and ~TObjArray() delete the elements only for an owner, so the four histograms are lost at FairMQExHistoServer.cxx:67 and 72. TH1::Streamer sets fDirectory to nullptr, so no directory frees them either. The bin arrays alone are 18.9 KB per message, and four devices that sleep 10 ms (FairMQExHistoDevice.cxx:68) send about 400 messages/s, so the server grows by several MB/s. The leak is real, but it is in an example, it gives no wrong data, and memory runs out only after a long run, so I rate it medium.

issues.title: fStopThread is a plain bool shared by the device thread and the HTTP thread
issues.description: PostRun() writes fStopThread on the device thread, and UpdateHttpServer() reads it in its loop condition, outside the mutex, on its own thread (FairMQExHistoServer.cxx:85, 99). This is a data race, which is undefined behavior in C++ and which ThreadSanitizer flags. In practice the mutex lock in the loop body makes the change visible, so the thread stops.
issues.fix: Declare fStopThread as std::atomic<bool>.

issues.title: start-mq-ex-params.sh does not source config.sh, so parmq-server sends empty replies
issues.description: parmq-server does not link ExParameters (fairroot/parmq/CMakeLists.txt:44), so it gets FairMQExParamsContFact only when ROOT autoloads libExParameters through its rootmap. ROOT looks for rootmap files only in its dynamic path (LD_LIBRARY_PATH, ROOT_LIBRARY_PATH, ROOT's lib directory), and config.sh is what adds <build>/lib; test-mq-ex-params.sh.in sources it, but the start script does not. From a shell without config.sh, FairRuntimeDb::getContainer() finds no factory, the server sends empty messages, and the client logs 'Received empty reply. Parameter not available' every second.
issues.fix: Add 'source @CMAKE_BINARY_DIR@/config.sh -p' at the top of the script, as test-mq-ex-params.sh.in does.

CLIENT="ex-params-client"

issues.description: The test is added only if(TARGET FairMQ::fairmq-dds-command-ui), but it runs startFairMQPixAlt.sh with --command static, which does not use DDS. Its fixture ex_MQ_pixel_static (pixelDetector/run/CMakeLists.txt:133-142) is added without this condition, so on FairMQ builds without DDS the test is silently missing.
issues.fix: Remove the DDS condition around add_test(ex_MQ_pixel_alt_static).

issues.title: ex_MQ_pixel_alt_static passes --processors 5, which the start script ignores
issues.description: startFairMQPixAlt.sh.in knows only -p|--nof-processors (line 52). Its case statement skips the unknown --processors without a message and then skips the value 5, so the test runs with the default of 2 processors instead of 5.
issues.fix: Pass --nof-processors 5 in the test, and make the script fail on unknown options.

issues.title: startFairMQPixAlt.sh checks APROCESSOR_PID[isimul] instead of [i] before kill
issues.description: In the static-mode cleanup loop, isimul is never set, so ${APROCESSOR_PID[isimul]} is always the first processor. If the first processor has already exited, the script kills none of the others, even if they still run, and they stay alive after the test.
issues.fix: Use ${APROCESSOR_PID[i]} in the kill -0 check.

issues.title: FairMQPixAltFileSinkBin constructs fOutFile from a null file name
issues.description: The initializer fOutFile(nullptr) calls the std::ofstream(const char*) constructor with a null pointer, which is undefined behavior. With glibc the open just fails, and Init() opens the real file later, so today it is harmless.
issues.fix: Remove fOutFile(nullptr) from the initializer list.

excerpt.code:
, fAckChannelName("")
    , fFileName()
    , fOutFile(nullptr)
{}

issues.title: pixalt-sink-bin stores only the first event of each aggregated message
issues.description: StoreData() reads only parts 0 and 1, that is the header and hits of the first event. With --aggregate N > 1 the processor sends 2N parts per message, so the sink writes one event per message and loses the rest. It still sends one ack per message, so the sampler does not notice.
issues.fix: Loop over the parts in (header, hits) pairs, as FairMQPixAltTaskProcessorBin::ProcessData() does.

issues.title: pixalt-sink-bin writes the first hit of each event nofHits times
issues.description: The loop in StoreData() reads payloadH->posX and the other fields, but never advances payloadH or indexes it with ihit. So every hit record in the output file is a copy of the first hit of its event. This happens whenever the sink runs, that is with startFairMQPixAlt.sh --output-type dat, which the README documents.
issues.fix: Use payloadH[ihit] inside the loop.
issues.evidence: The loop at FairMQPixAltFileSinkBin.cxx:63-83 never uses ihit and never moves payloadH, so lines 64-70 always read hit 0. The processor fills one valid hit for each digi (PixelAltFindHits.cxx:233-247), so every other hit of the event is lost and replaced by a copy of hit 0. The sink runs with startFairMQPixAlt.sh --output-type dat (startFairMQPixAlt.sh.in:100-101 and 152-154), which README.md:22 documents.

issues.title: pixalt-sampler-bin calls std::terminate at exit or rerun without an ack channel
issues.description: PreRun() always starts fAckListener (line 61), but PostRun() joins it only when an ack channel is set (lines 236-238). startFairMQPixAlt.sh adds the ack channel only in static mode, so in the default interactive mode the finished thread stays joinable. The device then calls std::terminate() when it is destroyed at exit, or when a second run assigns a new thread to fAckListener.
issues.fix: Start the listener only when fAckChannelName is set, or join it in PostRun() whenever fAckListener.joinable().

issues.title: ReadBinFile() drops the aggregated events when a non-last input file ends
issues.description: At EOF of a file that is not the last one, ReadBinFile() returns true (line 140) without sending its local parts. The events that it already collected for the current message are lost. This happens with --aggregate > 1 and more than one --file-name: up to aggregate-1 events are lost at each file change.
issues.fix: At EOF of a non-last file, open the next file and continue the loop (or send the collected parts before returning).

issues.title: ReadBinFile() uses a variable-length array sized by a value from the input file
issues.description: 'short int dataCont[constNofData]' is a variable-length array, a non-standard compiler extension in C++. Its size head[3]*4 comes from the file without a check, so a corrupt file can give a negative size or overflow the stack. PixelDigiBinSource.cxx:96 in pixelDetector has the same code.
issues.fix: Use a std::vector<short> and check that head[3] is in a sane range first.

issues.title: ReadRootFile() never stops at the end of the chain and reads the branch by chain entry
issues.description: ReadRootFile() stops only when fEventCounter == fMaxIndex. With the default --max-index -1, TChain::GetEntry() past the last entry reads nothing and leaves the buffers as they are, so the sampler sends the last event again and again. It also calls fDigiBranch->GetEntry(fEventCounter) with the chain entry number, which is the wrong local entry in every file after the first.
issues.fix: Stop when fInputChain->GetEntry() returns 0 (or fEventCounter >= GetEntries()), and drop the extra fDigiBranch->GetEntry() call.

issues.title: Processor reads the keep-data option into fDataToKeep but never uses it
issues.description: Init() stores --keep-data in fDataToKeep, and SetDataToKeep() sets it, but no code reads it. The option has no default (runPixAltTaskProcessorBin.cxx:24) and the start script never passes it, so FairMQ's GetValue() logs 'Config has no key: keep-data' at every start.
issues.fix: Remove the option, fDataToKeep and SetDataToKeep(), or implement the filter.

issues.title: FairMQPixAltTaskProcessorBin leaks parameter containers and drops them on a failed reply
issues.description: UpdateParameters() removes each container from fParCList and adds the object that UpdateParameter() returns. UpdateParameter() sets thisPar = nullptr before Deserialize(), so nothing deletes the old container, and each run ID change leaks one object per container. When a reply is empty or fails, UpdateParameter() returns nullptr, TList::AddAt() ignores it, and the loop skips the next container; without PixelDigiParameters, PixelAltFindHits::InitMQ() throws and the device goes to ERROR. The known pixelDetector issue (FairMQPixelTaskProcessor.h:188) has the same code, but it does not list this pixelAlternative copy.
issues.fix: Replace a container only after a valid reply and delete the old one then (and reset fGeoPar, which the destructor deletes), and stop with a clear error when the reply is empty.

issues.title: Writer creates branch 'DigiVector.', but pixalt-sampler-bin reads 'DigiVector'
issues.description: PixelAltDigiWriteToRootVector::Init() creates the branch 'DigiVector.', but FairMQPixAltSamplerBin::PreRun() (line 77) sets the address of 'DigiVector'. TTree::GetBranch() matches names exactly, so TChain sets fDigiBranch to nullptr and ReadRootFile() dereferences it on the first event. The writer's only use is commented out (examples/MQ/pixelDetector/macros/run_digiToBin.C:68-71), so the ROOT input path of pixalt-sampler-bin has no producer and no test.
issues.fix: Use one branch name in both classes, check fDigiBranch and fDigiArray in PreRun(), and use the writer in a macro or test.

issues.title: macros/CMakeLists.txt does not install run_hits.C
issues.description: The install() list leaves out run_hits.C (and run_hits_sep.C, run_hits_sep.sh and eventDisplay.C). So the installed macros have no hit-finding step between run_digi.C and run_tracks.C, which reads the .hits.root file; only run_reco.C runs the whole chain.
issues.fix: Add run_hits.C, and any other macro that should ship, to the install() list.

issues.title: eventDisplay.C does not compile, sets no source and draws a branch that does not exist
issues.description: Lines 17 and 18 both declare FairRunAna *fRun, so ROOT stops with a redefinition error. The FairFileSource created on line 19 is never passed to SetSource(). Line 31 draws FairTutorialtDetPoint, but the Pixel detector registers PixelPoint.
issues.fix: Remove the second declaration, call fRun->SetSource(fFileSource), and draw PixelPoint.

issues.title: In the build tree, four pixel scripts and the DDS topology look for inputs in run/
issues.description: For the build tree, pixel_file_dir is the binary dir of run/, so the scripts look for run/macros and run/param, which the build does not create. The ex_MQ_pixel_static test works around this with --work-dir ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/../ (line 135). startFairMQPixel_3Levels.sh, startFairMQPixelBin.sh, startFairMQPixelBinProxy.sh, startFairMQPixelMerger.sh and pixel-dds-topology.xml have no such option, so they cannot find their inputs in the build tree.
issues.fix: Set pixel_file_dir to ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/.. for the build-tree configuration.

issues.title: startFairMQPixelSimulation.sh kill loop never kills a running simulation device
issues.description: The cleanup loop tests ${SAMPLER_PID[isimul]} instead of ${SAMPLER_PID[i]}. After the loop at line 304, isimul is NOFSIMULS+2, so the test reads an unset element and kill -0 fails. The loop therefore never kills a device that still runs.
issues.fix: Use ${SAMPLER_PID[i]} in the check.

issues.title: PixelFindHitsTask is compiled into ExPixel, but nothing uses it
issues.description: The library source list compiles devices/PixelFindHitsTask.cxx into ExPixel. No other file in the repository uses PixelFindHitsTask.
issues.fix: Remove PixelFindHitsTask.cxx and PixelFindHitsTask.h, or use the class.

issues.title: FairMQPixelFileSink writes no folder and no BranchList, so FairFileSource cannot read it
issues.description: StoreData() writes only the cbmsim tree, without the cbmout folder and without a BranchList. FairFileSource::Init() logs "No Branch list in input file" (FairFileSource.cxx:189-191) and finds no branch objects in its empty folder. So the startFairMQPixel.sh modes -f PixelFindTracks and -f PixelFitTracks, which read the previous MQ output, send no data. FairMQPixelFileSinkBin writes both (lines 69-95).
issues.fix: Write the folder and the BranchList with the first event, as FairMQPixelFileSinkBin does.

issues.title: FairMQPixelMerger C-casts the EventHeader. object to PixelEventHeader* without a check
issues.description: MergeData() casts the object named EventHeader. with (PixelEventHeader*) and then calls GetPartNo() on it. If an upstream device sends a plain FairEventHeader, the merger reads past the end of that object.
issues.fix: Use dynamic_cast and reject the message when the cast fails.

issues.title: FairMQPixelMerger compares array names as pointers, so it never merges event parts
issues.description: MergeData() tests tempArrays[iarray]->GetName() == it->second->GetName(), which compares two const char* pointers into different TString buffers. The test is always false, so AbsorbObjects() never runs. Each sent event holds only the arrays of the part that arrived last, and the data of the other parts is lost. This breaks startFairMQPixelMerger.sh, which the README describes as merging the stations.
issues.fix: Compare the names with strcmp() (or as TString objects).
issues.evidence: FairMQPixelMerger.cxx:127 compares two const char* pointers with ==. The arrays are TClonesArrays named "PixelHits" (PixelFindHits.cxx:171; ROOT's TClonesArray::SetClass names an array after its class plus "s", and the Streamer reads the name back), so TCollection::GetName() returns each object's own fName.Data() and the two pointers never match. AbsorbObjects (line 129) therefore never runs, and lines 149-154 send only the PixelHits of the part that completed the event. This path is the documented startFairMQPixelMerger.sh (3 PixelDigiBinSource samplers, 3 PixelFindHits processors, merger with fNofParts=3).

issues.title: FairMQPixelMerger never deletes buffered or sent objects
issues.description: MergeData() erases the buffered headers and arrays from fObjectMap (lines 135-141) without deleting them. It does not delete the header and arrays of the complete event after Send() (line 154), and it never erases fNofPartsPerEventMap entries. So every event leaks all of its objects.
issues.fix: Delete the objects when they leave fObjectMap and after Send() (or hold them in std::unique_ptr), and erase the finished event from fNofPartsPerEventMap.

issues.title: Devices use the deprecated FairMQDevice alias in constructor init lists
issues.description: The constructors initialize the base class as FairMQDevice() instead of fair::mq::Device(). FairMQ marks this alias [[deprecated]] (fairmq/Device.h:699), so the build prints deprecation warnings. The same name is in FairMQPixelSamplerBin.cxx:31, FairMQPixelFileSink.cxx:26, FairMQPixelFileSinkBin.cxx:32, FairMQChunkMerger.cxx:30, FairMQPixAltSamplerBin.cxx:24 and FairMQPixAltTaskProcessorBin.h:29.
issues.fix: Replace FairMQDevice() with fair::mq::Device() in these init lists.

issues.title: FairMQPixelSampler with FairFileSource sends unfilled data arrays (no SetSource())
issues.description: InitTask() creates a FairRunAna and a FairFileSource but never calls SetSource(), so FairRootManager has no source. GetObject() then returns the array from the input file's folder and skips FairSource::ActivateObject() (FairRootManager.cxx:747-748), so ReadEvent() never fills it. The file stores the folder as it was at init time, before any event, so the sampler sends empty data arrays (for example PixelDigis) for every event. The ex_MQ_pixel_static test compares only event counts, so it does not catch this.
issues.fix: Call fSource->ActivateObject() for each branch as FairMQPixelSamplerBin does (line 63), or set the source on the run before GetObject(), and make the test compare hit counts.
issues.evidence: FairMQPixelSampler.cxx:53-68 never calls fRunAna->SetSource(), and only FairRun::SetSource (FairRun.cxx:256-259) sets FairRootManager::fSource. So ActivateBranch finds PixelDigis in the file folder (FairRootManager.cxx:737) and skips ActivateObject (747-748), while FairFileSource::Init sets branch addresses only for the event headers (FairFileSource.cxx:255-263). The folder copy was written once in FairRunAna::Init before any event (FairRunAna.cxx:250, FairRootFileSink.cxx:238-242), so every event goes out with an empty PixelDigis array and a correct EventHeader. FairFileSource is the default --sampler-type (runPixelSampler.cxx:30), and startFairMQPixel.sh.in:287-295 only compares event counts.

issues.title: Public setters of the pixel sampler and sink devices are overwritten by InitTask()
issues.description: InitTask() reads the file names, branch names, maximum index and channel names from fConfig and overwrites what the public setters stored, so only SetSource() has an effect. The same holds for FairMQPixelSamplerBin.h:35-43, FairMQPixelFileSink.h:33-37, FairMQPixelFileSinkBin.h:34-43 and the task processors (for example SetDataToKeep()). The README still documents these setters.
issues.fix: Remove the setters, or read a value from fConfig only when no setter has set it.

issues.title: FairMQPixelSamplerBin never joins its ack thread without --ack-channel, so it aborts
issues.description: PreRun() always starts fAckListener, but PostRun() joins it only when an ack channel is set, and the destructor is empty. Without --ack-channel (the default, used by startFairMQPixelBin.sh and startFairMQPixelBinProxy.sh), the joinable std::thread is destroyed with the device or reassigned by the next PreRun(), and std::terminate() aborts the process. FairMQPixelSampler.cxx:93-95 starts the thread only when an ack channel is set. Correction: The crash is an abort at process exit (or at a second PreRun), after the run has finished. No data is lost or wrong, so medium fits better than high.
issues.fix: Start the thread only when fAckChannelName is not empty, as FairMQPixelSampler does, or join it in PostRun() whenever it is joinable.
issues.evidence: PreRun (FairMQPixelSamplerBin.cxx:76-81) always starts the thread, PostRun (141-148) joins it only when there is an ack channel, and the destructor (165) is empty. --ack-channel defaults to "" (runPixelSamplerBin.cxx:27), and both bin scripts leave it out. FairMQ destroys the device when the DeviceRunner leaves main (FairMQ runDevice.h:25-48), and destroying a joinable std::thread calls std::terminate (a copy of this pattern aborted with status 134). The abort comes at shutdown, after ResetWrapper has already closed the transports (FairMQ Device.cxx:732-746), so all events are sent and no data is lost. That is why I lower it to medium.

issues.title: FairMQPixelTaskProcessor crashes when --keep-data names a missing object
issues.description: ProcessData() calls (fInput->FindObject(fDataToKeep.c_str()))->Clone() and checks for null only after that call. When --keep-data names an object that is not in the input, FindObject() returns nullptr, and the device crashes with a segmentation fault.
issues.fix: Check the FindObject() result for nullptr before calling Clone(), and log a warning when the object is missing.

issues.title: UpdateParameters() leaks old containers and drops containers after a failed reply
issues.description: UpdateParameters() removes each container from fParCList and never deletes it, so containers leak at each run ID change. When the reply is missing or cannot be deserialized, UpdateParameter() returns nullptr, TList::AddAt() refuses it, the list shrinks, and the loop skips the next container, which keeps its old values. A missing container then makes InitMQ() throw (for example "no PixelDigiParameters" in PixelFindHits), and the device goes to ERROR. FairMQPixelTaskProcessorBin.h:208-240 has the same code.
issues.fix: Replace a container only after a valid reply, deleting the old one then, and keep it or stop with a clear error when the reply is empty.

issues.title: FairMQPixelTaskProcessorBin reads parts.At(1) without checking the part count
issues.description: ProcessData() reads parts.At(1) without checking that parts.Size() >= 2. Parts::At() uses vector::at(), so a one-part message (for example from a sampler started with only one --branch-name) throws, and the device goes to ERROR. The empty-message check returns 0 (false), which would end RUNNING, but FairMQ never sends an empty multipart message (FairMQPixAltTaskProcessorBin.h:63-64 has the same check). fDataToKeep is read from --keep-data (line 171) but never used.
issues.fix: Check parts.Size() >= 2, return true to skip a short message, and remove or implement fDataToKeep.

issues.title: FairMQRunDevice prints with printf() without a newline and defines a global mutex
issues.description: SendObject() calls printf("sending %s", ...) without a newline and outside the logger, so the text runs into the next log line. Line 28 defines std::mutex mtx at global scope in the library, where any other global named mtx clashes with it.
issues.fix: Use LOG(info) for the message, and make the mutex a class member or give it internal linkage.

issues.fix: Serialize the original object, or hold the clone in a std::unique_ptr.

issues.title: ResetTask() leaves fRunInitialized set, so a second init/run cycle uses freed objects
issues.description: ResetTask() only resets fRunSim and keeps fRunInitialized true. ~FairRunSim deletes the modules that fDetectorArray still holds, and InitTask() has already moved fSink into the first run. After RESET TASK and a new INIT TASK, InitTask() adds the freed modules again with no sink, and PreRun() skips InitializeRun(), so the device runs a FairRunSim that was never initialized. FairMQTransportDevice::ResetTask() (FairMQTransportDevice.cxx:138-141) has the same problem and also leaves fVMC, fStack and fMCApplication pointing to deleted objects.
issues.fix: Reset fRunInitialized and rebuild the modules and the sink for a new cycle, or refuse a second INIT TASK.

issues.title: Typo "expexted" in a FairOnlineSink warning
issues.description: EmitPersistentBranchWrongTypeWarning() prints "(expexted: ...)". Users see this warning when they read a persistent branch with the wrong type.
issues.fix: Change "expexted" to "expected".

issues.title: PixelDigiSource::ReadEvent() loop condition is inverted, so each event is one line
issues.description: The do-while loop in ReadEvent() repeats only while the line just read is "EVENT END", and the continue after an EVENT line jumps to this test. So each call reads one line: an "EVENT BEGIN" line gives an event with no digis, and each digi line becomes its own event. A test program of the loop with events of 3 and 1 digis gives 0,1,1,1,0,1 digis per call; with != it gives 3 and 1. Correction: Not every call reads exactly one line. A call that reads EVENT END loops once more and also reads the next EVENT BEGIN line, and that is why it returns 0 digis. The per-call counts 0,1,1,1,0,1 in the description are right.
issues.fix: Change the condition to buffer != "EVENT END".
issues.evidence: In PixelDigiSource.cxx:89-117 the do-while repeats only while buffer == "EVENT END", and the continue at line 103 jumps straight to that test. I fed a copy of the loop (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8ce3faed-3785-59d4-9dc9-2418f32b8a1f/scratchpad/issues/work-high-09/loop.cxx) the format that PixelDigiWriteToFile.cxx:49-74 writes. For events of 3 and 1 digis it gives 0,1,1,1,0,1 digis per call, and the first four of those all carry MC entry 0; with != it gives 3 and 1. This source is documented in the README and used by macros/run_dAsciiSource.C and by pixel-sampler --sampler-type PixelDigiSource (runPixelSampler.cxx:44-48).

issues.title: PixelDigiSource::FillEventHeader() casts a plain FairEventHeader and writes past its end
issues.description: FillEventHeader() calls static_cast<PixelEventHeader*>(feh)->SetPartNo() on every header it gets. FairRootManager::SpecifyRunId() and FairRootManager::ReadEvent() pass the manager's own plain FairEventHeader (FairRootManager.cxx:89, 405, 425), so SetPartNo() writes past the end of that heap object. This heap overwrite happens at init and for every event in run_dAsciiSource.C and run_dBinSource.C. PixelDigiBinSource.cxx:151 has the same code.
issues.fix: Use dynamic_cast<PixelEventHeader*>(feh) and call SetPartNo() only when the cast succeeds.
issues.evidence: FairRootManager always owns a plain FairEventHeader (FairRootManager.cxx:89) and passes it to the source in SpecifyRunId (405) and ReadEvent (425). FairRunAna calls these at Init (FairRunAna.cxx:189) and once per event (FairRunAna.cxx:313), and FairRun::SetEventHeader (FairRun.cxx:157-160) does not replace this header. With the ROOT 6 64-bit layout, FairEventHeader is 88 bytes and PixelEventHeader::fPartNo is at offset 88, so PixelDigiSource.cxx:149 and PixelDigiBinSource.cxx:151 write 4 bytes past the end. I copied the layout into a test program: ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow, and with plain glibc the write overwrites the next chunk's size field, so a later free() aborts. Only the FairRunAna macros are affected; the MQ sampler calls the source's ReadEvent directly (FairMQPixelSampler.cxx:105).

issues.title: PixelDigiSource hides FairSource::fRunId, so headers and parameters use run ID 0
issues.description: PixelDigiSource.h:74 and PixelDigiBinSource.h:74 declare their own Int_t fRunId, which hides the protected FairSource::fRunId. ReadEvent() sets only the hidden member, so FairSource::FillEventHeader() always writes run ID 0. FairRunAna::Init() then calls initContainers(0), FairParRootFile::readVersions() finds no run 0, and no container from the ROOT parameter file (such as the geometry) is read. The output event headers also carry run ID 0. Correction: The fix must also remove fRunId(0) from the constructor initializer lists (PixelDigiSource.cxx:35, PixelDigiBinSource.cxx:34), because a derived class cannot initialize a base member there.
issues.fix: Remove the fRunId members from both sources so that ReadEvent() sets FairSource::fRunId.
issues.evidence: PixelDigiSource.h:74 and PixelDigiBinSource.h:74 hide the protected FairSource::fRunId (FairSource.h:56), so ReadEvent (PixelDigiSource.cxx:93, PixelDigiBinSource.cxx:99) never sets the base member, and nothing in FairRunAna calls source->SetRunId. FairSource::FillEventHeader therefore always writes 0 (FairSource.cxx:21,34). FairRunAna::Init then uses run 0 (FairRunAna.cxx:191,198,220), but the parameter file only has the simulation's time-stamp run ID (FairRunSim.cxx:179-183). So readVersions finds no run "0" (FairParRootFileIo.cxx:71-74), findInputVersion returns -1 (FairDetParRootFileIo.cxx:120-124), and the geometry that PixelFindHits needs (gGeoManager at PixelFindHits.cxx:91) is never loaded. The stored header also gets run ID 0. The MQ sampler path is not affected, because it sends the source's own fEventHeader, which gets the right run ID.

issues.title: Typo "succesfull" in four Init() log messages
issues.description: The Init() info message says "Initialization succesfull". PixelDigitize.cxx:236, PixelFindHits.cxx:207, PixelDigiWriteToFile.cxx:91 and PixelDigiWriteToBinFile.cxx:106 have the same typo.
issues.fix: Change "succesfull" to "successful" in all four files.

issues.title: PixelFindHits::InitMQ() allocates a new output array on every parameter update
issues.description: InitMQ() runs fHits = new TClonesArray("PixelHit", 10000) on every call. The task processors call InitMQ() after each parameter update (each new run ID), so the old arrays leak. PixelFindTracks.cxx:164-165 (fTracks and the TH2F fhDist2D) and PixelFitTracks.cxx:182 do the same.
issues.fix: Allocate the objects only when they are null, or delete the old ones first.

issues.title: FairMQChunkMerger::fNofParts and SetNofParts() are never used
issues.description: The constructor sets fNofParts(3), and FairMQChunkMerger.h:36 offers SetNofParts(). No code reads fNofParts, because the merger takes the chunk count from the event header.
issues.fix: Remove fNofParts and SetNofParts().
