issues.title: FairMQChunkMerger never deletes deserialized objects or finished event entries
issues.description: MergeData() deserializes a new header and new arrays for every message and never deletes them. fMCSplitEventHeader is overwritten for every message, the merged arrays are not deleted after Send() (line 183), and fNofPartsPerEventMap entries are never erased. Memory grows with every chunk.
issues.fix: Hold the deserialized objects in std::unique_ptr, free the merged objects after Send(), and erase the fNofPartsPerEventMap entry of each sent event.

issues.title: FairMQChunkMerger reads trackShift out of range when no MCTrack array is sent
issues.description: trackShift gets one entry for each buffered MCTrack array. When the channel carries no array named MCTrack, trackShift stays empty, and trackShift[addedArray++] reads past its end (undefined behavior). The merger needs an MCTrack branch but never checks for it.
issues.fix: Check that addedArray < trackShift.size(), and log an error when the MCTrack array is missing.

issues.title: FairMQChunkMerger loops with auto& it, so fObjectMap.erase() removes nothing
issues.description: The loops at lines 77, 122 and 148 declare auto& it = fRet.first, a reference, so ++it moves fRet.first itself. At line 166 fRet.first equals fRet.second, and fObjectMap.erase() removes nothing. The buffered entries, with arrays already emptied by AbsorbObjects(), stay in fObjectMap for the whole run. A test program of this pattern keeps all 3 entries after the erase.
issues.fix: Iterate with a copy (auto it = fRet.first), or erase by key with fObjectMap.erase(fEvRIPair).

issues.title: In rr mode the generator sends no reply after the last event, so transporters hang
issues.description: With --running-mode rr, Reply() calls GenerateAndSendData(), which returns false after the last event without sending a reply. The transport device sent its request in ConditionalRun() and blocks in Receive() until a controller stops it. So an rr run never ends by itself, and the test covers only pp mode.
issues.fix: Send an end-of-data reply before returning false, and let the transport device stop when it receives it.

issues.title: FairMQPrimaryGeneratorDevice leaks one FairMCSplitEventHeader per message
issues.description: GenerateAndSendData() creates a new FairMCSplitEventHeader for every message, serializes it, and never deletes it. So each sent chunk leaks one header.
issues.fix: Create the header on the stack or hold it in a std::unique_ptr.

issues.title: Chunk count and last-chunk end are wrong when nPrim is not a multiple of --chunk-size
issues.description: GenerateAndSendData() sets NofChunks to nPrim / chunkSize, rounded down, but sends one more chunk when there is a remainder. For that last chunk it sets NPrim to the remaining count instead of the end index, so FairStack::SetParticleArray() gets from > to and transports none of those primaries, and FairMQChunkMerger keeps one chunk per event in its buffer. When nPrim < chunkSize (for example --chunk-size 200 with the 100-particle box generator), NofChunks is 0 and the merger never sends any event. The test uses chunk size 10, which divides 100, so it does not catch this.
issues.fix: Set NofChunks to the rounded-up quotient and NPrim to min(fChunkPointer + fChunkSize, nPrim).
issues.evidence: Line 97 rounds nPrim/chunkSize down, but lines 117-122 send one more chunk when there is a remainder. Lines 100-101 set NPrim to the remaining count, and FairStack::SetParticleArray loops from the chunk start up to NPrim (FairStack.h:192-194, called at FairMQTransportDevice.cxx:245), so the last chunk transports nothing. I copied this logic into a test program with 100 primaries: chunk size 30 gives NofChunks=3 with 4 chunks sent and only 90 of 100 primaries transported, and chunk size 200 gives NofChunks=0. The merger waits until its received count equals NofChunks (FairMQChunkMerger.cxx:74,97), so with 0 it never sends, and in other cases the extra part stays in the buffer for good. --chunk-size is a documented option (README.md, runMQGen.cxx:32), and the tests only use 10 (test-splitMQ.sh.in:10, splitMC-topology.xml:10).

issues.title: A failed dlopen() or dlsym() lets FairMQTransportDevice run on without the detector
issues.description: When a --detector-library cannot be loaded, InitTask() logs LOG(fatal) and returns. fair::Logger runs a fatal callback only if one is set, and only the FairLogger singleton sets it (fairroot/tools/FairLogger.cxx:37); neither the devices nor FairMQ create it. So the device keeps running without that detector, skips the remaining libraries, and writes events without its points. The library names in the README example trigger this.
issues.fix: Throw an exception instead of LOG(fatal) and return, so that the device goes to the ERROR state.

issues.title: FairMQTransportDevice tags parameters with its own run ID, not the server's run ID
issues.description: fRunSim->SetRunId(fRunId) is commented out, and InitTask() sets the run ID to 0 (line 72), so FairRunSim::Init() generates its own run ID from the current second. UpdateParameterServer() (line 264) tags the containers with that ID, while TransportData() (line 246) gives the events the server's run ID. The parameter file matches the events only when the server and the device generate their IDs in the same second, so a second boundary between the two calls breaks the match.
issues.fix: Restore fRunSim->SetRunId(fRunId) before fRunSim->Init().

issues.title: Transport device log names InitTask() inside InitializeRun() and prints the local run ID
issues.description: InitializeRun() logs "end of FairMQTransportDevice::InitTask()". The run ID in the message is the one FairRunSim generated, not the server's, because FairMCApplication::InitGeometry() sets the header run ID from the run (FairMCApplication.cxx:880).
issues.fix: Name InitializeRun() in the message and print fRunId.

issues.title: TransportData() leaks the header and all primaries of the event for every chunk
issues.description: TransportData() deserializes a new FairMCSplitEventHeader and the full TParticles array for every chunk and never deletes them. The generator sends all primaries of the event with each chunk, so each chunk leaks all of them. TransportData() also uses meh without a null check (line 245) when a message has the particle part but no header.
issues.fix: Hold both objects in std::unique_ptr so they are freed after ProcessRun(), and skip a message that has no header.

issues.title: dataGenerator tests vm.count("help") but never declares --help, so --help fails
issues.description: main() checks vm.count("help") at line 83, but the options description has no 'help' option. With --help, parse_command_line() throws 'unrecognised option'. The program then prints the error and the options and returns 1, and the help branch never runs.
issues.fix: Declare a 'help,h' option in desc.

issues.title: startDataGenerator.sh drops its arguments, so the options in README.md do nothing
issues.description: The script runs ex-serialization-data-generator with fixed options and does not forward its own arguments. README.md (lines 10, 16 and 22) tells users to run ./startDataGenerator.sh with --help, --tmax 1000 or --Nmean 1000 --Nsigma 10. The script silently ignores these options and always writes the default 100 bunches.
issues.fix: Append "$@" to the command in startDataGenerator.sh.in.

issues.title: Serialization processor declares --num-msgs but never reads it
issues.description: addCustomOptions() in processor.cxx declares --num-msgs ('Stop after <n> msgs'), so --help lists it. Processor::Run() never reads the value, so the option has no effect. Only the sink implements it.
issues.fix: Remove the option from the processor, or stop after n messages as the sink does.

issues.title: Serialization sampler crashes in Run() when Init() cannot open the file or tree
issues.description: Sampler::Init() only logs an error when TFile::Open() fails or the tree 'cbmsim' is missing, and the device goes on to Run(). Run() then calls fTree->GetEntries() on a null fTree and crashes. Both error messages are also wrong. Line 47 says tree 'MyDigi', which is the branch name. Line 50 names SimpleTreeReader::InitSource().
issues.fix: Throw from Init() when the file, the tree or the branch is missing, and fix the two messages.

issues.title: Sampler runs a leftover FindHits() check on every event and throws the result away
issues.description: Run() calls FindHits(*fInput) for every event and stores the result in a volatile local that nothing reads. The comment calls it a temporary check, but it checks nothing. It only builds a TClonesArray of hits per event and wastes CPU in the sampler.
issues.fix: Remove the call, FindHits() and the 'temporary' includes from sampler.cxx.

issues.title: Trajectory-cut comments are wrong: SetStepSizeCut(0.01) is 0.1 mm, not 1 cm
issues.description: The comment '// 1 cm' follows SetStepSizeCut(0.01). The cut is compared with TrackStep(), which is in cm, so 0.01 means 0.1 mm. The comment '0 < Etot < 1.04 GeV' follows SetEnergyCut(0., 1.02). The same copied comments are in run_rad.C:115 and 118, Tutorial4/macros/run_tutorial4.C:138 and 141, and in examples/advanced.
issues.fix: Change the comments to '0.1 mm' and '0 < Etot < 1.02 GeV'.

issues.title: ex_sim_tutorial1_TGeant4 runs in MT mode, so no test checks sequential Geant4 output
issues.description: run_tutorial1() defaults to isMT = true (run_tutorial1.C:24), and the per-engine tests pass only the event count and the engine. So ex_sim_tutorial1_TGeant4 runs Geant4 in MT mode, like ex_sim_tutorial1_Geant4MT. Only ex_sim_tutorial1_PostInitConfig (1 event) runs this macro with sequential Geant4, and that test only looks for 'Loading Geant4 PostInit Config.'.
issues.fix: Pass isMT = false in the ex_sim_tutorial1_${mcEngine} tests.

issues.title: Tutorial1 eventDisplay.C opens file names that run_tutorial1.C never writes
issues.description: eventDisplay.C reads 'tutorial1_TGeant3_pions.mc_p2.000_t0_n10.root' and the matching params file. run_tutorial1.C builds the names with std::to_string() ('..._p2.000000_t0.000000_n10.root'). It also adds 'MT' to the prefix when isMT is true, which is the default. So FairFileSource cannot open the input, and the macro stops with a fatal error.
issues.fix: Build the names in eventDisplay.C the same way as run_tutorial1.C, or take them as macro arguments.

issues.title: tut1: stack modules and generator die before FairRunSim, which then deletes primGen
issues.description: run_tutorial1_main() declares `FairRunSim run` before the stack objects cave, tutdet, primGen, boxGen and parOut, so these are destroyed first. ~FairRunSim() then runs `delete fGen` (FairRunSim.cxx:109) on the destroyed stack object primGen. ~FairRuntimeDb() would then call close() on the destroyed parOut. This is undefined behavior (delete of a stack address) every time the installed executable tut1 exits. src/runTutorial1.cxx includes this file, and no test runs tut1.
issues.fix: Allocate these objects with new, as run_tutorial1.C does; FairRunSim and FairPrimaryGenerator delete the modules and generators themselves.

issues.title: run_tutorial1.C builds a std::string from getenv() without a null check
issues.description: string dir = getenv("VMCWORKDIR") builds a std::string from a null pointer when VMCWORKDIR is not set, which is undefined behavior. libstdc++ throws std::logic_error "basic_string: construction from null is not valid" (checked with GCC 13), and libc++ crashes in strlen(); neither result names the missing variable. The other Tutorial1 macros use TString, which turns a null pointer into an empty string.
issues.fix: Check the getenv() result and stop with a clear message when VMCWORKDIR is not set.

issues.title: Particle name "eplus" is paired with PDG code 11, which is the electron
issues.description: partName[1] is "eplus", but partPdgC[1] is 11, the PDG code of the electron; the positron is -11. A user who sets chosenPart = 1 gets electrons in output files named ..._eplus.... The same arrays are in run_tutorial1_mesh.C, _pythia6.C, _pythia8.C, _fastsim.C and _binary.C, in the three Tutorial2 macros, in pixelDetector macros/run_sim.C and run/runMQSim.cxx, and in pixelSimSplit run/runMQGen.cxx.
issues.fix: Use -11 for "eplus" (or rename the entry to "electron") in all copies.

issues.title: run_tutorial1.C names the geometry file with a double underscore
issues.description: outPrefix already ends with '_' (line 53), and line 63 appends "_geofile_full.root". So the geometry file gets a name like tutorial1_TGeant4MT__geofile_full.root.
issues.fix: Append "geofile_full.root" without the leading underscore.

issues.title: Tutorial1 macro calls FairBoxGenerator::SetDebug(), which does nothing
issues.description: SetDebug() is an empty stub kept for backward compatibility (FairBoxGenerator.h:117-121). The tutorial still calls boxGen->SetDebug(kTRUE), which suggests that it turns on debug output.
issues.fix: Remove the call from the tutorial, or replace it with a FairLogger verbosity setting.

issues.title: Tutorial1 macros point gRandom at a local TRandom3, so gRandom is null after the macro
issues.description: run_tutorial1() sets gRandom = &random, where random is a local TRandom3. When the macro returns, ~TRandom() sets gRandom to nullptr (ROOT TRandom.cxx), so a later use of gRandom in the same interactive ROOT session dereferences a null pointer, for example run_tutorial2.C:67 (gRandom->SetSeed()) or FairRunSim::Init() (FairRunSim.cxx:246). Batch runs with root -q and the tests are not affected. run_tutorial1_fastsim.C:112 and run_tutorial1_binary.C:117 do the same.
issues.fix: Call gRandom->SetSeed(randomSeed) instead of pointing gRandom at a local object.

issues.title: run_tutorial1.C prints the pass string before its checks, so failed checks pass the tests
issues.description: run_tutorial1() prints 'Macro finished successfully.' at line 166. Only after that does it check events, tracks, points, branches and leaves; lines 187-206 return 1 on failure. The tests ex_sim_tutorial1_<engine> (macros/CMakeLists.txt:50-55) pass on that string, and PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION ignores the exit code (checked with ctest 3.28). So a failed output check never fails these tests; only ex_sim_tutorial1_Geant4MT, which expects 'Simulation successful.', covers the checks.
issues.fix: Use 'Simulation successful.' as PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION for every run_tutorial1.C test, or print the success line after the checks.

issues.title: run_tutorial1.C MT check reads only _t1 and _t2, so it fails with more Geant4 threads
issues.description: In MT mode the output check chains only the worker files _t1.root and _t2.root. Each worker writes its own file (FairRootManager::UpdateFileName() appends _t<instance id>), and the number of workers is the G4MTRunManager default of 2, which G4FORCENUMBEROFTHREADS can change; FairRoot does not set it. With 3 or more workers the chain misses events, nofE < nEvents, and the macro returns 1 although the simulation worked, so ex_sim_tutorial1_Geant4MT fails; with 1 worker ROOT only reports the missing _t2 file.
issues.fix: Add the worker files with a wildcard (the output name with _t*.root) instead of two fixed names.

issues.title: FairSimConfig logs the debug leftover "YUPYUPYUP" for --multi-threaded
issues.description: ParseCommandLine() logs LOG(info) << "YUPYUPYUP" when --multi-threaded is given. This is a debug leftover that tells the user nothing.
issues.fix: Remove the line, or log a real message such as "Geant4 multi-threaded mode requested".

issues.title: tut1 exits with status 0 for an unknown --engine or an invalid option
issues.description: FairSimConfig::ParseCommandLine() returns 1 for an engine other than TGeant3 or TGeant4 (FairSimConfig.cxx:60-62), but main() then returns 0. For an option parse error, ParseCommandLine() sets fHelp and returns 0 (FairSimConfig.cxx:45-48), so main() prints the help and also returns 0. Scripts cannot detect a bad command line.
issues.fix: Let ParseCommandLine() report parse errors as failures, and return a non-zero status from main() when it fails.

issues.title: read_digis.C calls saveOutput() without setOutput(), so it saves nothing
issues.description: read_digis.C calls rtdb->saveOutput() at lines 94 and 115 but never sets an output. Without an output, FairRuntimeDb::writeContainer() skips the write but still resets the changed flag, and writeVersions() does nothing. The comment at lines 103-104 says this code shows how to change and save the parameters.
issues.fix: Call rtdb->setOutput(io1) before saveOutput(), as create_digis.C does.

issues.title: Register() comments name the branch FairTutorialDetNPoint; the code uses TutorialDetPoint
issues.description: The comment in FairTutorialDet2::Register() says the branch is called FairTutorialDet2Point, but line 124 registers 'TutorialDetPoint'. FairTutorialDet4.cxx:217-223 and FairTutorialDet1.cxx:98-104 have the same wrong name. FairFastSimExample.cxx and FairFastSimExample2.cxx name FairTutorialDet1Point but register 'FastSimPoint' and 'FastSimPoint2'. The sentence about kFALSE is a correct hint, not an error.
issues.fix: Put the real branch names in the comments.

issues.title: Container factory titles name libTutorial1 (Tutorial2, Tutorial4) and libSts (base)
issues.description: FairTutorialDet2ContFact has the title 'Factory for parameter containers in libTutorial1', but the library is ExSimulation2. FairRuntimeDb::print() shows this title. FairTutorialDet4ContFact.cxx:20 has the same copied text, and fairroot/base/sim/FairBaseContFact.cxx:27 says 'libSts'.
issues.fix: Put the real library names in the titles.

issues.title: DigiPar putParams() resizes its array, and getParams() never detects a wrong count
issues.description: putParams() calls ftutdetdigipar.Set(array_size) (line 64), so writing the container, or printing it with printParams(), changes its data. getParams() computes the expected size (lines 92-94), but FairParamList::fill(TArrayF*) then resizes the array to the number of values in the file. So a file with a wrong count is accepted, and a later print or write silently cuts or zero-pads the array. The shipped file has the right count (7584).
issues.fix: Do not resize in putParams(), and make getParams() return kFALSE when the filled size differs from array_size.

issues.title: Tutorial2 digitizer uses FairRunAna::Instance(), which is null under FairRunSim
issues.description: SetParContainers() and ReInit() (lines 44 and 57) call FairRunAna::Instance()->GetRuntimeDb(). FairRunAna::Instance() is nullptr when the task runs under FairRunSim or FairRunOnline, so the task would crash there. The shipped macros use FairRunAna, but users copy this pattern. FairTutorialDet4HitProducerIdealMisalign.cxx:51 and 61 do the same.
issues.fix: Use FairRun::Instance()->GetRuntimeDb(), as FairTutorialDet4::SetParContainers() does.

issues.title: Dead '!ioman' checks: FairRootManager::Instance() never returns null
issues.description: FairTutorialDet2Digitizer::Init() (lines 70-73) and FairTutorialDet2CustomTask::Init() (lines 35-38) check whether FairRootManager::Instance() returned null. Instance() returns the address of a thread_local static object, so this branch never runs. The same dead check appears in many other tasks, for example FairTestDetectorDigiTask.cxx:33.
issues.fix: Remove the checks and the else nesting.

issues.title: Tutorial2 digitizer never clears the InMemory1 vector, so it grows with every event
issues.description: FairTutorialDet2Digitizer::Exec() appends to fCustomData2, the memory branch 'InMemory1' registered at line 189, but never clears it. FairRootManager does not clear RegisterAny() branches between events either. So the vector keeps the entries of all earlier events, memory grows, and FairTutorialDet2CustomTask reads old data in every event.
issues.fix: Call fCustomData2->clear() at the start of Exec().

issues.title: compare.cxx reads an uninitialized mode flag; with any argument the flag is true
issues.description: isFortranFile is uninitialized when the program gets no argument, so the input format is chosen at random (g++ -O2 -Wall warns -Wmaybe-uninitialized). With an argument, 'isFortranFile = argv[1]' converts a non-null pointer, so the flag is always true. Both branches read shifts.txt, and lines 134-136 repeat the loop of lines 130-132.
issues.fix: Initialize the flag to false, set it from the value of argv[1], and delete the repeated loop.

issues.title: compare.cxx divides by the true shift, so labels without a shift give NaN or infinity
issues.description: The percentage at line 144 is diff / origShifts[i]. For labels without a true shift (label 0, labels 41-100 and the fixed planes), the result is NaN or infinite, so any non-zero fit value on these labels counts as bad. origShifts and recoShifts (lines 93-94) are variable-length arrays, which ISO C++ does not allow (g++ -pedantic warns).
issues.fix: Use the absolute difference when the true shift is zero, and use std::vector for the two arrays.

issues.title: pede steering file mp2str.txt names mp2tst.bin, not the file run_reco.C writes
issues.description: mp2str.txt lists mp2tst.bin, the default file name of FairTutorialDet4MilleWriter. run_reco.C sets the name to data/testmille_<align_><engine>, so the writer creates, for example, data/testmille_align_TGeant3.bin. pede cannot use the steering file without a manual edit.
issues.fix: Put the file name that run_reco.C writes into mp2str.txt, or document the edit.

excerpt.code:
mp2con.txt   ! constraints text file
Cfiles       ! following bin files are Cfiles
mp2tst.bin   ! binary data file
*hugecut 50.0     !cut factor in iteration 0
*chisqcut 1.0 1.0 ! cut factor in iterations 1 and 2

issues.title: endforeach() repeats a fixed engine list that differs from the foreach() header
issues.description: Line 43 closes foreach(mcEngine IN LISTS mcEngine_list) (line 18) with endforeach(mcEngine IN ITEMS TGeant3 TGeant4). CMake compares only the first argument, so it accepts the line without a warning (checked with CMake 3.28). The extra words suggest a fixed engine list that the loop does not use.
issues.fix: Write endforeach() without arguments.

excerpt.code:
PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION "Macro finished successfully"
  )
endforeach(mcEngine IN ITEMS TGeant3 TGeant4)

install(FILES

issues.title: run_reco.C parameter I/O lines do nothing: double open, read-only output, early save
issues.description: run_reco.C opens the ASCII parameter list twice (lines 71 and 73). At line 76 it sets the ROOT parameter input as the output, but open() opened that file read-only by default. At line 77 it calls saveOutput() before Init(), when no run is current. None of these lines has an effect.
issues.fix: Remove the second open() and the setOutput()/saveOutput() calls, or open the file in UPDATE mode and save after Run().

issues.title: Unused variables in run_tutorial4_createMatrices.C and run_tutorial4.C
issues.description: run_tutorial4_createMatrices.C never calls Run(), so its nEvents argument has no effect. Its variables outDir, geoFile and geoFileMisaligned (lines 30, 36-37) are never used. run_tutorial4.C builds geoFile (lines 37-49) only for the commented-out CreateGeometryFile() calls (lines 149, 151).
issues.fix: Remove the unused argument and variables.

issues.title: run_tutorial4_createParameterFile.C writes a parameter file that no class can read
issues.description: The macro writes the block [FairTutorialDetMissallignPar] with DetectorId, R11..R33 and TX..TZ. FairTutorialDet4MisalignPar reads [FairTutorialDet4MissallignPar] with ShiftX/Y/Z and RotationX/Y/Z. Two keys are also misspelled: '23:' and '33:' instead of 'R23:' and 'R33:' (lines 217, 227). The check 'if (!f)' after 'new TFile' (line 42) is never true, and the comment at line 79 is about CBM TRD nodes.
issues.fix: Write the keys that FairTutorialDet4MisalignPar::getParams() reads (or remove the macro), and test f->IsZombie() instead of !f.

issues.title: create_misalign_parameter.C declares 'ofstream myfile' twice and does not compile
issues.description: The macro declares `ofstream myfile;` at line 58 and again at line 174 in the same scope, so ROOT cannot compile it. It is the only writer of shifts.txt, which compare.cxx reads. It also writes the block [FairTutorialDetMissallignPar] (lines 62, 65), but the container is FairTutorialDet4MissallignPar, so its example.par could not be read either.
issues.fix: Reuse the first stream for shifts.txt and write the block name [FairTutorialDet4MissallignPar].

issues.title: TutorialDet.missallign.par is unused and could not be read
issues.description: No macro or class reads this file. Its block name FairTutorialDetMissallignPar does not match the container FairTutorialDet4MissallignPar. It also lacks ShiftZ and RotationX/Y/Z, which FairTutorialDet4MisalignPar::getParams() requires.
issues.fix: Delete the file; the macros use parameters/example.par.

issues.title: RotationX/Y/Z are Euler angles in degrees in the simulation but radians about z in reco
issues.description: FairTutorialDet4 passes RotationX, RotationY and RotationZ to TGeoRotation(name, phi, theta, psi), which takes Euler angles in degrees. So RotationX turns the plane about z, RotationY about x, and RotationZ again about z. FairTutorialDet4HitProducerIdealMisalign (lines 150-151) uses RotationZ as an angle in radians about z. example.par sets all rotations to 0, so the problem shows only when a user sets them; then simulation and reconstruction disagree.
issues.fix: Build the rotation with RotateX(), RotateY() and RotateZ() in one documented unit, and use the same convention in the hit producer.

issues.title: RegisterAlignmentMatrices() leaks one TGeoRotation and one TGeoCombiTrans per plane
issues.description: For each plane, the code calls new TGeoRotation and copies *(new TGeoCombiTrans(dx, dy, dz, rrot)) into a local object. Neither heap object is ever deleted, because the copy owns its own rotation. getMisalignmentMatrices() (lines 287-288) duplicates the whole loop and has the same leak.
issues.fix: Build the matrix on the stack (or directly as a TGeoHMatrix), and let RegisterAlignmentMatrices() call getMisalignmentMatrices().

issues.title: DoMisalignment(kTRUE) leaves Tutorial4 hits in local coordinates with z near 0
issues.description: In Exec(), the misalignment branch builds the hit from the local point coordinates and, unlike the default branch, never calls fGeoHandler->LocalToGlobal(). So every hit has x and y in the plane frame, and its z is the local z, near 0. The straight-line fitter and the Mille writer then see all hits at the same z. run_reco.C uses DoMisalignment(kFALSE), so no test covers this branch.
issues.fix: Apply the shift and rotation in the local frame, then convert the hit with LocalToGlobal() as the default branch does.

issues.title: Hit producer logs every point at info level, and its messages misspell 'misalign'
issues.description: Exec() logs each point position twice, plus a '****' line, with LOG(info) (lines 182-194). This floods the output of run_reco.C, which runs at screen level INFO. Init() logs 'HitProducerIdealMissallign: Initialisation successfull' (line 96), and the task name (line 31) and line 49 also say 'Missallign'.
issues.fix: Use LOG(debug) for the per-point lines and fix the spelling in the messages; the container name can stay.

issues.title: MilleWriter never deletes fMille, so the Mille output file is never closed
issues.description: Init() creates fMille with new (lines 60 and 63), and neither Finish() nor the destructor deletes it. Only ~Mille() closes its std::ofstream (Mille.cc:32-35), and Mille::end() does not flush. Records still in the stream buffer when the program ends can be lost, so the binary file for pede can end early.
issues.fix: Hold fMille in a std::unique_ptr and reset it in Finish().

issues.title: MilleWriter labels come from the hit index, not from the detector ID
issues.description: StraightLineShiftX() and StraightLineShiftXY() set the labels to iHit + 1 and iHit + 101 (lines 159, 227-228). These labels match the planes only when an event has exactly one hit in every plane, in plane order. An event that misses a plane shifts all later labels, and pede then assigns the residuals to the wrong planes.
issues.fix: Compute the labels from hit->GetDetectorID() (+1 and +101), which is the plane copy number.

issues.title: StraightLineFitter writes a stale track for rejected events and reads XPos[-1] at 0 hits
issues.description: Exec() returns when IsGoodEvent() is false but does not clear fTracks, and FairRunAna does not clear registered output arrays. So the persistent branch TutorialDetTrack stores the previous event's track again for every rejected event. The Mille writer is not affected because it checks IsGoodEvent() itself. For an event without hits, IsGoodEvent() returns true, and lines 114-115 read XPos[nHits - 1], that is XPos[-1], from zero-length arrays.
issues.fix: Clear fTracks at the start of Exec() and return early when there are fewer than two hits.

issues.title: NewDetector rename.sh scripts leave .bak files behind on macOS
issues.description: On macOS the script runs sed with '-i .bak' (L42), so BSD sed keeps a .bak copy of each .h, .cxx and CMakeLists.txt file that it edits. The project, NewTask and NewParameterContainer scripts delete their .bak files. This script never does, so the copies stay in the new detector folder. NewDetector_stl_containers/rename.sh and both MyProjGenerators/rename.sh copies have the same problem.
issues.fix: On macOS, delete the backups at the end, for example with find . -name '*.bak' -delete, as the project rename.sh does.

issues.title: NewDetector rename.sh ignores its project and prefix arguments, so MyProj names stay
issues.description: The script replaces FairDetectorList and FairStack with the prefix (L54-57). But the template code uses MyProjDetectorList.h, MyProjStack.h and the class MyProjStack (NewDetector.cxx:18-19, 126), so the third argument changes nothing. The second argument only sets ProjectSourceDir (L26-27), and nothing uses that variable. Tested: after './rename.sh CbmTrd CBMROOT Cbm' the code still includes MyProjDetectorList.h and MyProjStack.h, so it does not compile in a project whose stack is CbmStack. NewDetector_stl_containers/rename.sh is identical.
issues.fix: Replace MyProj with ${Prefix} in the .h and .cxx files (instead of FairDetectorList and FairStack), and either use the project-name argument or remove it.

excerpt.code:
find . -name "*.cxx" -exec sed -e "s/NewDetector/$DetectorName/g" $sedstring "{}" ";"
find . -name "*.cxx" -exec sed -e "s/NEWDETECTOR/$DetectorNameUpper/g" $sedstring "{}" ";"
find . -name "*.cxx" -exec sed -e "s/FairDetectorList/${Prefix}DetectorList/g" $sedstring "{}" ";"
find . -name "*.cxx" -exec sed -e "s/FairStack/${Prefix}Stack/g" $sedstring "{}" ";"
find . -name "*.h" -exec sed -e "s/FairDetectorList/${Prefix}DetectorList/g" $sedstring "{}" ";"
find . -name "*.h" -exec sed -e "s/FairStack/${Prefix}Stack/g" $sedstring "{}" ";"

sed -e "s#tutorial/NewDetector#$RelativeDir#g" $sedstring CMakeLists.txt

issues.title: NewDetector_stl_containers does not compile: NewDetectorPoint ctor has an extra evtId
issues.description: NewDetectorPoint.cxx defines the standard constructor with 8 arguments (an extra uint32_t evtId), but NewDetectorPoint.h:29-35 declares only 7. g++ stops with 'no declaration matches' (checked with a stub TVector3.h), and the 7-argument constructor that NewDetector.cxx:222 calls is never defined. No test builds this folder, because templates/CMakeLists.txt and test_project.sh.in build only the project_*_containers templates, whose copy is correct.
issues.fix: Remove evtId from the definition and set fEventId to 0 (or add evtId to the declaration and the AddHit() call), and let the template test also build the standalone NewDetector_* folders.

issues.title: NewTask log texts misspelled ('Defaul', 'Initilization'); ReInit() logs the Init() text
issues.description: The constructor logs 'Defaul Constructor of NewTask' (line 17) and Init() logs 'Initilization of NewTask' (line 40). ReInit() logs the same 'Initilization of NewTask' text (line 71), so the two steps look the same in the log. Projects copy these texts; the comments also say 'initilization' (line 61) and 'Initiliazation' (NewTask.h:27, 30).
issues.fix: Use 'Default constructor of NewTask', 'Initialization of NewTask' and 'Reinitialization of NewTask', and fix the comments.

issues.title: NewTask example Register() uses the same branch and folder name, which is fatal
issues.description: The commented-out example in Init() calls ioman->Register("OutputDataLevelName", "OutputDataLevelName", ...). FairRootManager::RegisterImpl() stops with LOG(fatal) when the object name equals the folder name (FairRootManager.cxx:158-161). A user who uncomments the example and fills in the placeholder gets a fatal error in Init().
issues.fix: Use two different placeholders, for example Register("OutputDataLevelName", "OutputFolderName", <OutputDataLevel>, kTRUE).

issues.title: NewTask.h: redundant by-value operator=, hooks without override, plain ClassDef
issues.description: The private copy constructor and operator= are redundant, because FairTask already deletes copy and move, and operator= returns NewTask by value. The hooks are public (protected in FairTask) and virtual without override, and the class uses ClassDef while FairTask uses ClassDefOverride. Projects copy this header, so the old style spreads.
issues.fix: Remove the two private declarations, mark the hooks override, and use ClassDefOverride(NewTask, 1).

issues.title: NewTask/rename.sh header comment describes the NewDetector script
issues.description: The header says that the script replaces NewDetector or NEWDETECTOR and suggests a detector name like CbmTrd. The script actually replaces NewTask and NEWTASK with a task name.
issues.fix: Rewrite the comment to describe the NewTask renaming.

issues.title: rename.sh of NewTask and NewParameterContainer fails with exit 1 on Linux
issues.description: The second case "$arch" block has only a darwin branch, so on Linux the * branch prints 'Platform not supported' and exits with status 1. This happens after the files are renamed and edited, so the user sees an error and the final instructions never print. templates/NewParameterContainer/rename.sh:45-53 has the same block, and running copies of both scripts on Linux shows the error.
issues.fix: Add an empty linux) branch to the second case block in both scripts.

excerpt.code:

case "$arch" in
    darwin)
      rm *.bak
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Platform not supported"
      exit 1
      ;;
esac

issues.title: Project templates never build MyProjGenerators: no target pythia8 ever exists
issues.description: CMakeLists.txt adds MyProjGenerators only if the targets pythia8 and Pythia6 exist (L142). FindPythia6.cmake creates the imported target Pythia6. But FairRoot's FindPythia8.cmake, which the template uses, creates no target; it only sets PYTHIA8_LIBRARY and Pythia8_FOUND. So CMake always skips the folder without a message, and the library MyGen is never built, even when Pythia8 is found. The STL template has the same file.
issues.fix: Test Pythia8_FOUND and Pythia6_FOUND instead. In MyProjGenerators/CMakeLists.txt, link FairRoot::Base and ${PYTHIA8_LIBRARIES} instead of the plain names Base and pythia8 (L32), and remove the missing ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/generators folder (L10).

excerpt.code:
add_subdirectory (MyProjData)
if(TARGET pythia8 AND TARGET Pythia6)
  add_subdirectory (MyProjGenerators)
endif()
add_subdirectory (NewDetector)
add_subdirectory (passive)

issues.title: MyConstField::Print() hides FairField::Print(Option_t*) const and never runs
issues.description: MyConstField declares virtual void Print() without an argument and without const, so it does not override FairField::Print(Option_t*) const, which is empty. createFairField() calls fMagneticField->Print("") through a FairField pointer (MyFieldCreator.cxx:60), so the field summary never prints. project_stl_containers/field has the same code.
issues.fix: Declare it as void Print(Option_t* option = "") const override and make the definition const.

issues.title: Field creator asks for MyFieldPar, but no factory creates it and nothing fills it
issues.description: MyFieldCreator::SetParm() calls getContainer("MyFieldPar"), but neither MyPassiveContFact nor NewDetectorContFact registers that container. So FairRuntimeDb logs 'Container MyFieldPar not created!', and createFairField() prints '-E- No field parameters available!' and gives FairRunAna no field. MyConstField also has no FillParContainer(), so FairRunSim only logs the FairField warning and never stores the field. project_stl_containers/field has the same code.
issues.fix: Register MyFieldPar in a container factory (as FairPassiveContFact does for FairConstPar) and implement MyConstField::FillParContainer() with MyFieldPar::SetParameters().

issues.title: MyFieldPar field-map branches (fType >= 2) can never run
issues.description: In putParams() and getParams(), the branch fType >= 1 && fType <= kMaxFieldMapType comes before fType >= 2 && fType <= kMaxFieldMapType. The first branch catches every value of the second, so the field-map name, position and scale are never written or read. project_stl_containers/field has the same code.
issues.fix: Order the conditions so that each field type reaches its own branch, or remove the unused branches.

issues.title: MyFieldPar.h comment names kTypeDistorted, which does not exist
issues.description: The fType comment lists 'kTypeDistorted = distorted field map', but no such constant exists in the templates or in FairRoot. project_stl_containers/field/MyFieldPar.h:71 has the same line.
issues.fix: Remove the kTypeDistorted line from both headers.

Int_t fType;

issues.title: Template Geane.C hard-codes PndStack, and rename.sh does not change it
issues.description: Config() creates 'new PndStack(10)' (L26). In gconfig, rename.sh edits only g3Config.C and g4Config.C (rename.sh:102-103), so this name never changes. FairGeane::Init() loads Geane.C from CONFIG_DIR or VMCWORKDIR/gconfig. So in a project with any prefix other than Pnd, the macro does not compile and Geane cannot start. The STL template has the same file.
issues.fix: Use MyProjStack in Geane.C and add the file to the s/MyProj/$Prefix/g passes of rename.sh.

issues.title: Template eventDisplay.C draws no tracks: FairMCTracksDraw rejects MyProjMCTrack
issues.description: FairEveMCTracks::Init() accepts the MCTrack branch only if its class inherits from FairMCTrack. The template stack fills MCTrack with MyProjMCTrack, which derives from TObject, so Init() logs 'does not contain FairMCTrack objects', returns kERROR, and FairTask::InitTask() switches the task off. The point drawing (line 23) is commented out, so the display shows no MC data; templates/project_stl_containers/macro/eventDisplay.C is identical.
issues.fix: Derive MyProjMCTrack from FairMCTrack, or give the template a draw task that understands MyProjMCTrack and NewDetectorPoint.

issues.title: run_sim.C comment says multiplicity 1, but FairBoxGenerator(13, 5) makes 5 muons
issues.description: The second argument of FairBoxGenerator(Int_t pdgid, Int_t mult) is the multiplicity, so the macro makes 5 muons per event. But the comment says '1 = multipl.' (L57). The comments also have the typos 'visualiztion' (L67) and 'ot a separate file' (L88). The STL template has the same macro.
issues.fix: Change the comment to '5 = multiplicity' and fix the two typos.

issues.title: Typo 'succesfully' in the final message of the template run_sim.C macros
issues.description: Both template macros print 'Macro finished succesfully.' (also templates/project_stl_containers/macro/run_sim.C:97). The FairRoot example tests use 'Macro finished successfully' as PASS_REGULAR_EXPRESSION, so a test that copies this pattern never passes with these macros.
issues.fix: Change the text to 'Macro finished successfully.' in both macros.

issues.title: MyProjMCTrack::GetNPoints() always returns 0 and SetNPoints() does nothing
issues.description: The bodies of GetNPoints() and SetNPoints() are commented out ('TODO: Where does this come from'), so GetNPoints() returns 0 for every detector. MyProjStack::FillTrackArray() counts the points of each track and calls SetNPoints(), but the counts are lost and fNPoints is always 0 in the output. MyProjMCTrack.h documents these functions as point-count accessors, and project_stl_containers has the same code.
issues.fix: Implement the bit packing of fNPoints for kNewDetector (as FairMCTrack does for its detectors) or remove the two functions.

issues.title: Typo 'dex map' in a fatal message of the template stack
issues.description: UpdateTrackIndex() stops with 'Particle index ... not found in dex map!'; the word should be 'index'. The commented-out copy in project_stl_containers/MyProjData/MyProjStack.cxx:300 has the same text, and the debug message on line 289 says 'indizes'.
issues.fix: Change the text to 'not found in index map!' and 'indices'.

issues.title: MyProjGenerators/rename.sh is a leftover detector script that renames nothing
issues.description: This script is a copy of the NewDetector rename.sh with NewDetector replaced by PndPythia. No file named PndPythia* exists (the folder has Pythia6Generator.* and Pythia8Generator.*). So ls fails, no sed pattern matches, and the script then prints hints about adding a detector. The project rename.sh keeps the script as <Prefix>Generators/rename.sh. The STL template has the same copy.
issues.fix: Delete both MyProjGenerators/rename.sh files.

issues.title: Detector templates re-add sensitive volumes in Initialize() and log false errors
issues.description: Initialize() calls DefineSensitiveVolumes() ('WORKAROUND needed for Geant4 in MT mode') before FairDetector::Initialize(). ConstructGeometry() has already added Det1, Det2 and Det3, so in a sequential run FairVolumeList::addVolume() logs an 'already defined' error for each of them. The workaround is obsolete, because FairDetector::Initialize() calls DefineSensitiveVolumes() itself in MT mode (FairDetector.cxx:93-97). The same call is in project_stl_containers/NewDetector/NewDetector.cxx:84, NewDetector_root_containers/NewDetector.cxx:85 and NewDetector_stl_containers/NewDetector.cxx:84.
issues.fix: Remove the call, the private NewDetector::DefineSensitiveVolumes() and the workaround comment from all four templates.

issues.title: Detector templates create the medium C in ConstructGeometry() but never use it
issues.description: ConstructGeometry() looks up the medium C and creates it if it does not exist (L175, L181-184). But no volume uses the variable Carbon; the passive volume Pass1 is silicon (L196). The same code is in project_stl_containers and in both NewDetector_* templates.
issues.fix: Remove the Carbon code, or build Pass1 from Carbon if it was meant to be a carbon absorber.

issues.title: GeoPar clear() leaves dangling pointers, and the empty destructor leaks the arrays
issues.description: clear() deletes fGeoSensNodes and fGeoPassNodes without setting them to nullptr, and FairDetParRootFileIo::read() calls clear() right before key->Read(). This works today only because NewDetectorLinkDef.h has no '+', so the old-style Streamer() just overwrites the pointers; with the '+' streamer, ROOT's TBufferFile::ReadFastArray() deletes the old pointer again (double free). The empty destructor never frees the arrays. All four NewDetector templates and the example GeoPar classes share this code, and examples/advanced/propagator already uses '+' for FairTutPropGeoPar.
issues.fix: Set both pointers to nullptr after the delete in clear(), and delete both arrays in the destructor.

issues.title: MyPassiveContFact registers FairGeoPassivePar, but createContainer() returns nullptr
issues.description: The constructor adds the container FairGeoPassivePar (L40-41). But createContainer() returns nullptr right away, and the real code is commented out (L50-56). FairGeoPassivePar exists only in the examples library (examples/common/passive), so the template cannot create it. If code asks for it, FairRuntimeDb::getContainer() logs 'Container FairGeoPassivePar not created!' and returns nullptr; the template itself never asks for it. The STL template has the same file.
issues.fix: Remove the registration and the dead code, or register only containers that the template defines.

issues.title: MyPipe builds its vacuum volume from the wall shape, so the two volumes overlap fully
issues.description: ConstructGeometry() builds the vacuum volume Vpipe from shape (L70). That is the carbon wall from r = 2.5 to 2.55 cm, not Vshape. Vshape is never used and has zero thickness (rmin == rmax, L66). Both volumes are named MyPipe and go into the top volume with copy number 1 (L72-73), so they overlap completely: the wall material depends on which node the navigator finds, and the inside of the pipe stays cave air instead of vacuum. run_sim.C adds this module to every template simulation, and the STL template has the same code.
issues.fix: Make Vshape the inside of the pipe (DefineSection(iSect, z[iSect], 0., r[iSect])), build Vpipe from Vshape, and give it its own name.

issues.title: Typos in rename.sh texts: 'to long', 'As an example the if', 'This iist'
issues.description: The help text of the project rename.sh says 'the class names. and some directories' (L9), 'shouldn't be to long' (L10) and 'As an example the if you want' (L12). The last hint of both NewDetector_*/rename.sh scripts says 'This iist can be found' (L67), and both MyProjGenerators/rename.sh copies repeat it. The project script also computes DetectorNameUpper (L27) but never uses it. The STL copy is identical.

issues.title: Project rename.sh breaks the project when the prefix or detector name starts with My
issues.description: After it replaces MyProj and NewDetector, the script runs s/My/$Prefix/ again on every CMakeLists.txt (L68) and on every file whose name starts with My (L88-93). So a prefix or detector name that starts with 'My' (in any case) is replaced twice. Tested: './rename.sh MyExperiment MyExp det' makes the folder MyexpData, but CMakeLists.txt adds MyexpexpData, five mv commands fail, and the exit code is still 0. Also, './rename.sh Panda Pnd MYDET' makes PndMydet.cxx, but mydet/CMakeLists.txt lists PndPnddet.cxx. The STL template has the same script.
issues.fix: Replace the generic My passes with the explicit class names (MyCave, MyPipe, MyConstField and so on) or reject such names, and exit with a non-zero code when a step fails.

excerpt.code:
sed -e "s/NewDetector/$DetectorNameLower/g" $sedstring CMakeLists.txt

for i in $(find . -type f -name CMakeLists.txt); do
  sed -e "s/MyProj/$Prefix/g" $sedstring $i
  sed -e "s/MYPROJ/$ProjectNameUpper/g" $sedstring $i
  sed -e "s#/NewDetector#/$DetectorNameLower#g" $sedstring $i
  sed -e "s/NewDetector/$Prefix$DetectorName/g" $sedstring $i
  sed -e "s/My/$Prefix/g" $sedstring $i
done

# Change file names
for i in $(find . -type f -name "MyProj*"); do
  oldfile=$i
  newfile=$(echo $oldfile | sed "s/MyProj/$Prefix/")
  mv $oldfile $newfile
  sed -e "s/MyProj/$Prefix/g" $sedstring $newfile
  sed -e "s/NewDetector/$Prefix$DetectorName/g" $sedstring $newfile
done

for i in $(find . -type f -name "NewDetector*"); do
  oldfile=$i
  newfile=$(echo $oldfile | sed "s/NewDetector/$Prefix$DetectorName/")
  mv $oldfile $newfile
  sed -e "s/NewDetector/$Prefix$DetectorName/g" $sedstring $newfile
  sed -e "s/MyProj/$Prefix/g" $sedstring $newfile

issues.title: STL project stack ignores StoreSecondaries, SetMinPoints, SetEnergyCut and StoreMothers
issues.description: In the STL variant, FillTrackArray() has the SelectTracks() call commented out and sets store = kTRUE (line 263), and the body of UpdateTrackIndex() is a comment (lines 290-341). So the public setters in MyProjStack.h:169-172 have no effect and every particle is written, while the ROOT variant applies them. The missing remapping is harmless only because no track is dropped; NewDetector::GetCollection() returns NULL, so the std::vector points could not be remapped.
issues.fix: Remove the selection setters and SelectTracks() from the STL template, or remap the track IDs of the vector points and call SelectTracks() again.

issues.title: STL MyProjStack.h describes track filtering that the STL stack never does
issues.description: The header says that the stack stores only tracks that pass the filter, and that the default minimum number of points is 1 (L19-29). In the STL template, the constructor sets fMinPoints(0) (MyProjStack.cxx:53), and FillTrackArray() does not call SelectTracks() (cxx:252), so it stores every particle. The body of UpdateTrackIndex() is also commented out, so StoreSecondaries(), SetMinPoints(), SetEnergyCut() and StoreMothers() have no effect. In both templates, the sentence that lists the filter criteria stops at 'or are the' (L25).
issues.fix: Say in the STL header that the stack stores all particles and ignores the cut setters, and finish or delete the cut-off sentence in both headers.

issues.title: STL NewDetector destructor leaks fVectorPoints when the vector is empty
issues.description: ~NewDetector() deletes fVectorPoints only inside if (fVectorPoints->size()). EndOfEvent() and Reset() empty the vector after each event, so it is normally empty at destruction and the vector object leaks. templates/NewDetector_stl_containers/NewDetector.cxx:68-77 has the same code.
issues.fix: Move delete fVectorPoints out of the if block.

issues.title: MyWriteoutBuffer::Modify() hides the base virtual, so the buffer never calls it
issues.description: Modify() takes std::pair<double, MyDataClass*>, but FairWriteoutBuffer::Modify() takes std::pair<double, FairTimeStamp*>. So it hides the base function instead of overriding it, and FairWriteoutBuffer::FillDataToDeadTimeMap() always calls the base version, which drops the new data (a stub with the same signatures confirms it). The template's charge summing never runs, and its body is also wrong: MyWriteoutBuffer.cxx:37 adds two absolute active times.
issues.fix: Declare Modify() with the std::pair<double, FairTimeStamp*> signature and override, cast to MyDataClass* inside, and keep the later active time instead of the sum.

issues.title: TimeBased/rename.sh leaves backup files with the suffix '' on macOS
issues.description: On darwin the script sets sedstring="-i ''" and expands it without quotes (lines 42-44 and 52-54). sed then gets -i and the literal two-character argument '', and BSD sed uses it as the backup suffix. Each new file gets a stray copy such as CbmTrdDigiWriteoutBuffer.cxx'' that the script never removes.
issues.fix: Keep the option in a bash array, for example sedargs=(-i ''), and expand it as "${sedargs[@]}".

issues.title: Check_Compiler() calls list(GET) on an empty list, so its own empty check never runs
issues.description: Check_Compiler() filters the INTERFACE_COMPILE_FEATURES of ROOT::Core for cxx_std_* and then runs list(GET ROOT_CXX_STANDARD 0 ...) without checking for an empty list. If ROOT::Core has no cxx_std_* feature, configure stops with 'list GET given empty list' (tested with a mock target, with and without the property). So the if() at line 26 and the fairsoft-config fallback never run in that case. ROOT 6.18 and newer always export cxx_std_<N> on ROOT::Core (ROOT_LINKER_LIBRARY), so the bug does not show with the supported ROOT versions.
issues.fix: Run list(GET) only when the filtered list is not empty, for example inside if(ROOT_CXX_STANDARD).

excerpt.code:
PROPERTY INTERFACE_COMPILE_FEATURES)
  message(VERBOSE "Using ROOT to detect CXX_STANDARD: [${ROOT_CXX_STANDARD}]")
  list(FILTER ROOT_CXX_STANDARD INCLUDE REGEX "^cxx_std_.*")
  list(TRANSFORM ROOT_CXX_STANDARD REPLACE "^cxx_std_" "")
  list(SORT ROOT_CXX_STANDARD ORDER DESCENDING)
  list(GET ROOT_CXX_STANDARD 0 ROOT_CXX_STANDARD)
  if(ROOT_CXX_STANDARD)
    set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD ${ROOT_CXX_STANDARD})
    message(VERBOSE "Taking CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=${CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD} from ROOT")
  endif()
endif()

issues.title: Intel C++ Debug flags contain '-0b0' (digit zero) instead of '-Ob0'
issues.description: For the Intel compiler, Check_Compiler() sets CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG to '-O2 -g -0b0 -noalign'. '-0b0' starts with the digit zero and is not a compiler option, while the C flags at line 103 use the inline-control option '-Ob0'. So Intel C++ Debug builds get an unknown option and keep the default inlining.
issues.fix: Change '-0b0' to '-Ob0'.

excerpt.code:
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELWITHDEBINFO "-O2 -g ")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE        "-O2")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG          "-O2 -g -0b0 -noalign")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUGFULL      "-g -Ob0 -noalign -W")

issues.title: macOS DebugFull C++ flags turn off exceptions, so FairRoot does not compile
issues.description: On macOS, Check_Compiler() sets CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUGFULL with -fno-exceptions and no later -fexceptions. The Linux flags at line 78 also contain -fno-exceptions, but they end with -fexceptions. FairRoot code throws exceptions (fairroot/tools/FairLogger.cxx:201, fairroot/geane/FairGeanePro.cxx:58), and clang++ rejects that with these flags ('cannot use throw with exceptions disabled'). So a macOS build with CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=DebugFull stops at the first such file (tested on Linux with clang++ and the exact flags, through CMake with -std=gnu++17).
issues.fix: Remove -fno-exceptions from line 157, or add -fexceptions at the end, as line 78 does.

excerpt.code:
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE        "-O2 -Wshadow ")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG          "-g -Wshadow  -fno-inline")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUGFULL      "-g3 -fno-inline -Wnon-virtual-dtor -Wno-long-long -ansi -Wundef -Wcast-align -Wchar-subscripts -Wall -W -Wpointer-arith -Wformat-security -fno-exceptions -fno-check-new -fno-common")
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_PROFILE        "-g3 -fno-inline -ftest-coverage -fprofile-arcs -Wall -Wextra")

issues.title: config.sh puts source and /lib folders into PYTHONPATH

issues.title: Linker flags become a list when LDFLAGS is set, so every Ninja link fails
issues.description: Lines 43-44 add -Wl,--enable-new-dtags with set(VAR ${VAR} "flag"), which makes a CMake list. When CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS or CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS is not empty (for example because LDFLAGS was set at the first configure), the value gets a ';' before the flag. With Ninja, the shell splits each link command at the ';' and every link fails with '/bin/sh: 1: -Wl,--enable-new-dtags: not found'. With Makefiles, the flag sticks to the last user flag (for example '-L/usr/lib;-Wl,--enable-new-dtags'), which breaks that flag (both tested with CMake 3.28).
issues.fix: Append the flag as a string on both lines, for example string(APPEND CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS " -Wl,--enable-new-dtags").

excerpt.code:
if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux")
  set(CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS ${CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS} "-Wl,--enable-new-dtags")
  set(CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS ${CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS} "-Wl,--enable-new-dtags")
  set(CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS  "${CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS} -z defs")
  set(CMAKE_MODULE_LINKER_FLAGS  "${CMAKE_MODULE_LINKER_FLAGS} -z defs")

issues.title: checkGeoSetNamingConventions() never tests module index 0
issues.description: Both sections use GENERATE(take(100, random(1, 1000))), and Catch2's random(1, 1000) draws from 1 to 1000 inclusive. So index 0 (the first module, prefix + '1') is never checked, and almost all draws lie above getMaxModules() (10 or 100 in the seven example tests that call this helper). The large indices are harmless, because getModuleName() rejects only m < 0, but the real module range is barely tested.
issues.fix: Draw the indices from 0 to modules - 1, for example with GENERATE_COPY(range(0, modules)).

issues.title: FairGeoSet test is disabled because it hangs; its sources stay in the tree
issues.description: FairTestGeo.cxx and tests_FairGeoSet.cxx are commented out of the GeoBase suite with the note 'Compilation works but when running the test doesn't finish'. These sources, FairTestGeo.h and the two data files configured on lines 33-34 serve only this disabled test, so the test of FairGeoSet::read() never runs.
issues.fix: Fix the hang and re-enable the two sources, or remove them and the data files until the test works.

# Compilation works but when running the test doesn't finish
# Disable for the time being 
#  FairTestGeo.cxx
#  tests_FairGeoSet.cxx

  DEPENDENCIES

issues.title: tests_FairGeoSet.cxx is disabled because testmedia.geo lacks npckov for 'air'
issues.description: The air entry in tests/geobase/data/testmedia.geo (lines 2-3) has no npckov line, so FairGeoMedia::read() never returns and the test hangs. CMakeLists.txt therefore comments out FairTestGeo.cxx and tests_FairGeoSet.cxx ('the test doesn't finish'), and the FairGeoSet test does not run.
issues.fix: Add the missing '0' npckov line to the air entry and re-enable both test sources.

issues.title: test_tgeo_units passes when the lengths are too large (no absolute value)
issues.description: The check (correct - value) < 0.001 has no absolute value, so any radiation or interaction length above the expected value passes. The comment on lines 30-31 says the test fails when the values are not equal. It still catches the known Geant4-unit error (values 10 times smaller), but not a deviation upward.
issues.fix: Compare TMath::Abs(correct - value) < 0.001 for both lengths.

issues.title: Typo 'differnt' in the failure message of test_tgeo_units.C
issues.description: The failure output says 'Radiation or interaction length differnt from expectation'. The TGeoManager title on line 21 says 'lengtyh', and the comments have 'differnt' (line 3), 'tye' (line 7), 'lenght' (line 8) and 'propertoes' (line 24).
issues.fix: Correct the spelling to 'different', 'length', 'the' and 'properties'.
